#19887. Dressing Like Your Boyfriend Is Actually Fine

Dressing Like Your Boyfriend Is Actually Fine

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (797 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cosmopolitan

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that is it so wrong to dress like your boyfriend?
  • I personally think it’s a silly argument given that Bella Hadid is one of the most notable supermodels with an eccentric, well-documented high-fashion sense of style.
  • The same argument has been made about Ariana Grande, Kim Kardashian, and, more recently (even by her own sisters, who do the same thing), Kourtney Kardashian.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that is it so wrong to dress like your boyfriend? Clearly, the internet thinks so. Most recently, Bella Hadid has found herself at the center of this conversation, with people highlighting her various boyfriend eras like some sort of sartorial identity crisis. From the emo-adjacent vibes when she dated the singer, The Weeknd, to the cowboy-rodeo-chic aesthetic with Adan Banuelos, and now her hockey-game-attending, matching outfit moment with new man Nathan Lacy, Bella has seemingly been accused of basing her clothes after her romantic partners.

I personally think it’s a silly argument given that Bella Hadid is one of the most notable supermodels with an eccentric, well-documented high-fashion sense of style. She was awarded Lyst’s 2022 Most Powerful Dresser, and she famously styles much of her own day-to-day looks. So who cares if, during a particular season of her life, she wants to tap into the aesthetic of the man she’s dating?

The same argument has been made about Ariana Grande, Kim Kardashian, and, more recently (even by her own sisters, who do the same thing), Kourtney Kardashian. Ariana’s personal style has never particularly screamed fashion girl to me, and I’m a huge proponent of the idea that not everyone needs to be one anyway. Grande works with stylists to build her looks, so if on her off days she wants to dress in tandem with her beau, there’s truly nothing wrong with that.

Industry observers note that kim Kardashian, meanwhile, notoriously skyrocketed into the high-fashion space during her relationship with Kanye West. To this day, Kim gives style credits to Kanye’s eye for fashion and his introducing her to the world she so desperately wanted to be part of. Did she take what he taught her and expand upon it, eventually establishing herself as a fashion mogul in her own right? Yes. So technically in the long term, borrowing an aesthetic from her boyfriend then husband clearly worked out for her.

And while I personally wouldn’t wear Kourtney’s ultra-rock-girlfriend aesthetic, I actually think it's fun. After spending a decade being terrorized by Scott Disick (terrible boyfriend, excellent family friend to her sisters), I think it’s perfectly fine for my girl to enjoy someone so much she clearly feels safe enough to wrap herself in his sartorial aesthetic.

It has been revealed that this idea that women are in the wrong for “adopting” their man’s fashion seems uninteresting to me. If anything, women should be stealing men’s aesthetics and making them their own more often. There's something cheeky about the whole thing, a small flip of patriarchy on its head. How often do we see the internet go viral over the invisible labor women put into the men they date? Making their style better, recommending the haircut that best frames their face, teaching them how to groom themselves. It’s always give, give, give. So why not take something too? Because the next video down my timeline after those labor of love, “girlfriend effect” ones is women complaining about men taking everything they gave in a relationship (from hair and clothing reccs) and bringing it to the next woman.

Industry observers note that there's something rather liberating about having your own style to return to while allowing yourself to experiment with whatever your boyfriend of the moment is into. It’s like playing dress-up. You’re enjoying a man, his world, and even his wardrobe, without having to make any of it your permanent identity—simply trying it out like free samples of ice cream. And when he’s no longer serving you, you move on. Thank you, next, as Miss Grande states.

Because women are so often expected to do the emotional and personal-care work in relationships, it’s honestly fine to me seeing these celebrities lean into their boyfriends’ fashion sense. (Side note: Incredible that these men have a style at all—it can be sartorially bleak out there!) Maybe his hockey jerseys look good on you. Maybe his leather jackets are better than yours. Maybe you just like the way you look in a cowboy hat right now.

It isn’t hurting anyone. And if anything, the most radical part of all is letting the men, for once, shape the fashion in their relationship. High time we all start letting them handle the burden of lessening the swag gap.

According to recent reports, aiyana Ishmael is the style editor at Cosmopolitan magazine. In her work, Aiyana focuses on the culture of fashion and how it intertwines and shapes the zeitgeist. She is an award-winning journalist from Miami, Florida, and a graduate of the historically Black university, Florida A&M. She is a 2024 Forbes 30 Under 30: Media honoree, and her debut romance novella PASSING GAME is set to release March of 2027 (831 Stories/Simon & Schuster).

Montana politics never cease to amaze me. The state voted for Bill Clinton twice but has gone red ever since. It had a long and proud tradition of campaign-finance legislation until Citizens United turned the table. Like all timber and mining states, Montana has a long—and fairly unique—history of labor activity. Butte became known as the “Gibraltar of Unionism.” In 1914, two factions of the powerful Western Federation of Miners went to war with each other. (The dissidents blew up the union hall in Butte.) The recent election shifted things around within that state tradition.

Similar relief spread all over the Mountain West.

And it seems possible that there’s more to come.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • According to recent reports, being the giving Sagittarius she is, Hailey Bieber actually gives us something every year for her birthday: a new Rhode collection.
  • Today, Rhode announced Pocket Plush, the brand’s new matte blush in two shades: Baldwin, a berry rose that’s allegedly Hailey’s go-to shade, and Tucson, a rich burgundy.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, we may earn commission from links on this page, but we only recommend products we love. Promise.

According to recent reports, being the giving Sagittarius she is, Hailey Bieber actually gives us something every year for her birthday: a new Rhode collection. Sometimes it’s a special-edition shade or flavor of her award-winning Peptide Lip Tint. Other years, it’s a brand-new product, like the Peptide Eye Prep Hydrogel Patches and a new snap-on lip case. But the 1996-er went all out for her 30th birthday, dropping new products, exclusive styles and colors on some of the brand’s go-to items, and even its first-ever apparel.

Today, Rhode announced Pocket Plush, the brand’s new matte blush in two shades: Baldwin, a berry rose that’s allegedly Hailey’s go-to shade, and Tucson, a rich burgundy. For now, it comes in a limited-edition mini navy packaging that’s v cute (and has been teased for a while on Rhode’s IG). What makes it different from Pocket Blush? Well, the creamy stick is stated to leave a velvety, soft matte finish on skin. Think blurring and smoothing, not dewy and fresh like the OG. You can also wear them on cheeks and lips, which Hailey loves to pair together for a monochromatic look.

Sources indicate that but that’s not even the most exciting newly introduced launch, IMO. For the first time ever, Rhode is launching apparel. It’s only on pre-order right now, but the HB Windbreaker was inspired by Hailey’s love of vintage sportswear. It’s an easy “throw on and go,” oversized jacket that can be worn two ways. There’s navy nylon on one side and gray fleece on the other. If you wanted to match your Rhode phone case, lip balm, and Glazing Milk, now’s your chance. I’m pretty confident this one will sell out, especially ahead of gifting season.

According to recent reports, oh! And that’s not all! (Told ya, Hailey went all out this year.) There’s a limited-edition flavor of the Peptide Lip Boost, a rich, moisturizing lip mask that Cosmo editors have loved since it launched. This one has a shimmery sheer pink tint and a cherry vanilla cola scent. Sounds delicious.

Plus, there are exclusive styles of the Peptide Eye Prep, both in navy to match the collection. You can also grab the Rhode Carry Case and Snap-On Lip Case, both now available in navy just for Hailey’s bday.

Of course, if you wanted to pick up a set to gift (ahem, as a fellow Sag, I can confirm anyone wIth a bday coming up soon would love it), grab The Birthday Set: it contains both shades of Pocket Plush and the Peptide Lip Boost in Cherry Vanilla Cola.

Everything introduces (including the windbreaker preorder) on Friday, November 20, at 9 a.m. PT. As all Rhode things go, these will absolutely sell out swiftly. If you have your eye on something, I wouldn’t wait.

  • Visit the show house and see each of the 22 designers’ rooms, from the first dedicated home gym in Kips Bay history by Dallas-based Platinum Gym Design, to a small but mighty European-inspired kitchen by Stephenson Home, to a 1970s-inspired primary bathroom fit with a glass brick shower and curtained-off water closet by Nuance Interiors.
  • As always, proceeds from the show house go to the Kips Bay Boys & Girls Club, which provides educational, enrichment, and developmental programs to thousands of young people, as well as Dallas-based nonprofits Dwell with Dignity and The Crystal Charity Ball.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, the seventh annual Kips Bay Decorator Show House in Dallas returns to 2999 Turtle Creek Boulevard, but don’t expect it to look anything like it did in 2025. A new group of the country’s leading designers has taken on the 25,000-square-foot French Renaissance estate, transforming each room to showcase bold ideas, highlight exceptional craftsmanship, and reveal the upcoming trends we can expect to see in the world of interior design.

Visit the show house and see each of the 22 designers’ rooms, from the first dedicated home gym in Kips Bay history by Dallas-based Platinum Gym Design, to a small but mighty European-inspired kitchen by Stephenson Home, to a 1970s-inspired primary bathroom fit with a glass brick shower and curtained-off water closet by Nuance Interiors. With sponsors like Benjamin Moore, The Shade Store, The Rug Company, and more, the vibrant and personality-filled spaces come as no surprise.

As always, proceeds from the show house go to the Kips Bay Boys & Girls Club, which provides educational, enrichment, and developmental programs to thousands of young people, as well as Dallas-based nonprofits Dwell with Dignity and The Crystal Charity Ball.

To see this celebration of exceptional design, you can purchase tickets here and visit the house from Saturday, November 14th to Sunday, December 6th. However, if you can’t make it to the Lone Star State in time, check out some of our favorite moments from the event below.

In a recent development, kelsi Lamberth of Nuance Interiors pulled inspiration from the 1970s for her primary bathroom, separating the shower from the main prep space using a curved glass brick wall. The sculptural aspects can be found throughout in this groovy space.

Sources indicate that in the primary bedroom, Troy Rivington of Rivington Marx Interiors cocooned the room in a dark floral wallpaper and accessorized with other moody botanicals throughout. He was inspired by the romance of 1940s Cairo, dressing the room up like it belonged to a well-traveled collector.

As the first ever dedicated home gym at the Kips Bay Show House, Peter Hoffman of Platinum Gym Design chose a refined, luxurious setup. He named the room Tanren after the Japanese art of hammering and refining metal, and used walnut in both the equipment and the ceiling slats, stainless steel frames, and brown leather accents to complete the exercise space.

In a recent development, in this bespoke bathroom, Russ Peters and Bill Cates of Peters Cates Design lined the wall behind the Studio McGee x Kohler bathtub with a rich merlot tile by RIAD Tile. It’s a beautiful statement and a fabulous way to bring more texture and dimension to the room.

In a recent development, in this tucked away library space, filled with collected finds, designers Christina Garcia Lysaught and Grayson Knight of Layered Dimensions finished off this dark space with a stunning statement mirror. Around the perimeter are resin busts of wildlife, like owls and deer, bringing in a bejeweled touch to the room.

According to recent reports, the small but mighty kitchen, designed by Katie Stephenson of Stephenson Home, is crowned with a crackled-gold blooming wallpaper, bringing a warm balance to the rest of the room. It’s covered in birds, butterflies, and blossoms, and it wraps the cook space in a golden glow, reminding all who enter that this room should be as beautiful as it is functional.

According to recent reports, the citron paint color wrapping the walls in Jen Bienvenu’s entrance hall is undoubtedly enchanting and serves as the perfect backdrop for her “After the Hunt” theme, but it’s the lampshades made from old silk saris that tie everything together for us. They provide such a magical warmth and really capture the essence of a collector’s treasure room.

Related Story: Almost Every Piece in This Layered Arkansas Home Was a Lucky Antique Find.

Step through the citron entry and enter the round room, designed in collaboration by Helen Bergin Interiors and Lichten Architects. The walls are softened by long curtains from The Shade Store, which create beautiful juxtaposition with the curved, sculptural silver media console by Asher Gillman. The actual turntable is flush to the surface, giving it a seamless look while it emits wonderful sound.

In the Withdrawing Room by Jen Stevens of Fonde Interiors, plaster botanicals by artist Amanda Norman come to life as they crawl from the mantel along the chimney breast, escaping to the ceiling. The vines were handmade by Norman and capture the essence of a garden left undisturbed, showing that this formal-at-first-glance room has a wilder side.

It has been revealed that the rosy palette in designer Jen Dean’s—founder of Jede Interiors—grand bathroom is topped off with a hand-painted floral mural that covers the ceiling. The rose-gold shine reflects the natural light in the room and give it more depth, while the natural motifs spread across the rest of the space.

Inside this observatory bedroom by sisters Amy Mobley and Katie Norrid of City Hill Design, the Verellen bed is raised up from the ground on a custom platform, emphasizing the importance of the furniture’s role in this space meant for relaxation and rest. It’s wrapped in a striped silk carpet that beckons your touch with a chartreuse mohair sofa at the foot.

Related Story: A Trip to the Lone Star State Inspired the Earthy Textures of This Tennessee New Build.

In a recent development, colorful and collected, this vibrant library by designer Betsy Wentz is not visually quiet. The maximalist space is covered in pattern-mixed Schumacher from ceiling to floor, and the designer pumped up the volume by opting for this triangular table in this tucked away corner.

In designer Amy Switzer’s textural bar lounge—filled with plush chairs, unique artwork, large tassel accessories, and beaded cigarettes—it’s the stone details that really make the room sing. Onyx cornices crown the windows, blue agate inlays decorate the floor, and a banquette which curves around a custom stone and wood table bring a natural coolness to the room that only stone can bring.

Latest Update: MobLand Episode 9 Sets Up a Seriously Violent Finale

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1554 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Esquire

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • I know you’ve got a lot to think about right now, like the rising cost of a flat white, celebrity sex criminals, and which brand of pasta to stockpile, but put that on ice for a minute and consider Tom Hardy’s smile.
  • I could count on one hand the number of times I’ve seen him crack a grin on screen.
  • According to recent reports, take episode 9 of MobLand, when Harry gloriously threatens Frankie.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Consider Tom Hardy’s smile. I know you’ve got a lot to think about right now, like the rising cost of a flat white, celebrity sex criminals, and which brand of pasta to stockpile, but put that on ice for a minute and consider Tom Hardy’s smile.

I could count on one hand the number of times I’ve seen him crack a grin on screen. He’s like those actors who’ll go nude only if it’s tasteful and in the name of art. Hardy’s smiles are anything but tasteful. When they happen, it’s as surprising as any jump scare.

According to recent reports, take episode 9 of MobLand, when Harry gloriously threatens Frankie. “That fucking face of yours, I’ll ‘ave that,” he growls like Burglar Bill’s psychopath cousin. “I’ll wear it to carnival as a mask when I cut it off with this pint glass.”.

It has been revealed that the eyebrows arch and the lips creak upward and the face cracks like a dam with a hairline fracture, exploding into a horrifying clown grin. Then… suddenly it’s gone, like a split atom, back into the cosmic darkness from whence it came. They say the best actors can tell a story with their eyes. Hardy can tell one with just his teeth, and it’s brilliant and it’s terrifying.

Anyway, that was my highlight of episode 9.

According to recent reports, what else? Well, the cold open, where Frankie gatecrashes Kat’s ambassadors’ convention disguised as a waiter to threaten her. Kat is ready: “Under the 1961 Vienna Convention, unlawful entry into a sovereign embassy is not seen as trespass but as an attack on the nation. I call Black Flag and you do not make it off this fucking rug.”.

Recent findings suggest that talking of smiles, Gina wipes one clean off Maeve’s face with an exit straight out of RuPaul’s Drag Race. You’ll recall Maeve’s dastardly scheme: persuade Gina to fake a suicide attempt, thus breaking Harry’s spirit and forcing him out. Instead, Gina sashays away, leaving a message in lipstick on the mirror: “Suck my balls, witch.”.

Industry observers note that meow. I don’t think Ru could have put it better herself.

Maeve turns back to Eddie. “You want to be a Harrigan, there’s one last task: Harry.”.

It’s not long before the smile returns to Maeve’s face, when she wakes to find Conrad in his pants, strapping on a bulletproof vest. “What are you doing, man? It’s not Friday. Friday night is bondage night!”.

Actually, Conrad has pried a tasty piece of intel from JoJo, the Frankie henchman he tortured to death: a large shipment of drugs is landing at Tilbury Docks, ripe for the nicking. Off they drive with a boot full of weapons, soundtracked not by a true-crime podcast but by the bloodcurdling recording of JoJo’s torture.

Trouble is, just as they arrive, the ghouls of Conrad’s past start stalking the corridors of his mind again, whispering. “Leave me alone,” he cries, swerving the car. Maeve reveals an almost uncharacteristic amount of empathy. “It’s okay,” she soothes.

Industry observers note that still, the heist is off. Conrad is in no fit state to add to the ranks of the ghosts he’s made. They drive home.

If there were an award for the weirdest scene of the series, it would go to Eddie asking Paul on a date. “Wondered if you fancied popping out for a pint later.” He might as well have asked him to go dogging in a Chipping Norton lay-by.

In a recent development, really, he wants a bomb to kill Harry. Paul laughs it off with a monologue on the history of bombmaking, until Eddie plays his ace: “What if I tell you I know it was you who told Harry that I was in Ireland? I wonder what Maeve would think.” Paul’s smile dissolves. Maeve would have his guts for sausages. Or, in Eddie’s words: “How does it feel to have your bollocks in my briefcase?”.

And so to the meat and potatoes of the episode: Harry and Frankie’s tête-à-tête.

It starts at Harry’s home. Jan has returned to him, having realized she’s safer in his giant hands than in anyone else’s. He wants to whisk her to a safehouse, urgently. So she does what anyone would do when their life is in imminent danger: run a bath, throw on some Damien Rice and soak her troubles away.

Trouble is, those troubles are literally downstairs with assault rifles, with Frankie close behind. Naturally, Harry keeps an even bigger gun under the sofa, so he festoons the walls of his home with their brains before leading Jan out to the car. Gina has just arrived. So, alas, has Frankie.

Still in his dressing gown, Frankie kidnaps Gina and spirits her off to the panic room/prison cell beneath his London home.

Recent findings suggest that there, Gina and Frankie bond over a spot of smoothie play, hurling their drinks in each other’s faces, followed by a round of Nerf. It’s sweet. He likes her. Maybe he even gets her. She is, as he later tells Harry, “spunky, full of spunk.” That may just be what keeps her alive.

Recent findings suggest that over at Kevin HQ (a shipping container on an industrial estate), Harry, Jan and Kevin await news of Gina. Kevin pitches a new proposal: go John Wick on the lot of them.

“You call Frankie and tell him we accept on the condition he returns Gina safely… then we meet Conrad and Maeve and blow their fucking brains out.” Then Eddie, then Frankie, then, through Bella’s nous, defenestrate Kat McAllister via legal channels.

Conrad, whose marbles have been rolling under the sofa all episode, is not expected to put up much of a fight.

According to recent reports, “I’m taking over tonight,” fumes Kevin. “You’re either with me or against me.”.

Well, no need for that just yet. Harry has a plan to save Gina. Leverage? Another child he can senselessly murder? No, no. Simply the good old-fashioned threat of violence.

Industry observers note that at the parley, they’re yin and yang: Frankie the exuberant chatterbox, Harry the man who’ll never use two words when one will do. Frankie squeezes Harry’s arm: “Cor, feel those muscles. I mean, I’m tasty, but if we got in an actual ruck, I wouldn’t stand a snowflake. I bet you could kill me with your bare hands…”.

Which is roughly what Harry has in mind.

“You’re not gonna kill her,” he growls wearily.

“You mind testing that?” And Frankie orders a goon to blow Gina’s head off with a shotgun and film it so they can watch.

He hands Harry the phone for the tersest of chats with his gaffer-taped daughter: “Try to stay calm. I’m gonna get you out of this as soon as I can.” Click. Frankie can’t believe it. “Is that it? Unless you’ve got some brilliant plans, that is actually a bit shit. What are you up to, Harry?”.

Harry’s reply is considered and simple: “If I was you, I would’ve had some really significant, scary fucking geezers in here with you to keep you safe, to prevent the exact scenario that is unfolding right here.”.

“B-b-b-but I’ve just got to pick up the phone,” stammers Frankie.

“Go on then. I fucking dare you.”.

The tension is suddenly tighter than a celebrity sex criminal’s grip on the prison soap.

Harry’s purring now: “It took me seven seconds to walk through those doors from the car… No more cutting around in the old burgundy tracksuit, that’s for sure. Not without wearing a fucking colostomy bag hanging off your limp arse.”.

Then the scary smile, the face-mask line and the clincher: “Speaking of seven seconds, that’s all you’ve got left to call your mate Joey and let Gina go. Three... two...”.

It has been revealed that but Frankie has one more trick up his tracksuit: he gets Kat McAllister on the phone. Remember the black flag stuff at the top of the episode?

She’s offering Harry another chance: “As of tonight there is no Harrigans. But the good news: you have a new job. Thank you for what you’re about to do for us. I am looking forward to you working for the team. Black Flag, motherfucker.”.

In a recent development, in other words, Black Flag has been called, and the Harrigans are its target. It’s a fitting phrase. Pirates flew a black flag to tell ships to surrender or else. In motor racing, it means you’re disqualified. And it’s a snarling late-seventies hardcore punk band, whose “Nervous Breakdown” gives this episode its title. Kat’s version is all three at once.

Cut to the Cotswolds, where police are dredging the lake. They’ve pulled out a body. Is it Richie’s? It’s someone’s, and I’d wager they didn’t die smiling. Hardy, on the other hand, lives to smile another day.

Industry observers note that the chips are down, the traps are laid, and there’s one episode left. Does Frankie have one last blueprint up his tracksuit? Will Conrad pull his brain back from the brink? Will Maeve get the last laugh? Or will it be Harry, God help us all?

As Shakespeare puts it in Macbeth: “There’s daggers in men’s smiles: the near in blood, the nearer bloody.”.

When Will the Next James Bond Movie Be Out? What to Know Following the Robert Pattinson Announcement

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (515 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cosmopolitan

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Robert Pattinson has officially been unveiled as the newly introduced 007, and now we’re left wondering: Just when will we see him on our screens as the famous secret agent in movie history?
  • The 40-year-old actor was confirmed earlier this afternoon to be playing the role of James Bond by Amazon MGM Studios.
  • Rob takes on the role following Daniel Craig’s departure as the spy in the most recent Bond movie No Time to Die in 2021.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Robert Pattinson has officially been unveiled as the newly introduced 007, and now we’re left wondering: Just when will we see him on our screens as the famous secret agent in movie history?

The 40-year-old actor was confirmed earlier this afternoon to be playing the role of James Bond by Amazon MGM Studios. He said of taking on the famous spy role, “James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honor of a lifetime. I’m deeply grateful to Denis, Amy, David, Tanya, and everyone at Amazon MGM Studios for their belief in me. To say this role is a dream come true is an understatement. I couldn’t be more excited about this partnership and the work ahead with this fantastic team.”.

Rob takes on the role following Daniel Craig’s departure as the spy in the most recent Bond movie No Time to Die in 2021.

Industry observers note that given it’s already been five years since we last had a James Bond movie, just how long will we have to wait for the next one? As of now, we don’t have an official release date for the new James Bond movie. However, given it’s November 2026 and Rob’s role has only just been revealed, it seems unlikely we can expect the movie to be released next year.

In a recent development, according to an April 2026 report from The Sun, it’s unlikely that a new movie would be coming out until at least 2028, due to director Denis Villeneuve wanting to take a break after the Dune franchise comes to an end. Dune: Part Three, which also stars Rob, comes out on December 18, 2026.

A source told the publication, “Bond won’t be back until 2028. The production mindset’s gone from ‘Let’s hurry this through’ to ‘Make sure we get this right.’ Denis wanted a long break after Dune 3 and has some broad ideas on the script. Steven will get on with drafts, before they map out the final version. That’ll take at least the whole summer.”.

They added, “Realistically, if they can make January 2027 work for pre-production, then that will be a success.”.

As for when we can expect the movie to come out in 2028, Digital Spy reports there are two dates booked out in Amazon’s release calendar—April 21 and August 4—for an “Untitled Amazon MGM Event Film.”.

According to recent reports, in 2022, Amazon acquired MGM Studios, and in 2025, they reached an agreement for a fresh joint venture with Barbara Broccoli and Michael G. Wilson, who controlled the creative rights to Bond. This new venture meant that “Amazon MGM Studios will gain creative control of the James Bond franchise following closing of the transaction.”.

Industry observers note that and since February 2025, the hunt has been on for the next leading actor to take on the role of James Bond. Also reportedly said to be in the running for the role of Bond were Callum Turner, Jack Lowden, and Josh O’Connor, among (many) others.

#19853. The 10 Leather Jackets You (Yes, You) Could Actually Pull Off

📅 13 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1449 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Esquire ↗ Open Full Page

The 10 Leather Jackets You (Yes, You) Could Actually Pull Off

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1449 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Esquire

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, I bought my first leather jacket at a vintage fair in an old English cathedral.
  • Despite what cinema tells you, you don’t need to ride a motorcycle in order to wear a leather jacket.
  • Leather jackets can be tricky to get right.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, I bought my first leather jacket at a vintage fair in an old English cathedral. I was 19, and a middle-aged British lady told me I looked good in it. Clearly a sales technique, but it worked, and I shelled out my grocery money for it. I had grand aims of fixing up my dad’s old Honda the following semester and riding around campus in a sick jacket. For various reasons, that didn’t end up happening, and I ended up on a 50cc Yamaha Zuma, a fun little scooter but one where a creaky moto jacket looked more like a comic prop than something out of a Dennis Hopper film. C’est la vie; we all look a little ridiculous in our 20s.

Despite what cinema tells you, you don’t need to ride a motorcycle in order to wear a leather jacket. Or fly a WWII-era fighter plane. Or be Steve McQueen photographed for Esquire. Leather jackets are imbued with the undeniable cool factor of their original functionality—like work jackets, chore coats, and waxed canvas, the modern menswear landscape supports multiple usages. From happy hours to midwestern winters to, yes, actually riding a motorcycle, we’ve rounded up nine Esquire-approved picks to guide your foray into the iconic outerwear. And to come full circle, I did actually test some of these on a motorcycle. More than a decade later, I finally got my license and am fixing up that old Honda; thank God for YouTube.

Leather jackets can be tricky to get right. Too trend focused and it’s a thousand-dollar flash in the pan; too trend agnostic and you get a museum artifact rather than a wearable piece. Ayr nailed the balance on its cleverly named Scrambler jacket, which draws on moto history and sits in the Goldilocks zone between classic and contemporary.

According to recent reports, I’ve worn it motorcycling through the Appalachian mountain roads and strategy on packing it for an upcoming jaunt to Europe. If you’re looking for a more classic moto style, I also own and highly endorse the elegantly named Baby Grand. The brand (and menswear lead Brice Pattison) has the Midas touch of outerwear; every style is worth its weight in gold.

Sure, there are excellent (and expensive) picks from Loewe, Celine, and Tom Ford with extra-premium materials, brand-specific takes on classic silhouettes, and the extra designer oomph that makes them worth it in some circles. But in this price range, I’m more interested in the experimental and new perspective of a brand like Stòffa, which you can tell is having fun with fabric and silhouettes. This Wave Leather jacket somehow manages to be sleek and drape-y all at once. A daydream of a jacket that’s definitely pricey but somehow still more affordable by half than other designer pieces out there.

Sources indicate that budget leather goods can be problematic. Under a certain price threshold, you’re almost certainly not getting the real thing, in which case you’d be better off going with a disclosed imitation-leather piece from the likes of all-star mall brands like Banana Republic and Abercrombie & Fitch. Or eBay, where a tape measure and a search for Wilson’s Leather or vintage Orvis will unlock a treasure trove of perfectly patinated jackets.

In a recent development, for brand-newly introduced on a budget, I recommend the Jacket Maker. Its cut will be a little less forgiving than those of the pricier brands in this list, but if you’re a guy who fits well into off-the-rack suits, you shouldn’t have an issue. Plus, the brand offers a custom, made-to-measure jacket-design tool that has me tempted to re-create McQueen’s from The Great Escape.

It has been revealed that this is the one on this list that takes the most bravado. This is the one that upon first wear will get you some looks for your usual drinking buddies. And with good reason—a Schott Perfecto is a loaded garment. Marlon Brando, James Dean, the Ramones, and any cool guy that’s worn one before are not easy acts to follow. But if this is what the heart wants, we stand behind you fully.

The key is in how you wear it. Crucially, you should not “style” it. You should pick it up as much as possible and wear it with as many disparate collections of clothes as you can. For the first few weeks, you might be seen as “The guy trying to wear a leather jacket.” But after a month or two, that will turn into “The leather jacket guy.” Wear it hard, wear it proud, and wear it everywhere.

And one note on the type of leather. If you’re buying upcoming, we think you should go for horsehide. It’s the toughest of the bunch and takes the longest to mold to your body, but that makes it fun.

A shearling jacket is hard to pull off in day-to-day life. Done incorrectly, it can rapidly devolve into a kind of cosplay of a WWII fighter pilot. Overland’s Lance jacket retains the genuine sheepskin lining but softens the look with a handsome dark navy colorway paired with a more subtle brown lining, giving you the warmth and badassery without crossing over into costume territory—unless that’s your thing, in which case the brand’s B-3 bomber re-creation is right up your alley. (Though, as always, Todd Snyder’s take is more wearable.).

According to recent reports, I want every leather jacket to have an origin story like Taylor Stitch’s, which begins with one of the brand’s designers re-creating a beloved café-racer-style jacket his dad bought in the ’70s and wore to perfection. It turns out the original manufacturer, Golden Bear, was around the corner from TS, and the two brands worked together to reissue the style.

It has been revealed that it’s got some modern twists like a Thinsulate lining but retains the design cues that make it functional on a bike and just plain cool on its own. I’ve coveted this jacket for years and recently got my hands on it IRL, and, boy, it does not disappoint. The Whiskey Steerhide colorway looks a little early-aughts coded online, but in person it looks like the magic liquid itself: golden and invigorating. For a non-insulated, more lifestyle-oriented take on the silhouette, I’d point you to Billy Reid’s Blake jacket, which is my dive bar go-to.

In a recent development, rough out has the wearability of suede, and doesn’t look as turbo as smooth leather. But unlike typical suede, which splits the original hide, rough out retains the whole of the hide. That makes it just as durable and water-resistant as any other leather.

Add that to Billy Reid’s Blake rider shape, and you get a jacket that any guy—literally any guy, we swear—off the street could toss on and feel good in.

Look, the whole oversized vibe is cool and all—but we’re also keenly aware it doesn’t work for everyone. Sure, it brings that chill, relaxed vibe. But sometimes you can just end up looking like a kid wearing their dad’s clothes. If you’re looking for something that hugs the body a bit more, opt for Mili Lotan’s Hammond jacket. It’s got enough slouch you could wear a few layers beneath, but will flatter the body a little more than some of the other options on this list.

Recent findings suggest that I am big on brands that care about details and let the clothes speak for themselves. Octobre Éditions is one such brand. The cut and the cloth set the clothes apart and create longevity outside the trend cycle. When you’ve designed a perfect OCBD, you can never really go out of style. Same too with the brand’s excellent Larren jacket, which I have and is unfortunately at the moment OOS. Thankfully, the Peylor cuts the same silhouette in a nubby split leather that I’m a little envious of. Get it while the getting’s good.

This is a dream leather jacket—the sort of thing you’d have on a list of “Things I’d Buy If I Had All The Money In The World.” It’s rugged, it’s suave, and damn is it comfy. Just looking at that sumptuous shearling tells you this is a jacket you’d never want to take off, especially on those brutal winter days.

Industry observers note that our editors spend a lot of time assessing what’s in, what’s cool, and what you should care about. It’s literally part of our whole job. Sometimes that means trying things out first-hand, sometimes it’s about thorough research, and sometimes it’s just something you know. Whatever the means, we’ve done the work to figure out what is and isn’t worth your time and money.

Tech Report: Christy Turlington’s Ruby-Red Lipstick Is the Easy Makeup Secret for Women Over 40

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (452 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Harpersbazaar

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that every product on this page was chosen by a Harper's BAZAAR editor.
  • The last few years have been marked by the “Lip Balm Wars.” That is, every brand—from Hailey Bieber’s Rhode to prestige labels like Chanel and Dior—has debuted more sheer, glossy, and hydrating formulas than classic lipstick bullets.
  • Last night, supermodel Christy Turlington stepped out at the Museum of Modern Art’s 2026 Annual Film Benefit in Fresh York, wearing a knit dress from Matthieu Blazy’s fall 2026 Chanel collection.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that every product on this page was chosen by a Harper's BAZAAR editor. We may earn commission on some of the items you choose to buy.

The last few years have been marked by the “Lip Balm Wars.” That is, every brand—from Hailey Bieber’s Rhode to prestige labels like Chanel and Dior—has debuted more sheer, glossy, and hydrating formulas than classic lipstick bullets. But even though we all own more than 10 emotional-support lip balms in various shades, flavors, and finishes, there's still nothing more powerful than a statement-making lip. This is especially true for women over 40.

Last night, supermodel Christy Turlington stepped out at the Museum of Modern Art’s 2026 Annual Film Benefit in Fresh York, wearing a knit dress from Matthieu Blazy’s fall 2026 Chanel collection. A dress this graphic and eye-catching needs makeup to balance it, and Turlington paired it with black eyeliner and a glossy ruby-red lipstick.

According to recent reports, while we don’t know the exact shade she wore last night, it’s clearly a formula that sits somewhere between a satin lipstick and a gloss-balm, with pigment that doesn’t sacrifice moisture or shine. Turlington is a Lancôme ambassador, so it could be the brand’s Lip Idole Butterglow Hydrating Lip Balm or L’Absolu Rouge Cream Lipstick. Otherwise, Chanel makes a gorgeous option in both the Rouge Coco Flash and Rouge Allure Extrait formulas. These formulas subtly plump and moisturize dry lips while blurring lip lines and imperfections.

Lancôme L'Absolu Rouge Moisturizing Cream Lipstick in 397 Berry Noir.

Chanel Hydrating Vibrant Shine Lip Colour.

Lancome Lip Idole Squalane-12 Butterglow Hydrating Lip Balm.

According to recent reports, the best part of this look is that it proves you don’t need to match your lipstick exactly to your outfit, as long as they’re in the same color family. While the Chanel dress is more of an orange-red knit, Turlington’s lipstick is a more neutral ruby that harmonizes with the warm tones and shades in the rest of her look. Plus, raspberry or ruby-red lipstick can brighten your face in seconds, even with little to no other makeup.

Bold lipstick is a bit outside Turlington’s day-to-day comfort zone; she told Bazaar recently that she’s “definitely an old-school Carmex or ChapStick kind of person, because I’m constantly reapplying it to my dry lips, especially in the winter.” The rest of her routine is equally as effortless: “I wash my face in the morning and moisturize a lot. Sometimes I even double-moisturize because, especially at this time of year, I get dry skin. And then, I’ll add a nice little layer of foundation, some blush, and mascara, and that’s kind of it, I’m on my way.”.

Having already dominated our cinema screens in 2026 with The Drama, The Odyssey, and Primetime, and with Dune: Part Three still to come, Robert Pattinson has somehow found room in his diary to take on another rather significant commitment: James Bond.

Yes, the man currently playing Batman is also our new 007. Somewhere, a casting director’s Rolodex is gathering dust.

Sources indicate that at this point, I’m half expecting the British actor to pop up in a director’s cut of The Devil Wears Prada 2 wearing a cerulean jumper. Then again, he did once profess his love of taking jobs from younger actors. Clearly, he wasn’t joking.

Now, don’t get me wrong, I’m hardly immune to Rob’s charms. As someone who lived through the cultural juggernaut that was Twilight, watching his transformation from sparkly vampire to one of the most charismatic actors of his generation has been a sight to behold. But his latest appointment begs the question: Is there only one leading man left in Hollywood?

For months leading up to the announcement, reports suggested the race to become Bond had been narrowed down to Damson Idris and Aaron Taylor-Johnson. Then Callum Turner’s name entered the mix, alongside Jack Lowden, Jacob Elordi, and Paul Mescal, followed by Nicholas Hoult, Josh O’Connor, and, at the eleventh hour, Robert himself. At one point, I was half-tempted to put myself forward for the role.

It has been revealed that yet, in hindsight, Rob’s casting perhaps shouldn’t come as much of a surprise. Bond will mark his second collaboration with director Denis Villeneuve before their first, Dune: Part Three, has even reached theaters. Christopher Nolan has already cast him twice (in Tenet and The Odyssey) while Matt Reeves is reuniting with the actor for The Batman Part II.

For all the talk of Hollywood’s movie star drought, its most influential filmmakers seem to have found their guy. And they’re not particularly keen on letting him go. Commercially, you can understand the appeal. The Odyssey alone has amassed more than $1.8 billion at the global box office, making it the second-highest-grossing film of 2026 so far behind Spider-Man: Brand Newly introduced Day.

In a recent development, of course, those ticket sales aren’t solely down to Robert Pattinson. Christopher Nolan’s name and the incredible ensemble cast of Zendaya, Tom Holland, Matt Damon, and Anne Hathaway, among others, carry considerable weight, but Rob’s ability to move between intimate independent films like The Lighthouse and sprawling blockbusters makes him an increasingly valuable commodity.

In a recent development, according to Box Office Watch, the five films Rob has appeared in over the past two years have collectively grossed more than $2.1 billion worldwide. And that’s before he sets foot on Arrakis to face Paul Atreides and the Fremen in December.

However, what’s interesting about the British actor becoming Hollywood’s ultimate leading man is that he’s spent much of his career actively dismantling that very archetype.

Look at his recent filmography: a fiancé whose behavior in The Drama triggers an intervention of sorts; the rather unpleasant Antinous in The Odyssey; a morally complicated exploration of To Catch a Predator’s Chris Hansen in Primetime; and the hapless Jackson grappling to support his partner in the throes of postpartum depression in Die My Love. Even his Batman is more emotionally unavailable sad boy than conventional superhero.

Speaking to The Guardian in July, veteran film journalist Steven Gaydos described Robert as “an accomplished and fearless actor with tremendous range,” praising his refusal to simply give audiences what they expect.

Perhaps that’s precisely what makes him so appealing to filmmakers. But there’s a difference between recognizing an actor’s talent and an industry becoming overly reliant on it.

Recent findings suggest that historically, Bond has been a vehicle for turning actors into international superstars. Rob’s casting arguably reverses that relationship. For Amazon MGM Studios, entrusting its first Bond outing to an established star with a multigenerational fan base feels like a particularly safe bet.

It has been revealed that but where does that leave the next generation of leading men? How do we discover another Robert Pattinson if Hollywood keeps casting Robert Pattinson?

Sources indicate that perhaps Hollywood doesn’t have a leading man problem so much as an imagination problem. And perhaps the next great movie star is already out there, waiting for someone to take the same chance on them.

After all, even Robert Pattinson had to be discovered once—no thanks to Jack Whitehall’s dad.

In a recent development, I spent much of Thursday staring at photographs of Jensen Huang’s shoes arranged in one soldierly line longer in both directions than the frame could hold. These dozen pairs—each different, all dazzling—were but a glimpse of his footwear armies. Jensen’s Hermès slip-ons and dozens of black leather jackets are not only his fashion signatures; they’re also proof of his decision to not waste precious energy deciding what clothes to wear each morning.

Industry observers note that this is a philosophy I share with Jensen, and my version saves even more time and energy: Don’t change clothes. But I like men’s shoes, I’ve sold men’s shoes, and I believe that a man’s shoes reveal facets of his public persona and private desires.

In Jensen’s case, there’s no mystery. He’s a brilliant guy who was once a small, smart immigrant kid bullied and beaten at a Kentucky Baptist reform school that his uncle mistook for a boarding school. Now he’s 63, a five-foot-six AI titan standing in adorable—size 9 is my guess—multi-thousand-dollar slip-ons atop his $140 billion, with his dick out and dripping all over his kicks du jour.

And we are left to sort the tragedy, seek catharsis, and remind ourselves again—and again—that Jensen Huang’s downfall awaits any man who ignores the fundamental law of our own animal nature: Ven der putz shteht, der sechel licht in drert: When the penis stands, the brain goes to hell.

Recent findings suggest that I make no moral judgment here; we have no basis or right to do so. The college sweetheart he married 41 years ago, along with their two grown children, are the only souls with standing in this case. But I think it’s only fair, in light of current reporting on Jensen’s three concurrent affairs—that’s two side pieces plus Princess Honey-Pot plus a wife—to reconsider that vast battalion of decision-saving slip-ons and what it notes.

The shoes reveal a man with smallish feet whose penis was too busy making decisions to consider laces, love, or the welfare of his family and business. And there aren’t enough shoes, dollars, or women in the world to fill the hole in Jensen Huang.

The Latin word ‘invidia’ means envy. This, given Jensen’s shoes, is not coincidence or irony; it’s a weakling’s shamed confession. Hermes needs to cobble one last pair for Jensen Huang, long, bright red, and floppy.

It’s that time of year again. Just as festival season comes to a close, awards season is already off to the races. While musicians and artists do it for the love of the game, you have to admit: getting a shiny trophy and industry-wide recognition from your peers is kinda nice.

While this year’s Grammy nominations included a ton of pleasant surprises (ahem, RAYE’s 11 nominations, Remi Wolf’s Best Upcoming Artist nod, and some posthumous recognition for the late Dolly Parton), they seemed to fall flat in a few areas. I’ll say it: Overall, I’m not that pressed over the 2027 nominations and am excited to see acts like Tinashe and underscores finally get recognition from the Recording Academy.

But known Grammy darlings like Harry Styles and Doja Cat were seriously snubbed this year, along with rising acts like Audrey Hobert and Malcolm Todd. So, without further ado, and in true Cosmo tradition, here are the biggest snubs from the 2027 Grammy nominations.

According to recent reports, after seeing Audrey Hobert transform from behind-the-scenes collaborator with her (equally snubbed!) bestie, Gracie Abrams, into a front-line singer-songwriter, I thought she’d be a shoo-in for Best New Artist this year. I was an early adopter when I proclaimed “Sue Me” as the song of summer 2025, and her debut album as one of the best albums of the year. Since then, she’s been the shooting star pop music has been craving with diary-entry songwriting and intimate sleepover vibes on stage—though she’s performed to thousands at Lollapalooza and beyond.

In a recent development, speaking of Audrey, her younger brother and fellow musician, Malcolm Todd, was also expected to potentially earn recognition in the Best Upcoming Artist category. Not only did he drop his third album Do That Again in June, but he also had several of his previous hits like “Earrings” and “Obsessica” take off on TikTok. Not to mention, Best New Artist nominee Don Toliver featured a sample of Malcolm’s track, “Chest Pain (I Love),” on his hit, “E85.” At least he landed that subtle nod!

Sources indicate that my man Harry is a known Grammy darling. He’s swept in the past, but this time around, he’s been seriously snubbed. For his fourth album, Kiss All the Time. Disco, Occasionally to not be recognized at all—let alone in any of the major categories—feels strange. Some will argue that it “didn’t hit the same” as his other albums, but after taking some time off and finding his way back to the club, he dropped an incredible body of work in KISSCO. Our intro to the record is his five-minute lead single “Aperture,” which reminded us all that the revolution might take place on the dancefloor.

Recent findings suggest that sienna Spiro rightfully earned a nod in the Best Newly introduced Artist category after winning the same award at this year’s VMAs. If she has a similar pipeline to Chappell Roan, she might just take home the golden gramophone, too. Her breakout moment comes off the success of her mega-viral ballad, “Die on This Hill.” And because ROTY honors production, the stunning string arrangements and her heart-wrenching vocal performance deserved some recognition here.

Sources indicate that another snub I’m shocked by is Noah Kahan. I personally don’t go here, but I know so many industry insiders and personal friends who ride hard for Noah, and I think they’re right to do so. His songwriting chops have made him one of the most successful artists of the streaming age, and to see his massive 2026 track “The Great Divide” get paid dust in the core categories feels out of character for the Recording Academy. (Though, his album of the same name earned a nod in the Best Contemporary Folk Album category.).

As much as I love Doja Cat, I’m not entirely surprised by her snub here. “Jealous Type,” as well as her Jack Antonoff-produced album, Vie, was a campy ode to the ’80s and should have been a major contender here. It’s unclear whether she submitted anything for consideration this year, but I find it hard to believe given Jack’s involvement and her track record as a Grammy darling. This era deserved more, but it’s not entirely a loss—I can see it having a bit of a resurgence in a few years.

It has been revealed that say it with me: JUSTICE FOR WEST END GIRL! Though Lily Allen and her art directors, Leith Clark and Nieves González, rightfully earned a nod in the Best Album Cover category, she didn’t land any in the core four categories. She made a powder-blue polka-dot puffer coat instantly recognizable, and along with a Duane Reade bag, it’ll serve as “gay Halloween” costume inspo for decades to come.

But back to the music—Lily hadn’t released an album since 2018 before she poured her heart out on West End Girl. It’s a deeply confessional record about her personal life and the downfall of her public marriage with Stranger Things star David Harbour, but it was also a comeback for the ages. To lay everything out as she did takes serious guts, and she did it the only way she knows: with her signature wit and deliciously unexpected production choices, standing ten toes down. (While…maybe wearing a dress printed with actual receipts and text messages, or a bib that reads “CUCK” in all caps.) Lily, I never doubted you!

Every product was carefully curated by an Esquire editor. We may earn a commission from these links. Here’s how we test products and why you should trust us.

In 2026, young men are generally on top of their skincare. But in the before times, a splash of cold water to the face was the extent of most morning regimens. That’s probably why so many middle-aged guys find themselves with dried-out, sun-damaged skin that isn’t quite where they want it to be. The good news is that it’s never too late to pick up good habits.

With that in mind, we asked six of the glowiest people we know to share the products they reach for every day—and the lessons they’ve learned along the way.

Sources indicate that caroline Hirons, aesthetician and writer: "Men’s skin is slightly thicker, and a high majority of men shave daily, which can cause its own set of problems if not done properly. Using the right kit and products is crucial: shaving oils, facial shaving products, post-shave moisturizers … A lot of men with a heavier beard would also benefit from using a daily acid exfoliator to prevent ingrown hairs.”.

“Skin Rules” by Caroline Hirons is out now.

Saul Nash, menswear designer: "“Korean skincare is everything. I use Reedle Shot 100 masks—I love them and they leave my skin glowing. I do think it’s crucial, though, not to trouble your skin too much—I have combination [different conditions across the face] to oily skin, so I try not to touch my face a lot or put too many products on it.”.

Harris Reed, designer: “It’s all about eye cream and a silk eye mask—these are non-negotiables.”.

Dr Richard Devine, aesthetic doctor and founder of Devine Clinic: “A product that’s working shouldn’t leave your skin feeling persistently red, sore, itchy, or inflamed. Mild adjustment periods can occur with certain active ingredients, but ongoing discomfort is usually a sign that the skin barrier is becoming irritated rather than improved. If redness, burning, or sensitivity continues beyond the first few uses, it’s often worth reducing frequency or reassessing whether the product is appropriate for your skin.”.

Ziad Halub, co-owner of Iranian-Iraqi café bistro Logma in Hackney: “After a hot and sticky day, your skin needs help. Sweat, dead skin, SPF, pollution, and general city grime can build into a layer of filth. A good foaming cleanser, one that doesn’t strip the skin, is essential. You want fresh, not squeaky. I’m currently loving African Botanics’ Baobab Clay Oxygenating Cleanser.”.

In a recent development, marc Terlet, co-founder of French grooming brand Horace: “At a minimum, an effective skincare routine involves washing your face, applying moisturizer, and then sunscreen. Make things easier with an SPF moisturizer but remember to reapply every couple of hours. The sun is responsible for 80 per cent of your skin aging. Imagine how young you would look if you’d used sunscreen every day since you were 20?”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, R ivals has returned to our screens, and Rutshire’s residents are hornier than ever.
  • There is a lot of awareness around age-gap couples in pop culture right now, and audiences seem very done with the classic younger woman, older man dynamic.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, R ivals has returned to our screens, and Rutshire’s residents are hornier than ever. But Rutag fans might have to hang on a little longer to see them enter their relationship era. Frustrating? Not necessarily, as maybe this intense slow-burn is exactly the reason Rivals has managed to create an age-gap relationship we’re actually rooting for.

There is a lot of awareness around age-gap couples in pop culture right now, and audiences seem very done with the classic younger woman, older man dynamic. Movies like A24’s Babygirl and Amazon’s The Idea of You have gone some way toward challenging outdated tropes around age-related power dynamics, but that still doesn’t erase how Hollywood handled things in the past (Pretty Little Liars and Fifty Shades of Grey come to mind).

Rivals is a bit of an anomaly in how it has tackled Rupert and Taggie’s age-gap relationship so far, and the slower pace seems to have played a very necessary part in that. Rutag’s slow-burn underpins the entire foundation of their connection. What’s working for me personally is that Rupert hasn’t been rushing Taggie emotionally or physically to match where he’s at in his current stage of life. In fact, even though he seems besotted with her—she’s sort of become his moral touchstone—he’s doing his best to stay away from her. He seems to find the idea of letting her down (or fully letting her in) absolutely terrifying, despite how much he clearly cares.

According to recent reports, rivals gains further grace from viewers for its willingness to openly acknowledge Rupert and Taggie’s age gap as being an obstacle to overcome in their relationship, rather than just glossing over it or choosing to pretend it doesn’t exist. Rupert even acknowledges the age gap as being an issue himself by making a promise to Declan in season 1 that he’ll stay away from Taggie. By showing us these hurdles early on, it gives deeper insight into what a relationship would eventually mean for these two and what they’d be up against.

Watching Taggie gain life experience and have her own adventures of self-discovery—not everything has to involve Rupert—has helped them remain exciting to us as a potential couple. Her catering business seems to be thriving, for example. The slow-burn gives Taggie the opportunity to forge her own identity and ambitions, which would be important to have going into a relationship with Rupert, given their differences in life experience. Taggie is slowly blossoming into herself, without falling into that cliché trap of trying to change who she is to impress a man, and that’s empowering and necessary.

As long as Rivals continues to explore the age gap with care and consideration, I think fans will keep rooting for Rutag’s romance, no matter how long the slow-burn takes.

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1022 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Harpersbazaar

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • On a recent Tuesday afternoon, I stopped by 7 for All Mankind’s SoHo store to meet Nicola Brognano, the brand’s newest creative director, for a one-on-one styling session.
  • Brognano’s aesthetic couldn’t be further from my own.
  • According to recent reports, brognano brought an exciting upcoming energy to 7 for All Mankind that built upon the label’s roots.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

On a recent Tuesday afternoon, I stopped by 7 for All Mankind’s SoHo store to meet Nicola Brognano, the brand’s newest creative director, for a one-on-one styling session. I felt a bit nervous, knowing I’d need to step outside of my sartorial safe space. For reference, my personal style tends to lean more minimal, a “classics with a twist” vibe. When I entered the store, I was wearing a striped button-down shirt, black jeans, and a trench coat—my typical uniform. Immediately, Brognano, wearing a leather jacket layered over a hoodie, was warm and kind. I felt my anxiety lessen, knowing I was going to be in good hands.

Brognano’s aesthetic couldn’t be further from my own. At Blumarine, where he served as creative director from 2020 to 2023, he transformed the brand away from bohemian, romantic whimsy and injected it with a jolt of Y2K energy (butterfly crop tops, slinkier dresses, and low-rise pants). In 2025, the designer took the creative helm of 7 for All Mankind and staged the brand’s inaugural runway show in February during New York Fashion Week. The appointment was a fitting choice for the American-born brand, which, when it rolled out in the 2000s, had every It girl wearing its low-rise jeans, from Britney Spears and Christina Aguilera to Nicole Richie and Paris Hilton. It was a time when Gossip Girl was the hottest show and Mary-Kate and Ashley Olsen were regularly spotted around the downtown New York scene with skinny scarves wrapped around their necks.

According to recent reports, brognano brought an exciting upcoming energy to 7 for All Mankind that built upon the label’s roots. His collection had a nostalgic Y2K-era undertone, but polished up for 2026. Models walked the runway in shrunken black peacoats with exaggerated shoulders, skinny scarves, cropped leather jackets, and sheer, silky blouses.

In a recent development, ultra-skinny jeans, wax-coated maxi skirts, and babydoll dresses were key hero pieces. Latest York’s coolest It girl, Chloë Sevigny, stars in the fall campaign; images from the shoot appear on digital screens throughout the store.

When he joined the brand, Brognano tells me, “I really wanted to bring that sexiness back.” In designing the collection, “I imagined a super cool, strong woman with an eccentric attitude,” he indicates. Could it be me?

Recent findings suggest that after we met and assessed my sizing, Brognano went straight to pulling looks for me. The first look I tried on was a semisheer blouse with an exaggerated pussy bow at the neck, ultra-low-rise dual-panel waxed skinny jeans (a leather-like finish on the front and rigid denim on the back), and, to top it off, a shrunken black peacoat. For the finishing touch, I slid on a pair of sky-high platform heels. I felt like I just stepped out of the early aughts and was ready to head to the club (in a good way).

I rarely wear heels. (I’m more of a flats-and-loafers kind of girl.) I don’t think I’ve ever worn platform heels in my life. While walking in them posed its own challenge, I did feel an overwhelming sense of confidence and sexiness. “The most key thing for the collection, for me, was the attitude,” Brognano tells me about the inspiration, adding, “I started thinking about Mary-Kate and Ashley Olsen at the time. And a mix of girls like that—a little bit rockish, a little bit indie sleaze.” I felt this spirit wearing his clothes, a sensibility that I hadn’t experienced since my early 20s and one I thought I’d moved far away from. I am presently nine months postpartum. The outfit gave me a jolt of energy that felt exhilarating.

7 for All Mankind Double-Breasted High Shoulder Jacket.

7 for All Mankind Silk Bow Houndstooth Shirt.

Recent findings suggest that the next look was a nice medium between what I would normally wear—a sweater and jeans—and something more off-kilter. The look was amplified in small ways: instead of a crewneck, it was a cape sweater with an extra-high neck; the jeans weren’t dark and tailored but light, fitted, and straight; the sky-high heels remained. I felt a little bohemian in this look, in a good way.

7 for All Mankind High Neck Shawl Sweater.

7 for All Mankind Slim in Cashmere Denim.

Sources indicate that for the final look, Brognano styled me in a deep-plum cinched leather peacoat. Underneath, I wore a silky, sheer brown bow-tie blouse and dark-gray vintage-style coated jeans. I was surprised by how soft and comfortable this particular pair of jeans was.

Recent findings suggest that this look felt more grown-up and polished than the other two, something I could wear out to dinner. While I’m not hitting the club these days, the clothes still felt like they were designed for someone like me too.

7 for All Mankind Double-Breasted High Neck Leather Jacket.

7 for All Mankind Long-Sleeve Bow Silk Shirt.

7 for All Mankind Calie Straight in Coated Denim.

While the skinny jean is the centerpiece of the collection, Brognano explains, “Denim is very democratic, and you can choose your shape every season because you have to feel good with your denim, and it has to give you the best shape for your body.… I think it’s something very personal.” Despite the fact that I’ve been a non-skinny-jean wearer for over a decade, Brognano found a sweet spot in my comfort level.

It was fun to play dress-up and step outside my traditional style for once. Sometimes all it takes is a push. While I won’t be wearing head-to-toe leather, leather skinnies, or platform heels every day, I left the day feeling more inspired, more confident, and more eager to have fun with my outfits again—not for anyone else, but just for myself.

Industry observers note that living vicariously through the characters in a romance show is always fun, but when the love story unfolds in a gorgeous location, it makes the fantasy even better. Are you enjoying the French series Campus Drivers on Prime Video, and feeling the itch to start exploring the area on Google Maps, Airbnb, and even Zillow? These Campus Drivers filming locations will get you started.

Sources indicate that the series follows a college student named Lois, who becomes temporarily homeless after getting dumped by her boyfriend/roommate and moves in with her neighbor. He happens to have a ride-share app, which is definitely not just for transporting drunk coeds he and his friends want to hook up with, and is named Lane. Normal meet-cute stuff. Also, Lois and Lane... get it?!

It has been revealed that but the setting really stands out. Dare I say it, the hallowed hall and shiny shores of Campus Drivers is far more glamorous than anything you’d see on Off Campus, Gossip Girl, and even Elite. The beaches, clubs, and architecture are beyond what we’re used to on collegiate shows like this. Here’s how they brought it to life.

Recent findings suggest that nope! The Prime Video series takes place at a fictional school on the French Riviera. However, according to Decider, Quill attended Carlone University (locally referred to as Campus Carlone) in Nice. So if you’re looking to study abroad, that might be a good place to start.

This is a major change from the book series, however, which takes place in the United States at a fictional school called Sycamore University. But since Quill herself is French, and went to school in France, this doesn’t feel like that significant of a change.

The Prime Video series filmed on the French Riviera, a.k.a. the Côte d’Azur, in the South of France between Nice, Cannes, and Antibes. Lane’s apartment is filmed at the Marina Baie des Anges, a famous waterfront complex in Villeneuve-Loubet. And finally, Villa Eilenroc in Cap d’Antibes is where they filmed Belrose University.

According to recent reports, while we can’t promise that your ride-share driver will become a fling (or more), these are fairly easily attainable vacation spots. Beaches like Les Ondes and Port Mallet on the Cap d’Antibes appear on the series and are open to the public. Start your planning now!

#19824. Is The Rings of Power Still Worth Watching?

📅 13 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (967 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Esquire ↗ Open Full Page

Is The Rings of Power Still Worth Watching?

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (967 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Esquire

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, when I was a kid, I was obsessed with something called Mystic Knights of Tir Na Nog.
  • According to recent reports, however unfair, it’s through that spectrum of two extreme ends that I see fantasy television like The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power.
  • According to recent reports, we’re four years and three seasons (lol) into The Rings of Power’s planned five seasons on Prime Video.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, when I was a kid, I was obsessed with something called Mystic Knights of Tir Na Nog. If you weren’t a first-grader in 1998, it was a Fox Kids Saturday morning series about four heroes in medieval Ireland who morphed into armored knights to battle dragons and evil witches. It was Power Rangers by way of Celtic mythology, and it kicked ass. I was a wee bit too young for Hercules and Xena then, and Mystic Knights made sword-and-sorcery stories accessible to my Saturday morning-addled brain. Two years after it went off the air, The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring stormed into theaters.

According to recent reports, however unfair, it’s through that spectrum of two extreme ends that I see fantasy television like The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power. I have a standard through which I see this genre in this particular medium. On the big screen, fantasy can feel endless, its scope stretching beyond the horizon. On the small screen, you can feel the ceiling over everyone’s heads. Even Game of Thrones had a coffee cup slip through the veil. Which is why, despite the distant relation to Peter Jackson’s immaculate movies, The Rings of Power is quintessential fantasy TV on par with Mystic Knights. That’s not a bad thing—it’s just perspective.

According to recent reports, we’re four years and three seasons (lol) into The Rings of Power’s planned five seasons on Prime Video. After all this time, it still hasn’t won over skeptics. There are long and boring reasons why Tolkien faithful have been averse to the prequel show. They have complaints about pacing, plotting, creative liberties from Tolkien’s textbooks of lore, and general execution. Regrettably, they more often than not get mixed up with old-fashioned racism and misogyny. (Valar forbid a dwarf be a Black woman.) But sometimes the worst people you know have a point: The Rings of Power has been an underwhelming experience. Despite its strong start in season 1, the show simply hasn’t escaped the long, long shadow of Jackson’s cinematic trilogy. (Even Jackson never lived up to his own standards. See: The Hobbit.).

Sources indicate that amid the show’s large ensemble, the series bet many of its chips on Charlie Vickers as Sauron. Though handsome, Vickers’ lack of charisma, middling scriptwriting for his role, and a severe lack of sexual tension with co-star Morfydd Clark (as Galadriel) have sadly made Rings of Power somnambulant. Now in season 3, the chance to course-correct is long past, and the rigor mortis of its missteps have now settled in.

According to recent reports, season 1 had a strong start. Sauron is a hottie, and his early relationship to Galadriel carried with it an air of intrigue and yearning until his mask came off. Maybe there could have been a whole show about their forbidden attraction. (Some fans have already coined “Saurondriel.”) The good girl/bad boy pairing is a tried and true tradition, with a subset of the Star Wars fandom possessing a bizarre obsession with Daisy Ridley’s Rey getting it on with Adam Driver’s Kylo Ren. Who are any of us to deny ourselves this pleasure?

But season 2 didn’t seize on nor improve what was its grace. Their characters were kept separate until the finale, where they reunited on the battlefield. It’s a good scene, to be fair, it’s just maddening that what could have been the whole show was just five minutes, including a bloodless sword fight.

Now here we are in season 3, and it’s more of the same. All of the characters are on a journey across Middle-earth, the story is moving along at a steady, if at times meandering pace, Sauron is quite literally plotting everything from his high tower, and there is a clear endpoint at the end of it all: the forging of the One Ring. As of this writing, the season’s four episodes (available to stream now) suggest we’ll get there in due time. There have been some major-name casualties already, and some impressive set pieces that actually feel like things are intensifying at the right temperatures.

It has been revealed that still, this is Lord of the Rings we’re talking about here. For all the lore and imagination Tolkien spilled onto his pages, his was a story still mired in the age-old tradition of good versus evil. That is Rings of Power too, where even morality comes in shades of stark black and white (mostly) and just enough polished VFX and production design to sell the immersion. One could ask, “What more do you want?” Somehow, it’s still not really enough. Even now, there is still too little energy, too little thrust, too little verve—and yes, still too little sex appeal—to warrant undivided attention. The Rings of Power is mighty pretty to look at on a big 50-inch LED screen. (I’m particularly engrossed anytime we follow Daniel Weyman’s Gandalf, who is always strolling through the most picturesque backdrops.) But it’s also far too easy to get distracted by more exciting things, like your laundry machine timer going off. In other words: The Rings of Power is a television show.

Sources indicate that for all the money Jeff Bezos spent on making Rings of Power a reality, it’s still just TV. It’s maybe a cruel, cosmic, and frankly righteous joke that the billionaire’s very clear marching orders to his team—“I want my Game of Thrones,” is how he was quoted—have resulted in precisely that. A fantasy television series. Blame the streaming era for pigeonholing everything of this caliber into a blockbuster with lofty expectations. Not all TV should be appointment viewing. Sometimes a TV show can and should just be what it is: Mystic Knights, with a few extra zeroes.
