The Men on 'The Gilded Age' Don't Deserve Your Praise

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (725 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cosmopolitan

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that it feels like television shows (and real life, let’s face it) are currently overrun with men who constantly fall short when it comes to matters of the heart.
  • We may only be a few episodes into the season, yet already viewers have witnessed several examples where the men in the show are found lacking when it comes to their romantic partnerships.
  • In a recent development, many fans online have been quick to come to Larry’s defense, criticizing Marian for self-sabotaging or playing the part of a martyr.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that it feels like television shows (and real life, let’s face it) are currently overrun with men who constantly fall short when it comes to matters of the heart. In the latest season of Nobody Wants This, many fans noticed how Joanne was constantly making sacrifices for their relationship while Noah just… wasn’t. The latest season of Love Is Blind also found the guys seriously wanting, with many failing to put in a bare minimum of effort to make a love connection. And it saddens me to say that this trend of low-effort men seems to have made its way to the fourth season of The Gilded Age as well. That’s right, my friends—not even the 19th century is safe from this epidemic of male apathy.

We may only be a few episodes into the season, yet already viewers have witnessed several examples where the men in the show are found lacking when it comes to their romantic partnerships. First, there’s Larry, who appears to have zero appreciation for the tough position Marian is now in after they spent the night together. Although he does suggest they get married, Marian worries it’s only out of obligation, and he seems to not really grasp the severity of the situation she’s in, that social ruin could be waiting for her if anyone found out about their night together.

In a recent development, many fans online have been quick to come to Larry’s defense, criticizing Marian for self-sabotaging or playing the part of a martyr. But I disagree. Her concerns are valid and Larry is being ambiguous about his feelings. Now would be the perfect time for a grand romantic gesture on Larry’s part to show Marian how serious he is about their relationship. Where’s the big, swoonworthy “You have bewitched me body and soul” moment? Where is the standing-outside-her-window-with-a-boombox (or 1800s equivalent) scene? I want to root for them, but Larry is making it extremely difficult with his underwhelming devotion.

Then there’s Hector, who was praised by Bertha for choosing to save Gladys’s life over their unborn child’s during an extremely difficult labor. While it is nice to know how much affection he has for his wife, it never should’ve been his choice to begin with, so applauding him for “saving” Gladys feels like a very low bar to set for these male characters. I understand this was a customary practice at the time and him making the decision was more the doctor’s doing than anything else, but now he’s also gatekeeping that she can’t have any more children. Watching a man determine when a woman should know something about her own body feels outrageous in any time period. I’m not saying that Hector is a bad guy, but I don’t think he deserves so much admiration for doing the bare minimum.

Meanwhile, George Russell continues to deal with (or rather, not deal with) his ongoing laudanum addiction, which is already growing tiresome with each passing episode. His relationship with Bertha has never been worse. She is putting in all the effort to repair their marriage while he remains cold and distant, lying to her at every turn. I understand this change in his behavior is due to his drug dependency, but should that make all of his missteps completely forgivable? Bertha assured him at the end of Sunday night’s episode, “I won’t disappoint you.” But it is he who is the disappointment right now.

Recent findings suggest that unfortunately, not even Dr. William Kirkland can get a free pass, despite his impeccable behavior leading up to his wedding day. Buying Peggy a house, standing up to his mother, and refusing to let her dictate the wedding — those are all major green flags. Yet next week’s promo indicated William might pursue a newly introduced job in Washington, which feels completely out of nowhere considering he just bought a house for the two of them. Also, this is something he should probably consult his wife about before making any public declarations. Is the honeymoon phase over already?

Bottom line: Chivalry may not be completely dead on this show, but its pulse is weak at best and if these gentlemen don’t do something about it soon we’re going to have even bigger problems than prematurely pouring milk into someone else’s tea.

I Just Finished My Kitchen Renovation, and This “Hidden” Island Feature Is the One Upgrade I’d Recommend to Everyone

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (831 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Housebeautiful

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that I’m always noticing something cool in someone else’s home and thinking, “Oh, I need that, too.” That happened last year when my family stayed with my in-laws.
  • It was simple, practical, and exactly the kind of feature I wanted in my own kitchen.
  • Ahead, here’s why I love having a pop-up outlet, what to consider before installing one, and a few other kitchen gadgets that you might want to consider adding to your next upgrade.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that I’m always noticing something cool in someone else’s home and thinking, “Oh, I need that, too.” That happened last year when my family stayed with my in-laws. It was my first time seeing their newly renovated kitchen, and after a quick tour, one small detail caught my eye: the pop-up outlet in the kitchen island.

It was simple, practical, and exactly the kind of feature I wanted in my own kitchen. When we recently renovated our cook space, it went to the top of our wish list—and it has indeed been a game-changer with how we use the area.

Ahead, here’s why I love having a pop-up outlet, what to consider before installing one, and a few other kitchen gadgets that you might want to consider adding to your next upgrade.

Recent findings suggest that like the name suggests, a pop-up outlet is basically an electrical outlet that hides inside your countertop until you need it. Most models have a top you press or pull, and the outlet rises up so you can plug in your blender, mixer, or whatever else you're using. When you're done, you push it back down and it's out of sight.

Industry observers note that there are a few different versions, including ones that pop up manually and others that rise with the push of a button. Some, like the one we have, include USB ports or wireless charging built in. The outlet connects to power underneath the countertop, so it's something you'll want to plan for before your new counters go in.

In a recent development, like pretty much any kitchen gadget, there are a range of options available from budget to high end. We opted for something mid-tier that still included the main functions we wanted like the additional USB ports and the charging capability on the top. If you’re a chronic “let your phone get down to one or two percent before finally charging it” person like me, I highly recommend this.

There also are some that will go nearly fully flush with the countertop, and can even have part of the countertop material on the top of it to look seamless. We did not go this route, but if you prefer the look of a flawless countertop, this might be the way to go.

Sources indicate that we put ours in the corner of our kitchen where it’s almost entirely hidden by decor. That corner of the kitchen was otherwise without any spots to plug in appliances, so this fixed multiple problems by having electricity access while remaining discreet.

In a recent development, you can really put them anywhere you want, but keep in mind where you’ll need extra power accessibility and where it won’t be an eyesore, if that’s a concern. I’m also a major fan of in-drawer charging outlets.

There was some back-and-forth about adding this pop-up outlet to our kitchen remodel budget. The outlet itself isn’t break-the-bank expensive, but there were extra expenses that went with it, like hiring an electrician and paying to have a hole cut in the upcoming countertop.

Though we decided it was worth the expense, here are some of the pros and cons you should consider if you’re on the fence.

Industry observers note that I’m always so impressed by kitchens that integrate small, helpful gadgets like this one into their design. Here are a few other popular additions that we either made or were thinking about adding to our renovation.

Maybe it’s just a me thing, but I feel like the harder it is to find an appliance or trash can, the fancier a kitchen is. The pull-out trash can was integrated into our kitchen peninsula, and we purchased a more expensive panel-ready dishwasher so it looked like a regular cabinet. An integrated refrigerator was almost twice as expensive as a regular one, so we did not go that route.

According to recent reports, with the way our kitchen is laid out, we unfortunately have two awkward corner cabinets. For one, we upgraded with blind corner cabinet hardware, which was well worth it.

In a recent development, we did not integrate a bottle rinser into our current kitchen design, but we did in our last two kitchens and loved them. It got so much use when our two kids were babies, since we could promptly rinse out bottles. They’re also great for wine drinkers or anyone who hosts a lot of parties.

Admittedly, this one is controversial, as some designers don’t like this feature. But personally, we love the look and it’s next on our “cool kitchen wish list.”.

Alex Shoemaker is a writer and digital content strategist who covers home renovation, DIY projects, and design inspiration. He has written for multiple home improvement magazines and websites, drawing on his own experience renovating homes with his wife to create practical, inspiring content for homeowners and DIY enthusiasts alike.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Surprise! Sam Hartman has officially gone from being the Washington Commanders’ quarterback to becoming the lead for The Bachelor season 30. Some fans are all too familiar with the NFL athlete, but in case you don’t go here in the sports department…there’s apparently already some drama behind the scenes.

According to recent reports, after ABC officially announced Sam as the next Bachelor on Friday, November 13, some of his ex-girlfriends reacted to the news. Let’s just say they didn’t seem too pleased with his quarterback-to-reality-star pipeline.

An interior designer from Naples named Becca Hunt shared an old photo of herself with Sam—who she claims to have dated in the past—on TikTok.

“The most toxic relationship of my life is now the bachelor LOL,” her post reads.

In a separate comment, she added, “look yall i am not going to say anything more abt this i just thought it was ironic because it’s a dating show.”.

Naturally, her comments section went wild over the revelation.

“This tracks. A man can’t have a face card this lethal and be pure of heart,” one fan alleged, while another chimed in, “I said ‘wow he’s hot’ then they asked what he was looking for in a wife and he said ‘competitiveness’ and lost interest immediately.”.

As it turns out, she isn’t the only ex of Sam’s who has spoken out amid his announcement.

Lauren Blake Boultier, who reportedly dated the football star for seven months (and who, earlier this year, was accused of photoshopping her face onto Black content creator Tatiana Elizabeth’s body) jokingly told TMZ that he has the “personality of asparagus.”.

As for what that really means? According to Lauren, “He’s good for you, but he’s not exactly the most exciting thing on the menu.”.

She emphasized that she’s “genuinely rooting for him, even if their own romance didn’t work out,” and even named some of his redeeming qualities: “family oriented, down to earth and absolutely husband material for the right woman.”.

While the model and DAZN boxing host is more adventurous and spontaneous, she claimed that Sam loves his routine, which includes football, family, and fishing in his free time.

What’s more: She took to TikTok to post a photo of herself and Sam together with the caption, “When you get casted to go on the Bachelor but the Bachelor turns out to be your ex”…only to delete remarked post.

As far as exes go, Sam is also rumored to have dated former Wake Forest soccer star Tyla Ochoa (having confirmed he was dating a Wake Forest soccer player during a 2024 interview), but she has yet to weigh in on the casting news.

So…what is the truth? Is this man boring, toxic, both, or neither? Guess we’ll have to find out when The Bachelor season 30 hits ABC next year.

Latest Update: Nanofat Is Dermatologists’ Best-Kept Secret for Younger, Fresher Skin

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (916 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Harpersbazaar

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that the last few years have been unkind to our facial fat.
  • In a recent development, “Adipose tissue is a rich source of growth factors and progenitor cells, and re-injecting fat is probably one of the best ways to regenerate the full potential of healthy skin I've seen in the last decades,” says Patricia Ogilvie, a Munich-based dermatologist and member of the Dior Reverse Aging Board.
  • In a recent development, you’re probably familiar with fat transfer, a procedure that’s been around for decades.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that the last few years have been unkind to our facial fat. We sliced out our buccal pads to create sunken-in, razor-sharp cheekbones. We zapped our skin with thermal devices that accidentally melted fat away in pursuit of boosting collagen. We injected our stomachs with fat-loss GLP-1 medications, leaving our faces looking hollow. Droopy. Structurally unsound. As it turns out, facial fat is critical infrastructure—not just for looking younger, but for your skin's overall health and quality. And while you can’t choose where you lose or gain fat, you can choose to have a doctor siphon it, remix it, and reinject it.

In a recent development, “Adipose tissue is a rich source of growth factors and progenitor cells, and re-injecting fat is probably one of the best ways to regenerate the full potential of healthy skin I've seen in the last decades,” says Patricia Ogilvie, a Munich-based dermatologist and member of the Dior Reverse Aging Board. “There are trends that are not really worth being a trend. I think the restaging of the importance of adipose tissue is very justified.”.

In a recent development, you’re probably familiar with fat transfer, a procedure that’s been around for decades. In simple terms, fat transfer takes adipose tissue from one area of your body, like your flanks, liposuctions it, and moves it to another area, like your breasts or cheekbones. “With traditional fat transfer, it’s about restoring volume. And because it’s your own living tissue, it can integrate beautifully and give you very natural-looking results,” says dermatologist Shereene Idriss, medical director and founder of Idriss Dermatology in Latest York City. “But what’s interesting is that fat isn’t just fat. It also contains regenerative cells, including adipose-derived stem cells, and growth factors that may help improve the surrounding tissue over time. Nanofat is where it gets really exciting.”.

Nanofat is part of a newly introduced class of regenerative aesthetics offered by dermatologists and plastic surgeons, treatments that don’t just make you look better, but rather address the signs of aging from the inside out by stimulating collagen or repairing tissue. Imagine taking that same fat from a traditional fat transfer and processing it into a fine, milky liquid rich in your own stem cells and growth factors, then injecting or microneedling it back into your face—that’s nanofat.

“Instead of using it to restore volume, you’re using it to potentially improve skin quality itself,” says Idriss. “These cells and growth factors communicate with surrounding tissue and can stimulate processes involved in collagen production, tissue repair, and blood vessel formation. So you’re not just trying to fill a wrinkle. You’re trying to improve the skin itself—its thickness, resilience, and texture—so that wrinkle potentially becomes less noticeable.”.

It has been revealed that the best areas for nanofat injections include under the eye, a notoriously risky area for hyaluronic acid fillers, and the cheekbones. “The ideal patient for nanofat is someone who's starting to notice thinner, crepier skin, fine lines, or changes in skin texture, especially around the eyes, neck, or chest, and wants to improve skin quality rather than add volume,” adds Idriss, who both has had the treatment done and offers it in her practice. Plus, Ogilvie notes, nanofat doesn’t attract water the way fillers do, so it won’t cause under-eye puffiness (a common post-filler complaint). But because nanofat doesn’t restore volume as much as it reinvigorates your skin, you can inject it almost anywhere you’re noticing signs of aging.

Recent findings suggest that “We do it under tumescent local anesthesia, so you’re awake the entire time, and recovery is usually pretty quick,” says Idriss. “I personally had nanofat and fat transfer in June and was back at work the next day. The biggest downside is some soreness at the fat extraction site, which usually lasts a few days, and you’ll want to avoid strenuous exercise for about a week. Because there’s no general anesthesia, you’re also avoiding the grogginess and recovery associated with being put under.”.

Like any cosmetic treatment, it has risks and downsides. Experts note that nanofat isn’t the right treatment for anyone looking to restore significant volume loss or seeking instant results. “Improvement in skin quality can vary from person to person, and it takes months to see the full results,” Idriss adds. “There are rare but serious risks, including infection, vascular complications, and even vision loss when injecting certain areas of the face.” But patients who have tried the procedure say the recovery is quick and easy, with results compounding over weeks, though they ultimately fade away faster than traditional injectables.

Nanofat injections sit somewhere between microfat and hyaluronic acid fillers. Microfat can be lumpy and unpredictable when injected, sometimes leading to lopsided results. Plus, in any fat transfer, only a small amount of fat survives. Fillers, on the other hand, offer long-lasting precision and volume restoration, but patients are tired of looking overfilled and unnaturally plump. Nanofat helps your skin look naturally healthier, fresher, and firmer, at least for a while. After all, it’s made from you.

According to recent reports, “I look at this as something you can do periodically throughout your life, but what you do in between treatments is just as important. And that’s why I don’t believe in demonizing any one treatment, including filler,” indicates Idriss. “When used appropriately, for the right indication, these treatments can all work beautifully together. It’s about knowing what you need, when you need it, and when enough is enough.”.

Your Expert-Backed Guide to Preparing for Top Surgery

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1632 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cosmopolitan

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that we may earn commission from links on this page, but we only recommend products we love.
  • Getting ready to go under the knife can be scary—even when it’s for a procedure you’ve wanted for as long as you can remember.
  • If you’re wondering how to prepare for top surgery without all the panic-inducing anecdotes, you’ve come to the right place.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that we may earn commission from links on this page, but we only recommend products we love. Promise.

Getting ready to go under the knife can be scary—even when it’s for a procedure you’ve wanted for as long as you can remember. If you’re preparing for top surgery (a gender-affirming chest surgery to remove or augment breast tissue) right now, chances are you’re probably trying to ease your pre-op anxiety by googling every question you can possibly think of. And that’s normal! But it can also lead you down some deep, dark Reddit threads that’ll do nothing but amplify your nerves.

If you’re wondering how to prepare for top surgery without all the panic-inducing anecdotes, you’ve come to the right place. I chatted with three experts and got their best advice on how to get ready for the procedure while preserving your peace of mind.

Recent findings suggest that before we get into the tips, keep in mind that the most notable part of preparing for top surgery is choosing the right surgeon for you. In addition to finding an experienced and gender-affirming doctor, you’ll want to pick someone who can give you the results you’re looking for. “The techniques your surgeon will use can vary quite a lot depending on your breast size and shape, the texture and quality of your skin, and your goals for the procedure,” explains Eric Plemons, PhD, an associate professor of anthropology and cochair of the Transgender Studies Research Cluster at the University of Arizona.

To make sure you’ll be happy with your results, he suggests watching YouTube videos showcasing before-and-afters and looking at post-surgery images online to help you get an idea of what you want. Then be sure to find a surgeon who understands your goals—if they seem like they’re not listening to you, ditch them. Once you’ve made an appointment with a surgeon you trust, here’s everything else the experts recommend doing to prepare for top surgery.

Industry observers note that this might seem like a no-brainer, but it’s worth mentioning. Before your surgery, your doctor’s office will normally provide you with instructions on what to do before and after the procedure. They typically include info on dietary guidelines, activity restrictions, wound care, and any medications you might need. Make sure that you read all of the information carefully, and keep it handy for the recovery process. “Following these instructions diligently significantly improves surgical outcomes and ensures a smoother recovery,” explains Scott Mosser, MD, FACS, a plastic surgeon who performs gender confirmation surgery and the founder of The Gender Confirmation Center of San Francisco.

Top surgery is a major surgery, and you’ll likely spend the first one to two weeks at home resting after the procedure. So it’s a good idea to prep your space accordingly. Make sure you’ve got a cozy couch or bed setup ready, and consider getting a mastectomy pillow to make lounging and sleeping more comfortable. The Trans Health Program at Fenway Health also recommends getting other items like a long phone charger, a grabber tool, and a back scratcher to make recovery go a bit smoother.

In a recent development, also, keep in mind that you’re not supposed to lift your arms above your head in the days following top surgery. To make that easier to navigate, consider moving food and essentials to lower, easy-to-reach spots, suggests Plemons.

According to recent reports, the last thing you want to do is spend your recovery period stressing about going back to your job. Be sure you request enough time off to allow yourself to truly rest and heal. Exactly how much time you’ll need to spend OOO varies from person to person, so it’s a good idea to chat it through with your surgeon at one of your pre-op appointments.

Industry observers note that one of the main factors that determines how long you’ll need to take off work is how physically demanding your job is. You’ll have restricted movement in the weeks after your surgery, and you won’t be able to lift heavy objects, which could impact your responsibilities, depending on your line of work. “I generally ask patients to identify the most physically strenuous aspect of their job, and together we determine an appropriate leave period,” explains Dr. Mosser.

For your post-op wardrobe, you’ll want a stack of loose-fitting shirts that are easy to put on and take off without raising your arms. (Yup, t-shirts might be off the table for a bit.) Button-up and zip-up options will be your best friends during the recovery period. The loose-fitting aspect is also important because you may need space for surgical drain tubes under your shirt. Tops with interior pockets can also be helpful if you do end up with drains, says Dr. Mosser. And heads-up: Your shirts might get stained during the healing process, so Plemons recommends grabbing some options from the thrift store so that you’re not worried about ruining them.

In order to help your skin adjust post-surgery, you may want to get an emollient-infused moisturizer like Bio-Oil or Palmer’s Cocoa Butter Lotion. As long as it’s okay with your doctor, you can even start applying these one to two weeks before the procedure to start prepping your skin, if you’d like. After the surgery, Dr. Mosser recommends using one of these moisturizers on your chest every morning and evening—but be careful to avoid your incision sites. This will help with skin relaxation and reduce the appearance of stretch marks, if that’s something you’re concerned about, he explains.

Double-check with your surgeon, but after any scabs from the surgery have fallen off, you should also be able to start using silicone scar tape. Dr. Mosser suggests using it for three months to help optimize healing.

According to recent reports, if you vape or smoke cigarettes or weed, you’ll need to quit ahead of your top surgery. The American College of Surgeons recommends quitting smoking four to six weeks before any major surgery and staying smoke-free for at least four weeks post-op to lower your risk of complications, and most doctors require a similar timeline for top surgery.

According to recent reports, the stakes are high: According to the Gender Confirmation Center of San Francisco, smoking increases the risk of anesthesia complications and postoperative complications like losing a nipple graft, which can require additional surgery to fix. It also delays healing, which can prolong the recovery process and make it more uncomfortable. Dr. Mosser requires all of his patients to stop smoking for at least three weeks before and after top surgery—no exceptions.

You’ll need some help taking care of yourself and your basic needs in the days following top surgery, so talk to your friends and/or family in advance to put together a plan. “We’ve consistently seen better outcomes in patients who have a positive, supportive presence in their lives. The best way to ensure this support is to communicate openly with loved ones in advance, set clear expectations about what assistance might be needed, and cultivate an environment of encouragement and care,” Dr. Mosser states.

Industry observers note that decide who’s going to drive you home after the procedure (you won’t be allowed to drive yourself), and think about who might be a good fit to help you with activities like getting dressed and showering the first few days, suggests Plemons. You’ll probably also need someone to help you with tasks like meal prep, medication reminders, carrying groceries, and caring for any pets for a bit.

Industry observers note that in addition to logistical support, you’ll likely need some emotional support during the top surgery process. The procedure is often something you’ve been anticipating for a long time, and it can be an emotional experience. “Such a big event comes with big feelings about your body, about yourself, and about your future,” says Plemons. So think about who you proposal to lean on for support as you navigate your feelings both pre- and post-op. Staying connected to your community—whether that be friends, chosen family, or an online community—is really important. “Even small moments of support, like check-ins or affirming conversations, can make a huge difference in feeling cared for during recovery,” adds Jesse Kahn, LCSW-R, CST, director and sex therapist at the Gender & Sexuality Therapy Center in New York.

“Top surgery is a significant emotional and physical milestone, and a range of feelings—excitement, anxiety, or unexpected emotions—are completely normal,” explains Kahn. They recommend giving yourself permission to feel and process your emotions without judgment or criticism. Your emotional support network can help with this, but if you’re already seeing a therapist you may want to schedule a session early on in your recovery. “[A therapy session] can be a good opportunity to just check in, look inward, reflect on what you’re experiencing, and give space for your emotions,” claims Kahn. Practicing self-care, managing expectations, and doing activities that bring you comfort are also very important during the top surgery process, they add.

Give yourself something you look forward to by thinking about what you want to wear once you’ve healed. Buy a shirt in a style you’ve always wanted to wear, or initiative out an outfit that’ll showcase your post-op body. “Choose something that will fit you well and show off the body you’re excited to have," suggests Plemons. "After soreness and swelling, it is amazing how gratifying it is to slip into that special shirt (or strut around in no shirt at all).”.

This article is not intended to be a substitute for medical advice. Always seek the advice of your doctor or other qualified health professional with any questions you may have regarding surgery.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, last month, while taking in the spring/summer 2027 demonstrates at Paris Fashion Week, I was eager to write about the street style trends bubbling up around the showgoers in town. Which proved harder than anticipated. For one thing, the flashiest dressers had been given full looks by the brands whose shows they were being paid to attend, and reporting on those felt like a somewhat dishonest exercise in journalism. For another, the consensus seems to be that we are living in a post-trend world, and fashion people in particular have little interest in dressing like anyone else. And so I turned my attention to real-life Parisians, among whom one item seemed to proliferate: jeans.

No, this isn’t going to be a trend report on something as perennially popular as denim, but on a particular high-waisted, flared style that I spotted so frequently, I was forced to dredge up what little French remains from my GCSEs to ask a woman where hers were from as I caught her climbing onto a Lime bike outside Le Saint-Gervais bar. “Excuse-moi, madame, votre pantalons… le brand?” She paused for a moment, swung her leg over the saddle, and unleashed a torrent of French from which I managed to decipher just two words: “Anna” and “Gérard Darel”, the latter needing no explanation.

Industry observers note that founded in Saint-Germain-des-Prés in the 1970s, the brand has long been a shorthand for what the rest of the world considers the tenets of French-girl style: discreet, easy-to-wear classics with a cultivated air. (So cultivated, in fact, that the brand acquired the original handwritten Proust Questionnaire in 2003, and recently collaborated with the philosopher Alain de Botton on a card-game version.) Which is all very Left Bank, of course, but perhaps the clearest evidence of its credentials is just how commonplace Gérard Darel is in everyday Parisian life. You can scarcely move for its iconic 24H bag—a soft, logo-free shoulder bag that Vogue once named among the bags of the century, alongside the Hermès Birkin – during the school rush on the Métro, where it is generally to be found stuffed with binders and tangled wired headphones.

But back to the jeans–an American invention, admittedly, but then again, this is the land of French fries. What made my startled Parisienne’s look so good? Much of it comes down to the cut–something Kate Moss, a woman who found fame in nothing more than a pair of jeans, understands, having been photographed in the brand’s Anna jeans as early as 2019. Designed by former creative director Valérie Gerbi and named after her daughter Anna – granddaughter of the brand’s founders, Danièle and Gérard Darel–the design braces at just the right point on the hips, fits snugly through the thighs and flares outwards just below the knee, skimming the top of a pair of shoes to create the illusion of longer legs. The double belt loops, meanwhile, criss-cross along the waistband to give the impression of a cinched waist, while the back pockets perform a similarly flattering service for the bum.

In a recent development, and yet the technicalities of a good fit can only explain so much. Perhaps the true appeal was in the way she wore them–with white ballet flats that I’m convinced were from Repetto’s men’s section (the Luciens) and a navy three-quarter-zip jumper with the sleeves pushed up–or the ease with which disappeared into the Marais, hair whipping in the wind.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, every product on this page was chosen by a Harper's BAZAAR editor.
  • It’s almost 9:00 p.m., and my work dinner in Manhattan’s SoHo neighborhood is finally coming to a close.
  • My idea to walk after dinner came from a video I saw months ago from a TikTok nutritionist who touted a brisk 10-minute walk after meals as the key to boosting metabolism, regulating blood sugar levels, and helping your stomach digest food.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, every product on this page was chosen by a Harper's BAZAAR editor. We may earn commission on some of the items you choose to buy.

It’s almost 9:00 p.m., and my work dinner in Manhattan’s SoHo neighborhood is finally coming to a close. As the people around me start to get up and call their Ubers, I head out the door to go home—on foot. After a lavish dinner, most people’s last thought is to get a brisk walk in, but for me, it’s crucial—not to hit a step count or burn calories, but as my version of a digestif, if you will.

My idea to walk after dinner came from a video I saw months ago from a TikTok nutritionist who touted a brisk 10-minute walk after meals as the key to boosting metabolism, regulating blood sugar levels, and helping your stomach digest food. My two favorite pastimes are eating and walking. I never thought the two would go hand in hand.

“Sitting briefly after eating isn’t inherently harmful, but prolonged, uninterrupted sitting can lead to a higher post-meal blood-sugar response compared with breaking it up with short walks,” says Elizabeth Sharp Edens, an internal medicine and obesity medicine physician, functional medicine practitioner, and founder of HMW Method. A 2022 meta-analysis in Sports Medicine found that light-intensity walking reduced post-meal glucose by almost 17 percent. The same study found that standing breaks after meals reduced glucose spikes by 9.5 percent on average. The TL;DR: Research says that any type of movement can improve glucose levels.

In a recent development, we know walking can do wonders—it can clear the mind, help you lean out, and even boost dopamine—but why is it a solution for feeling less full and avoiding afternoon crashes? “When you walk, your muscles use glucose for energy,” Edens explains. “Muscle contractions move glucose transporters called GLUT4 to the surface of muscle cells, helping draw glucose out of the bloodstream through a pathway that doesn’t depend on insulin.” Since your legs, the vehicle for walking, contain some of the biggest muscles in your body, it makes sense that walking effectively stimulates muscle contractions that move glucose transporters. “Walking breaks are a simple way to support blood sugar management while getting your steps in,” she adds.

While many rely on peptides, green powders, and “magic” supplements, walking is an easy, mindless (and free) way to improve digestion and prevent blood-sugar crashes. “Even two to five minutes after a meal can help, ideally before the glucose peak, typically 60 to 90 minutes after eating,” Kiran Krishnan, a research microbiologist, the founder and chief science officer of the Biome Learning Center, and Dose key opinion leader, adds.

I often joke after large meals that I will have to be rolled home. The good news: Walking can also reduce the overwhelming feeling of fullness. “Walking also helps the gut physically,” Krishnan claims, citing a study that found that a slow walk after a meal significantly shortened the time it took the stomach to empty half its contents. “For people prone to bloating, mild [walking] cut intestinal gas retention from 45 percent to 24 percent and eased symptoms,” he adds. Plus, Krishnan says studies show reduced LDL cholesterol levels and improved liver function in those who walked after meals.

Then there’s good old gravity, says Caitlin Hosmer, a Maine-based registered dietitian and co-founder of MenoPantry. “Gravity helps too, which is part of why walking may help people who feel uncomfortably full or get reflux after meals,” she explains. “Gentle movement and staying upright help food move out of the stomach and along the digestive tract.”.

In a recent development, ten minutes isn’t long, but studies show it’s just as effective as a longer walk. A 2025 study published by PubMed Central found that a 10-minute walk lowered glucose measurements by 6 percent and a 30-minute walk lowered glucose levels by 5 percent, meaning just 10 minutes of walking is all you need to help reduce a post-meal glucose spike. If you can walk for 30 minutes, an hour, or even longer—that’s great. But just 10 minutes can work just as well.

Industry observers note that what matters most is how swiftly you get moving. “Glucose typically peaks 60 to 90 minutes after eating, and moving before that peak is what blunts the spike,” Hosmer says. “A walk puts your muscles to work just as glucose from the meal is flooding into the bloodstream.” At first, I questioned whether I had to walk after every meal. “Put your effort where it counts most: after your largest, most carbohydrate-rich meal,” Hosmer advises, adding that for most, that’s after dinner, but walking after all three meals is ideal.

My post-meal walks varied—some days I would walk for 30 minutes or even an hour, depending on how much time I had and where I was going next. But as I started incorporating them into my work schedule, especially on busy office days, I often had only 10 minutes to spare. When in a pinch, I would get up and walk around the office floor and, at home, do air squats, which engage the same large leg muscles as walking and can be just as effective as a post-meal walk.

It may feel strange to pencil in time to walk after every meal, but the benefits I have noticed surpass any inconvenience or awkwardness. I have fewer crashes after I eat, whereas I previously would feel lethargic after every meal. I’ve also noticed improved digestion. While this can be chalked up to a number of things (my beloved vibration plate, greens powders, or digestive enzymes), I always feel lighter and less full after a post-meal walk.

It’s also not meant to feel daunting or like a chore. “Your post-dinner walk isn’t a workout. It’s a way of helping your body handle the meal,” Hosmer says. “The one real ‘wrong way’ is skipping it because you think it has to be long or perfect. I often say something is better than nothing, and that’s especially true here. Even a few minutes of walking, started soon after you finish eating, can blunt the blood sugar rise, and it may help your digestion too.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It’s been an incredible year in New York City. The start of Zohran Mamdani’s mayoralship set a joyful tone that underscored the city’s immaculate vibe these last few months: the Knicks’ championship win, Harry Styles’ MSG residency, and a Saturday Halloween/Sunday marathon double whammy. So leave it to John Mulaney to take the city down a peg.

According to recent reports, in the latest Saturday Night Live, the sketch of the night was easily “Central Park Horse & Carriage Ride.” Mulaney plays an off-kilter horse-cab driver (“You just trust me implicitly? You realize I have a top hat and a whip, right?”) who shows two tourists, played by Kam Patterson and Marcello Hernández, the best and worst of Latest York. With the impending ban on horse-drawn carriages in Central Park slated for June 2028, this is among the last times anyone can tour the city like this.

The sketch is unofficially a tribute to Broadway—a New York cultural staple—with short songs that pay homage to indicates like Little Shop of Horrors, Funny Girl, Annie Get Your Gun, and West Side Story. The buzzy Oh, Mary! gets a major tip of the hat too, with current star Bowen Yang making a surprise return to 30 Rockefeller Plaza.

After a mandatory number pointing out that Central Park isn’t safe at night, you get Kenan Thompson as a weed cloud, Tommy Brennan as a rival pedicab cyclist (“I’ll take you to the MoMA/Put you in a coma” is a bar, I’m sorry), and a genuine crowd-pleasing duet with James Austin Johnson and Jeremy Culhane who sing “about a boy named Mamdani.” And there’s Yang, as “Mary Todd Lincoln Tunnel,” who sings a cover of “And I Am Telling You” about commuting through Newly introduced Jersey.

Recent findings suggest that but really, the biggest showstopper of the sketch and frankly all of Saturday Night Live this week is VERONIKA SLOWIKOWSKA. As a marathon runner who still hasn’t finished the race, Slowikowska highlights off her golden pipes in a cover/parody of “Don’t Rain on My Parade.” Plainly, she crushes it. It’s moments like these that make you remember that SNL is full of overqualified, overly energetic theater kids now, and not stand-up comics blitzed out on cocaine.

You can watch the sketch in the embed below.

Industry observers note that the sketch was maybe the best part of a pretty standout SNL, which was owed to the simple fact that Mulaney was the host. A former show writer turned seven-time guest host, Mulaney’s presence was essentially permission to let everyone’s hair down so they could take bigger swings. Mulaney himself said it: “I used to be a writer at this show, and one of the only difficult things about working here was dealing with the host. So it’s fun when I host, because it’s like there’s no host.” Kinda explains the sketch.
