  • Investor(s): Republic Brands Group (portfolio includes: Jason Wu, Christian Siriano, Joie).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that introducing the Vogue Business Funding Tracker, a running list highlighting the most notable and intriguing investment and M&A activity in fashion and beauty. From emerging disruptors to legacy giants undergoing major changes, we spotlight the deals that are shifting the dynamics of the sectors we cover, including fashion, beauty, tech and sustainability.

Tech giant description: Republic Brands Group has acquired Rebecca Minkoff, which was founded by Minkoff and her brother Uri in 2005. The acquisition comes as the brand enters a newly introduced phase of growth following a successful transition to an asset-light licensing model, according to the company. Republic Brands plans to expand the brand’s international footprint and retail partnerships, with the view of doubling the business in 2027. Minkoff, who is chief creative officer, will remain closely involved in the brand’s creative direction under its new ownership.

Funding and round: Acquisition.

Investor(s): Republic Brands Group (portfolio includes: Jason Wu, Christian Siriano, Joie).

In a recent development, investor comments: “Rebecca Minkoff represents exactly the type of brand we believe has tremendous untapped potential,” Sami Souid, founder and CEO of Republic Brands Group, mentioned in a statement. “It has strong consumer recognition, an authentic design identity and significant opportunities for global expansion. Our strategy is to unlock that potential through best-in-class operating partners, disciplined brand management and a focused approach to building a global lifestyle business.”.

Company description: Founded in 2023, Counsel Health is an AI-powered primary care platform that combines medical AI with a network of physicians to deliver personalized medical guidance and treatment. The company has agreed to be acquired by Finnish smart ring maker Oura for $625 million, as Oura looks to move beyond biometric tracking toward more holistic, tailored health insights and actionable medical care. The acquisition will integrate Counsel’s AI and on-demand physicians with Oura’s continuous health data collection, enabling users to access medical advice, prescriptions, lab result interpretations, and chronic care support through the Oura app.

Funding and round: Acquisition, $625 million.

According to recent reports, investor comments: “Oura helps members understand their physiology and, with Counsel, they can take action on their health across a range of needs, from quick questions and prescriptions to lab results, chronic care and referrals,” said Oura CEO Tom Hale. “Together, we can create a new model of care that extends the current healthcare paradigm by delivering an experience that’s more immediate, personalized, and proactive.”.

Tech giant description: Founded in 1889, Lee has made its marks as one of the biggest heritage names in denim. The American brand generates an average of $1.5 billion in annual sales across 73 countries, of which almost 40% comes from outside the US and Canada. Latest York-based Authentic Brands Group has successfully acquired Lee from Kontoor Brands in an effort to expand Lee into adjacent categories, including activewear and workwear, as well as lifestyle offerings.

Funding and round: Acquisition.

Investor(s): Authentic Brands Group (portfolio includes: Guess, Juicy Couture, Reebok).

Investor comments: “We are thrilled to welcome Lee to the Authentic family,” mentioned Jamie Salter, founder and executive chair of Authentic Brands Group. “Lee has the heritage, recognition and consumer loyalty we look for in a brand. By connecting Lee to Authentic’s global platform and the right partners in key markets, we see a significant opportunity to expand its reach through content, experiences and latest product categories.”.

Organization description: Touted as London’s first functional smoothie bar, Elevate introduced at the Royal Exchange in June 2025, before opening in Selfridges in April 2026. Founded by Julia Baldet, its bestselling smoothie, The Glow, made with collagen and hyaluronic acid, has grossed close to half a million pounds since rollout. Elevate has collaborated with brands such as Nike x Skims, Adanola, Ouai and Medicube, as wellness continues to crossover into beauty and fashion. The new funding will be used to open additional London sites next year, after finishing its first full year with over £1 million in sales.

Funding and round: £2 million, seed.

Investor(s): JamJar (portfolio includes: Innocent Drinks, Deliveroo, Humantra), Active Partners (portfolio includes: Tala, Healf, Salad Project) Cassius, Soho House founder Nick Jones.

Investor comments: “Elevate’s proposition is perfect: delicious smoothies that look great while meeting real nutritional and wellness needs. It’s clearly working; loyal customers love the brand. But most of all, we’re backing Julia. She’s focused, ambitious, creative and commercial, and we’re thrilled to support her as she builds Elevate into a category-defining brand,” JamJar partner Adam Balon said in a statement.

Company description: Frasers Group has successfully taken control of Hugo Boss. Following a rejected takeover bid of €2 billion (€38 per share) in June, the British retail conglomerate has raised its stake to approximately 50.08% — an additional purchase of 198,666 shares, equating to €7.63 million, according to the stock market filing. The German fashion company will now become a subsidiary of the Mike Ashley-owned business.

It has been revealed that hugo Boss believed the June takeover proposal to be “financially inadequate”, urging its shareholders to reject. Though Frasers continued its efforts, gradually raising its holding once again to 48% in mid-August (up from 30.3% in June, alongside the initial takeover bid). Frasers Group CEO Michael Murray assumed the Hugo Boss chair position last month, after Stephan Sturm stepped down.

Investor(s): Frasers Group Luxury (portfolio includes: Flannels, The Webster, Harvey Nichols, Matches).

Company description: Frasers Group has adjusted its stake in Burberry from 7.4% to 6%. This comes after the growing British retail group raised its position in the company from 6.3% last week, after upping it from 4.2% at the end of September. This marks a potential pullback from its current luxury brand spending spree.

Investor(s): Frasers Group Luxury (portfolio includes: Flannels, The Webster, Harvey Nichols, Matches).

Company description: Frasers Group has acquired a 8.78% stake in US-based sports brand Under Armour, continuing a string of cross-category investments in recent months. Earlier this week, Frasers upped its investment in Burberry to 6.3%, having also taken on ownership of esteemed department store Harvey Nichols in August. The Frasers portfolio spans discount retailer Sports Direct through to The Webster, House of Fraser, and Flannels, as well as a strong stake in Hugo Boss — upped to 47.89% in August. Under Armour’s share price has risen since the SEC filing was made on October 1.

Investor(s): Frasers Group (portfolio includes: Harvey Nichols, Sports Direct, The Webster).

Sources indicate that company description: Frasers Group has upped its economic interest in Burberry from 4.2% to 6.3%, with the British brand now part of a new luxury division launched in early October. Also part of the luxury portfolio, Hugo Boss — of which Frasers now owns almost 48% — continues to reject the retail group’s takeover bids; it may be looking elsewhere for potential acquisitions.

Investor(s): Frasers Group (portfolio includes: Flannels, The Webster, Harvey Nichols, Sports Direct).

Industry observers note that company description: Activewear brand 437 was founded in 2016 by co-CEOs Adrien Bettio and Hyla Nayeri. Initially founded as a swimwear brand, 437 moved into activewear in 2023, which is now the core of its business. The Toronto-based brand is the top-selling activewear brand on Revolve, and has fast become a celebrity go-to.

Funding and round: $15 million CAD, minority stake.

Investor(s): Revolve (portfolio includes: Alliance Apparel, Alexandre Vauthier).

Investor comments: “437 is still a small player, but is already outselling nearly every activewear brand on our site, including billion dollar brands. The brand is great and the aesthetic and products are great — it’s really just building on their core momentum and continuing to gain awareness. Hyla and Adrien had built something very special, but had also reached a point where they needed additional capital, infrastructure, and a thought partner who had been through the same journey,” said co-founder and co-CEO Michael Karanikolas.

In a recent development, company description: Founded by former fashion executive Yasmin Sewell, Vyrao introduced in 2021 as a fragrance brand blending aromatherapy and neuroscience principles. The brand was ahead of the curve tapping into the cross-section of fragrance and wellness, by offering customers something more than just a scented mist. Following the acquisition, the genderless brand will embark on its next development phase under its latest owner.

Funding and round: Acquisition, terms undisclosed.

It has been revealed that manufacturer description: Based in LA, Arey released in 2021 under entrepreneur Allison Conrad and celebrity hairstylist Jay Small, offering vitamin, antioxidant and peptide-infused products to help delay and repigment aging hair. The funding will support Arey’s new product development, ongoing clinical research, and expansion through retail partnerships.

Funding and round: Series A, terms undisclosed.

Investor(s): Unilever Ventures (portfolio includes:), Greycroft, Female Founders Fund.

In a recent development, company description: AI-driven discovery platform Slayd debuted in Gurugram, India, in 2025. Targeted at Gen Z, the startup sorts fashion items from more than 300 marketplaces and brands by theme and curates personalized feeds that enable product discovery across multiple sites. Slayd claims to currently have more than 200,000 users, and can identify emerging trends through its proprietary tech software. The investment will help strengthen its team and accelerate the growth of its private-label business, Slayd Originals.

Funding and round: $156,400, Pre-Seed.

Investor(s): AJVC (portfolio includes: Midcase, Bubble Me, Trufides).

In a recent development, tech giant description: ISDIN is a product of pharmaceutical company Corporación Químico-Farmacéutica Esteve (CQFE) and beauty group Puig, who partnered to launch the skincare brand in 1975. Since then, both families have supported ISDIN’s evolution into a global dermatological skincare business focused on scientific formulation and innovation. In acquiring CQFE’s 50% stake, Puig will obtain complete ownership of the Spanish brand.

Funding and round: Acquisition.

Investor(s): Puig (portfolio includes: Charlotte Tilbury, Byredo, Penhaligon’s, Dr. Baraba Sturm).

Investor comments: “Expanding our presence in dermocosmetics is a strategic priority for Puig. ISDIN is a unique company, with a strong management team, a clear strategy and a distinctive position in dermatology and skincare. Full ownership will give Puig the best platform to support its next phase of growth and continue investing behind the science and innovation that have made ISDIN successful,” Puig CEO Jose Manuel Albesa said.

Industry observers note that company description: Founded in 2021, Talm (“To All the Mamas”) initially focused on bodycare products during pregnancy and postpartum, however the brand has gradually expanded to offer sensitive skincare for all stages of life. It currently offers around a dozen products, operates in roughly a dozen countries, and reports double-digit revenue growth. This marks the first acquisition for Caudalie, which intends to accelerate Talm’s global expansion and product development by leveraging its pharmacy network, sales force and infrastructure.

Funding and round: Acquisition.

Company description: Medici Brands, owner of David Protein and newly launched confectionery brand HallPass, will use its Series B funding to enter the next phase of growth. This includes expanding HallPass’s retail presence, alongside the remainder of its product portfolio — extending David into new formats and categories, advancing product innovation, and enabling the launch and scaling of new brands such as Rowdy.

Funding and round: $250 million, Series B.

Investor(s): Greenoaks (portfolio includes: Stripe, Canva, Discord, Robinhood), Valor Equity Partners (portfolio includes: GoPuff, SpaceX, BitGo), Peter Rahal, Iconiq, Imaginary Ventures.

Industry observers note that investor comments: “Two years ago, David Protein indicated customers they no longer had to choose between great macros and great taste, and it became one of the fastest-growing CPG brands in America. Now, Medici is bringing that approach to the rest of the store, building a house of brands that delivers the taste consumers adore, without making the compromises they have grown to accept,” remarked Greenoaks partner Neil Shah.

Recent findings suggest that tech giant description: Truly Beauty is a plant-based personal care brand founded in 2013 by Maxx Appelman. Known for its viral, Gen Z-focused bodycare and social media marketing, Truly Beauty combines high-performing active ingredients with a luxurious but playful aesthetic. It is headquartered in Los Angeles. For razor company Dollar Shave Club, this marks its first acquisition as it extends beyond grooming.

Funding and round: Acquisition.

Investor(s): Dollar Shave Club.

Investor comments: “By layering Truly’s fast-turn product engine onto our AI-driven inventory planning and backend logistics, we are building a high-velocity innovation model that legacy CPG conglomerates simply cannot replicate,” noted Dollar Shave Club CEO Larry Bodner.

Sources indicate that company description: Scottish-born accessible luxury leather goods brand Strathberry has closed its second funding round, consisting of a growth investment from Soho Square Capital’s newly introduced Fund II, and marking the fund’s first investment. The funding comes on the heels of a strong year for Strathberry, which delivered 39% year-on-year growth in 2026 at $50.5 million. Soho Square’s investment will support Strathberry founders Guy and Leeanne Hundleby’s ambitions to accelerate the brand’s North America expansion.

Funding and round: Undisclosed minority investment valuing the manufacturer at approximately £100 million, second funding round.

Investor(s): Soho Square Capital’s Fund II.

According to recent reports, investor comments: “Strathberry is an exceptional brand with a rare combination of craftsmanship, a distinctive design signature and a genuinely international, loyal customer base. The label’s ‘high-end quality at accessible prices’ ethos is resonating with shoppers disillusioned with top luxury houses. Guy, Leeanne, and the team have created something special, and there is significant scope to grow the business internationally,” Soho Square Capital director David Steel stated in a statement.

Firm description: Thorne, the science-backed supplements brand founded in 1984, has entered into a definitive acquisition agreement with P&G. Thorne is currently owned by L Catterton’s Flagship Fund. It is now best known in the wellness space for its creatine product, leaning into the rise of the supplement and its various formats. The acquisition helps to further Thorne’s attempt at becoming the market’s most-trusted personalized health brand, as well as P&G’s aim to move its personal health business upmarket. The transaction is expected to close later this year, subject to regulatory approval.

Investor(s): Procter & Gamble (portfolio includes: Seven Seas, Oral-B, Pepto Bismol).

Investor comments: “Consumer interest in selfcare, prevention, wellness, and personalized health continues to grow, and Thorne strengthens our position in premium wellness with a trusted, science-backed brand that complements our existing portfolio,” CEO of P&G Health Care Paul Gama noted.

According to recent reports, organization description: Frasers Group has taken a 4.2% position in British luxury brand Burberry. Frasers, the company behind House of Fraser, Sports Direct and Flannels, is holding the position through put options, which gives Frasers Group the right to buy shares at a predetermined stock price. The company is also the second largest shareholder in Mulberry PLC.

According to recent reports, frasers Group has been on an investing spree of late, increasing its stake in Hugo Boss to 30.3% and offering a takeover proposal. Frasers Group also bought Matches for £52 million in December 2023, before it announced that it was going into administration; Matches was sold in December 2025 to form part of newly established luxury group Hulcan.

Investor(s): Frasers Group (portfolio includes: House of Fraser, Flannels, Sports Direct).

Company description: Solomei AI, the company behind the Callimacus platform, has unveiled that it has entered into an agreement for an investment from Salesforce. The investment will “support Callimacus’s efforts to expand its engineering and AI research capabilities, accelerate product development, and scale commercial operations across Europe and North America.” In January 2026, Callimacus, whose chairman is Brunello Cucinelli, was used to build the latest e-commerce experience for the designer’s eponymous luxury brand.

Investor comments: “Brunello has always believed that technology should elevate humanity, and that conviction is at the heart of Callimacus,” noted Marc Benioff, chair and CEO of Salesforce. “The team has developed an innovative platform that reimagines AI-powered experiences — bringing together conversational AI, enterprise context, and real-time personalization to create entirely fresh ways for businesses to engage with their customers.”.

In a recent development, “Three years ago, Marc Benioff and I began an endeavor with mathematicians, philosophers, humanists, and technologists, from which Callimacus was born. Our idea was to create a simple, intuitive product capable of speaking the language of human beings; a sort of new web, without pages, categories, or predetermined paths, able to accompany the intent of each individual navigator. I look with great confidence and hope for the path that Callimacus will pursue with Salesforce’s investment,” Brunello Cucinelli, chairman of Solomei AI, added.

According to recent reports, tech giant description: Founded in 2021, Merit is a US-based beauty brand designed as an antidote to using multiple, trend-led products — collapsing everyday cosmetics into a curated, minimal line-up. The investment is led by Vasiliki Petrou, managing partner at Semcap Beauty & Wellness, who also founded the Unilever Prestige division in 2014, spanning Dermalogica, Paula’s Choice, Hourglass, K18, and more.

Funding and round: Undisclosed.

Investor(s): Semcap Beauty & Wellness.

Industry observers note that investor comments: “Merit is one of the most thoughtfully built brands in beauty, a true icon in the market. I love the timeless brand aesthetic, the simplified and edited approach to beauty, and the focus on the millennial and Gen X consumer, which is a significant white space in our industry. I am thrilled to support the continued global scaling of the brand,” Petrou stated in a statement.

It has been revealed that manufacturer description: Frasers Group has increased its stake in Hugo Boss to approximately 30.28% (up from 26.06%), which demands an official takeover bid in line with German legislation. The move follows Frasers’s €2 billion (€38 per share) takeover proposal in June, which Hugo Boss believed was “financially inadequate”, urging its shareholders to reject. Frasers, now Hugo Boss’s largest shareholder, said its offer still stands through July 27.

Investor(s): Frasers Group (portfolio includes: House of Fraser, Flannels, Sports Direct).

Organization description: Syntetica is a French startup that transforms textile waste into recycled nylon through a proprietary chemical method that allows the processing of fabrics containing multiple materials. The funding will help Syntetica build its first commercial facility in France, which will be able to transform hundreds of tons of post-consumer textile waste annually. While Syntetica already works with labels such as Victoria’s Secret and Etam, it also looks to scale its recycling efforts and partner with more fashion brands.

Funding and round: $30 million, Series A.

Investor(s): Ecotechnologies 2 (portfolio includes: Standing Ovation, Mantle8), Lululemon (portfolio includes: Epoch Biodesign, Samsara Eco, Zymochem), MAS Holdings (portfolio includes: Victoria’s Secret, Calvin Klein, Gap), Swen Capital Partners, EQT Ventures.

Organization description: Founded in 2021 by Abhi Arora and Sanket Agarwal, Fleek is a wholesale vintage fashion marketplace. Fleek connects retailers and resellers with verified, secondhand clothing wholesalers worldwide, enabling them to source vintage inventory in bulk through a digital marketplace with integrated logistics and quality assurance.

Funding and round: $25 million, Series B.

Investor(s): Burda Principal Investments (portfolio includes: Vinted), Ebay Ventures, FJ Labs, H14, Andreessen Horowitz, HV Capital, Y Combinator, and more.

Sources indicate that manufacturer description: Whering is a digital wardrobe and styling app founded in 2020 by Bianca Rangecroft. The app enables users to catalogue the clothes they already own, create outfits, track wardrobe usage, and receive styling recommendations, with the aim of encouraging more intentional fashion consumption and reducing unnecessary purchases.

Funding and round: $7 million, Seed.

Investor(s): Ebay Ventures, Google AI Futures Fund.

Industry observers note that firm description: Hair technology company Halo has developed its first product, HaloBraid. Launching in salons this fall, the device will be the first automated hair braiding tool that works alongside stylists to halve braiding time from as long as 10 hours per appointment. Reddit co-founder Alexis Ohanian’s VC firm Seven Seven Six is leading the investment into a business that was rolled out off the back of Yinka Ogunbiyi’s winning Harvard Innovation Labs pitch last year.

Funding and round: $7 million, Seed.

Investor(s): Seven Seven Six (portfolio includes: Anthropic, ElevenLabs, Flock Safety), Bling Capital (portfolio includes: Palantir, Gusto, Everlane), AlleyCorp (portfolio includes: ShopMy, Gilt Groupe, Business Insider).

Sources indicate that investor comments: “As an investor, I look for founders that see something broken that everyone else has accepted as fixed. Braiding is a perfect example: it is a process that has not materially changed in thousands of years, despite being one of the most popular hairstyles for millions of Americans and a significant part of the $270 billion salon services industry,” said Ohanian. “Yinka has introduced a novel technology to a traditionally manual and highly specialized professional service.”.

Company description: L’Oréal Group has taken a stake in Indian personal care company Innovist. (Vogue Business reported on speculations back in March.) The company has a successful portfolio that includes Indian haircare brand Bare Anatomy, skincare brands Chemist at Play and Sunscoop, and bodycare brand Vinci Botanicals. The company was founded in 2018 by Rohit Chawla, Sifat Khurana, and Vimal Bhola with a focus on science-first formulations, transparent ingredients, and in-house research and development.

Funding and round: Majority stake, terms undisclosed.

Investor(s): L’Oréal Group (portfolio includes: Cerave, La Roche-Posay, Vichy, Armani Beauty, SkinCeuticals).

Investor comments: “Our investment in this innovative Indian startup is a clear testament to our unwavering commitment to expanding L’Oréal’s footprint in India,” CEO Nicolas Hieronimus noted. “By bringing together the very best of L’Oréal’s global expertise with Innovist’s high-performing, science-led products and deep-rooted understanding of the Indian consumer, I believe we are poised to shape the future of beauty in this dynamic market.”.

Firm description: Remedy is a dermatologist-developed skincare brand founded by Dr. Muneeb Shah in March 2024. The brand’s products target skin concerns such as dark spots, dryness, fine lines, dullness, keratosis pilaris, and sensitive skin. Remedy is stocked on Amazon, TikTok Shop and Target, the latter of which it partnered with in December 2025. The Series A investment will support the skincare brand with its next phase of growth, including advancing clinical research, expanding its product categories, and improving inventory. Remedy also intends to strengthen its formulation, testing, and consumer education.

Funding and round: Series A, terms undisclosed.

Investor(s): L Catterton (portfolio includes: Merit Beauty, Tula, Kopari, Elemis, Nutrafol, Intercos, Ex Nihilo).

It has been revealed that investor comments: “We seek to partner with exceptional founders building brands that will redefine categories, and we believe Remedy is uniquely modernizing dermatological skincare,” L Catterton partner Tehmina Haider said. “As both a clinician and a consumer educator, Dr. Shah has built a portfolio of simple, effective, and accessibly priced products that leverage advanced ingredient technologies to address real patient needs — and that is what will define the next generation of dermocosmetics. The brand’s rapid growth reflects deep consumer demand for affordable, clinically-grounded skincare, and we are thrilled to partner with the Remedy team on its next chapter.”.

Recent findings suggest that manufacturer description: Bacchus is a London-based PR agency founded in 1998 by Anouschka Menzies and Charlotte Lurot, who right now lead the business alongside co-CEO Daize Washbourn. The agency specializes in luxury hospitality and culture, as well as in the prestige VIC and high-net-worth communities. With around 100 employees across seven offices (London, Upcoming York, Miami, LA, Dubai, Riyadh, and Doha), Bacchus generates annual sales of approximately $17 million. Its client portfolio includes Red Sea Global Residences, Six Senses, Auberge Resorts, the Victoria & Albert Museum, and Monte-Carlo Société des Bains de Mer.

Funding and round: Acquisition, majority stake.

Investor(s): Mazarine Group (portfolio includes: La Mode en Images, the show producer of Louis Vuitton, Dior, and Gucci).

Investor comments: “There were several objectives [with this investment],” Mazarine founder Paul-Emmanuel Reiffers tells Vogue Business. “First, we needed to add a public relations and influence branch to our group. Second, it had to be large enough for us to develop and accelerate it. With Bacchus, we’re starting from a platform that’s already large enough to consolidate operations, grow further, and open an office in Paris in the short to medium-term. Third, the acquisition gives us seven offices at once, providing an established global network and strengthening our geographic footprint. We already had a presence in Dubai, but now we’re able to establish ourselves in Riyadh, which is notable because the Middle East is about to rebound strongly. We’re also strengthening our position in the US by expanding our network from New York to LA and Miami, allowing us to serve clients more effectively.”.

He continues: “Finally, the acquisition aligns with what we see as the luxury sectors of tomorrow: hospitality, real estate, and longevity. As luxury brands increasingly move into these areas, we are positioning ourselves to support their expansion. It also creates valuable synergies, allowing us to integrate Bacchus’s expertise and network of personalities, influencers, and guests into our events.”.

Company description: Bella Hadid has been slowly growing her fragrance brand Orebella since its launch in 2024. Now, with Series A funding from Silas Capital, which has previously invested in beauty brands including Makeup by Mario, Oak Essentials and Ilia, she can scale the line further across categories and markets.

Funding and round: Series A, terms undisclosed.

Investor(s): Silas Capital (portfolio includes: Makeup by Mario, YSE Beauty, Dôen).

Recent findings suggest that manufacturer description: NYC-based startup Vetir is pitching itself as an AI luxury shopping app that goes beyond discovery and transactions to act as “a system of record for the wardrobe” for high-value consumers. In practice, this is something of an AI stylist that learns from the data users share with the app, including existing closet items, shopping preferences, as well as their calendar, travel, and purchasing behavior. It’s also building out a business-to-business, CRM-type system for private stylists and luxury clienteling systems, aiming to bring “structure and continuity to what has traditionally been a fragmented, relationship-driven space”.

Funding and round: $5.5 million, Series A.

Investor(s): A consortium of investors across technology and luxury-adjacent family offices.

Recent findings suggest that company description: Ruka Hair was founded in 2021 by Tendai Moyo and Ugo Agbai, with the mission of supplying hair extensions that are safe, ethical, and good quality. The brand has now received $4.5 million in funding led by Henkel Ventures, the owner of Olaplex and Schwarzkopf. Ruka will be using the investment to scale its business, starting with the launch of US-based operations later this year. The brand has raised $10 million to date and is stocked at Selfridges.

Funding and round: $4.5 million.

Investor(s): Henkel Ventures, Freedom Trail Capital, Big Issue Invest, Backed VC, Dina Asher-Smith, Knut Alicke, Sophia Dennis, Didier Morais.

According to recent reports, investor comments: “Ruka Hair exemplifies what we look for: founders solving a real problem with genuine commitment, building through community rather than hype,” mentioned Samyr Laine, co-founder and managing partner of Freedom Trail Capital. “Tendai and Ugo built this brand during one of the most challenging periods for consumer businesses, scaled through an authentic community, and are now pioneering biotech innovation that could reshape an entire category.”.

Sources indicate that manufacturer description: Since founding Anomaly in 2021, Priyanka Chopra Jonas has scaled her haircare brand across North America, the UK, and the Middle East. In the US, the brand is stocked at Target, while in the UK, Superdrug is one of its biggest retailers. Chopra Jonas rolled out Anomaly with the aim to bring accessibly priced clean and vegan haircare products to the masses. The investment from Reliance will focus on scaling the brand further in India, alongside growing its international presence.

Funding and round: Acquisition, terms undisclosed.

Investor(s): Reliance Retail (portfolio includes: Pahadi Local and Tira).

Recent findings suggest that investor comments: “Bringing Anomaly into our portfolio marks a strategic step in expanding our basket of latest-age, high-growth beauty brands. Anomaly’s strong global positioning, clean formulation, and accessible pricing make it a compelling addition to our ecosystem,” noted Isha Ambani, executive director of Reliance Retail Ventures Limited.

According to recent reports, company description: Luxury skincare brand 111Skin was co-founded by husband and wife duo, Dr. Yannis and Eva Alexandridis, in 2012. Their face masks have gone viral since, and in 2025, the brand received a minority investment from Kim Kardashian and Jay Sammons’s private equity firm Skky Partners to help fund its US expansion. Now, the Estée Lauder Companies (ELC) has invested a minority stake that will go toward science-driven innovation.

Funding and round: Minority investment, terms undisclosed.

Investor(s): The Estée Lauder Companies (portfolio includes: Le Labo, Jo Malone London, Clinique, La Mer).

Sources indicate that investor comments: “Skincare is entering a new phase, shaped by the convergence of procedures, longevity, and beauty, as consumers increasingly seek products that deliver visible, treatment-inspired results,” mentioned ELC president and CEO Stéphane de La Faverie. “111Skin exemplifies this shift, translating Dr. Alexandrides’s more than 35 years of surgical and aesthetic treatment experience into high-performance skincare inspired by in-clinic treatments and built on clinical insight, next-generation actives, powerful formulas, and proven efficacy.”.

Recent findings suggest that company description: ICCF is a Shanghai and Paris-based premium fashion group that owns Chinese brand Icicle and French brand Carven (acquired in 2018). Kering has acquired a minority stake in ICCF to help develop the former label as part of Kering’s latest House of Wonders initiative, which aims to build partnerships that equip emerging luxury houses with strong cultural relevance across markets, categories, and geographies. Icicle will use the funds to expand internationally and into new product categories.

Funding and round: Minority acquisition, terms undisclosed.

Investor(s): Kering (portfolio includes: Gucci, Saint Laurent, Bottega Veneta).

Investor comments: “This partnership brings together ICCF’s deep understanding of the Chinese luxury ecosystem and cultural landscape with Kering’s longstanding expertise in craftsmanship, operations, and brand development in Europe,” Kering noted in a statement. “Through House of Wonders, Kering aims to build long-term value through a disciplined, partnership-driven approach, engaging with brands defined by a distinctive vision, deep authenticity, and global resonance potential.”.

Icicle FW26. Photo: Benjamin Cremel/Getty Images.

Industry observers note that firm description: Grüns is a US-based supplement brand founded in 2023 by Chad Janis, best known for its greens superfood gummy supplement. The brand is digitally-native, with a strong community and a mixed distributed network across retail and direct-to-consumer. The acquisition signals Unilever’s push into the premium wellness category.

Funding and round: Acquisition, terms undisclosed.

Investor(s): Unilever (portfolio includes: Liquid I.V., Dermalogica, Paula’s Choice).

Investor comments: “As a leader and true innovator in the greens supplement category, what sets Grüns apart is its focused portfolio of science-backed products that people genuinely enjoy, trust, and consistently use,” Jostein Solheim, Unilever Wellbeing CEO, said. “This combination of efficacy and experience is powerful, and together we see a significant opportunity to scale the brand within our wellbeing business.”.

Funding and round: $122 billion.

It has been revealed that investor(s): Softbank, Andreessen Horowitz, D. E. Shaw Ventures, MGX, TPG, Amazon, Nvidia, Microsoft, BlackRock, Sequoia Capital, and more.

Company description: Whoop is a wearable tech company known for its fitness tracker that analyzes sleep, recovery, and performance. The company has raised $575 million at a $10.1 billion valuation, and aims to invest the funds into expanding globally, particularly in the US, Europe, the Gulf region, Latin America, and Asia.

Funding and round: $575 million, Series G.

Investor(s): Collaborative Fund (portfolio includes: Reddit, Lyft, TaskRabbit), 2PointZero Group, Qatar Investment Authority (QIA), Mubadala Investment Company, Abbott, Mayo Clinic, Cristiano Ronaldo, LeBron James, Rory McIlroy, Niall Horan.

Investor comments: “Whoop has become one of the most key tools I use to support my long-term health,” stated Ronaldo in a statement. “I am proud to participate in this round because I believe in the future we are building together. No other firm has created a health platform this powerful that people are proud to wear.”.

It has been revealed that tech giant description: Enkei is a Stockholm-based circular material startup founded by CEO Lovisa Sunnerholm (ex-Google and Electrolux) and creative director Miriam Bichsel (a former fashion PR who worked with Hermès and Bottega Veneta). The company has developed ReCeramix™, a circular material made from 90% construction and demolition waste that can be used for architectural surfaces and interior applications, replacing concrete, marble, and terrazzo. With the pre-seed funding, the company will invest in research and development and commercialization opportunities.

Funding and round: €3 million, pre-seed.

Investor(s): Redcap Ventures (portfolio includes: Done, Goodfeed, Eatit), Danish architect Anders Lendager, Lendager Group founder Christina Åqvist, Vinning co-founder and former Tarkett CEO Ulf Mattsson, retail exec Fabian Månsson, bio-materials professor Thomas Granfeldt, materials scientist Daniel Strömberg.

It has been revealed that investor comments: “What Enkei has done in less than two years is what the industry has been talking about for decades. The future of architecture depends on how we rethink materials. Solutions that transform waste into high-value building materials are exactly what the construction industry needs if we want to move toward truly circular buildings,” mentioned Lendager.

It has been revealed that company description: Olaplex was founded in 2014 as a salon-first prestige haircare brand. Slowly becoming the poster child for bond-building hair products, Olaplex has spent recent years navigating slowing sales, as well as legal and consumer scrutiny — including a 2023 lawsuit (which has since been dismissed and disputed) alleging a link between its products and hair loss, scalp irritation, and brittle strands.

Funding and round: Acquisition, $1.4 billion.

Tech giant description: Former professional snowboarder Nima Jalali founded Salt & Stone, a Los Angeles-based premium body care in 2017. The brand has rapidly grown with its minimal packaging and products ranging from deodorants, body wash and oils to facial cleansers and candles. Salt & Stone’s distribution is a growing one as it counts Sephora, Healf, Amazon and Space NK as retail partners. Vogue Business first reported the possibility of a Salt & Stone acquisition back in January.

Funding and round: Majority stake, terms undisclosed.

Investor comments: “We are thrilled for the opportunity to partner with Salt & Stone, a truly exceptional brand that stands apart in the premium body care and wellness space for its ability to blend experience, performance, and a compelling brand aesthetic,” remarked ​​David Paresky, a director at Advent. “Nima and the Salt & Stone team have built something rare – a brand with deep consumer loyalty, outstanding products, and an authentic purpose that resonates with today’s consumer all around the world.”.

In a recent development, salt & Stone. Photo: Courtesy of Salt & Stone.

In a recent development, company description: Huel was founded in 2015 by British entrepreneur Julian Hearn and nutritionist James Collier. Known for its nutritionally complete plant-based meal replacement shakes, Huel hopes to use the investment to expand its position in the competitive supplements category.

Funding and round: Acquisition, €1 billion.

Investor(s): Dandone (portfolio includes: Alpro, Activia, Evian).

Investor comments: “Combining [Huel’s] range and best-in-class digital capabilities with Danone’s global reach and deep nutritional expertise offers exciting opportunities into the fresh and fast-growing nutritionally complete space, in line with our Renew Danone strategy,” stated Dandone CEO Antoine de Saint-Affrique in a statement. “We look forward to learning from one another and unlocking new opportunities and growth for both businesses.”.

Organization description: Founded in 2020 by Karlee Zhang and Omer Ozener, Hello Klean is a water filtration brand known for its detachable shower heads. The company generated $14.7 million in revenue in 2025, and is projecting $27 million for 2026. Water filter manufacturer Brita has invested a minority investment, with the option to purchase a majority stake over time. Hello Klean looks to use the funds for further product development.

Funding and round: Minority stake, terms undisclosed.

Investor(s): Brita (portfolio includes: Brita, Vivreau, Larq).

Company description: Saks Global has received approval of its five-year business plan by an ad hoc group of the Company’s senior secured bondholders, and has secured access to an additional $300 million of its $1.75 billion in committed capital accordingly. This will provide the company with sufficient liquidity to continue to support operations.

Funding and round: Saks has secured access to an additional $300 million of its $1.75 billion in committed capital.

Firm description: Quince, the direct-to-consumer brand that bills itself as a high-quality, accessible alternative for fashion and beyond, has announced a $500 million funding round, resulting in a post-money valuation of $10.1 billion. The funding will support the continued growth and global expansion of Quince’s manufacturer-to-consumer (M2C) operating system, per the release.

Funding and round: $500 million, Series E.

Investor(s): ICONIQ (portfolio includes: Oura, Uber, Warby Parker, Zoom), with participation from Baillie Gifford, Basis Set Ventures, DST Global, Marcy Venture Partners, Notable Capital, Wellington Management and WndrCo.

According to recent reports, investor comments: “Quince has built hyperefficient infrastructure that enables it to deliver unmatched value to consumers at scale and, in turn, has built a brand people love,” Yoonkee Sull, general partner at ICONIQ, said in a statement. “By redesigning how premium products are manufactured and delivered, compressing traditional retail cycle times and reducing waste, and building a deep understanding of what customers want in real-time, the company is correcting structural inefficiencies that have long defined retail economics. We are excited to triple down in Quince following a year of strong execution by the team and believe the platform is positioned for durable, long-term growth.”.

Sources indicate that organization description: Estée Lauder Companies (ELC) has taken full ownership of Forest Essentials, the cosmetics, skincare, and fragrance brand known for its ayurvedic products. The beauty giant took out a minority stake in 2008, before increasing its investment in 2020 to 49%. It marks the first M&A move made by ELC CEO Stéphane de La Faverie, with a full takeover of Forest Essentials expected to close in the second half of 2026.

Funding and round: Acquisition, terms undisclosed.

Investor(s): Estée Lauder Companies (portfolio includes: Jo Malone London, Le Labo, Tom Ford Beauty, and more).

Industry observers note that investor comments: “Today marks a meaningful new chapter in a partnership built over the past 18 years on a foundation of mutual trust and respect. Forest Essentials is an exceptional brand, beloved in India, and created and nurtured by its founder Mira Kulkarni,” stated de La Faverie. “We are honored to strengthen our partnership with Mira, who, like Mrs. Estée Lauder, has elevated the prestige beauty industry through a clear vision of authenticity and purpose.”.

Photo: Courtesy of Forest Essentials.

Recent findings suggest that firm description: MA+Group was founded in 1999 by brothers Massimiliano and Michelangelo Di Battista in 1999 as an artist management agency, which has since expanded with a production arm. The group has now joined The Independents group of agencies to offer its services on a broader geographical scale and to a wider network of clients, the company said.

Funding and round: Acquisition, terms undisclosed.

Investor(s): The Independents (portfolio includes: Karla Otto, Lucien Pagès, Lefty).

In a recent development, investor comments: “[MA+Group’s] distinctive portfolio with expertise across artist management, strategy, visual communication and content production creates immediate and natural synergies within The Independents,” remarked The Independents co-founder and CEO Isabelle Chouvet. “As demand grows for new content and entertainment formats, we are excited to expand our capabilities across artist management and content production, bringing even greater creativity and depth to our integrated global offering.”.

Recent findings suggest that organization description: Sleep tech company Eight Sleep, known for its temperature-controlling mattresses covers, is now valued at $1.5 billion after a $50 million round led by Tether Ventures. Now, the company plans to invest the capital in scaling R&D to accelerate predictive model development, expanding clinical trials and regulatory pathways, and deepening global commercial partnerships.

Funding and round: $50 million, strategic round.

Investor(s): Tether Ventures (portfolio includes: Bitdeer, Rumble, Sorted).

Investor comments: “Eight Sleep has the potential to define the future of health tech by building intelligence that learns, scales, and evolves directly with humankind, turning advanced AI into practical, everyday insights and enhancements about core human biology,” said Paolo Ardoino, CEO of Tether. “By helping people better understand sleep, recovery, and long-term health, Eight Sleep is laying the groundwork for a fresh standard in longevity-focused technology that is truly personalized, can function in any condition, directly on-device, resilient, and aligned with how people live.”.

According to recent reports, tech giant description: RAS Luxury Skincare is a premium direct-to-consumer beauty and skincare brand based in India. The brand looks to use its latest funding round to expand its omnichannel presence, grow its team and invest in R&D. It follows a $5 million Series A round led by Unilever Ventures in 2025.

Funding and round: $7.5 million, Series B.

Investor(s): Dabur Ventures, Unilever Ventures.

Industry observers note that investor comments: “RAS offers a distinct skincare value proposition at the confluence of nature, science and luxury,” said Abhinav Dhall, Dabur India executive director and group head corporate strategy. “We believe that the premium beauty segment will witness strong growth in the coming decade and RAS Beauty is well-positioned to capture the emerging opportunity.”.

Company description: Glo Skin Beauty is an American skincare brand known for its clinical-grade products, which are formulated for sensitive and post-surgical procedure skin, targeted at the Gen X demographic. The brand has been acquired by consumer-focused investment firm KYT Group, which aims to grow the brand’s geographical and distribution footprint. As part of the deal KYT’s co-founder and managing partner Kurt Kober will become Glo Skin Beauty’s CEO.

Funding and round: Acquisition, terms undisclosed.

Investor(s): KYT Group (portfolio includes: Haus Labs, The Honest Organization, Charlotte Tilbury).

It has been revealed that investor comments: “We see Glo as a brand with strong foundations and meaningful opportunity ahead,” said Kurt Kober, co-founder and managing partner of KYT Group and incoming CEO of Glo Skin Beauty. “Glo already has deep professional credibility and a loyal following. Our focus is to sharpen those strengths, invest behind the categories where we have real authority, and build disciplined, sustainable growth. We believe professional expertise will define the next chapter of beauty.”.

Company description: Founded in 1961, Fred Segal is known for its Californian aesthetic and Melrose Avenue flagship boutique, which has been referenced in pop culture by Beverly Hills, 90210, Clueless and more. Canada-based womenswear brand Aritzia has acquired Fred Segal for an undisclosed sum.

Funding and round: Acquisition, terms undisclosed.

According to recent reports, investor comments: “Fred Segal has long been a cultural touchstone in Los Angeles — a place where creativity, community, and style converge,” remarked Jennifer Wong, CEO of Aritzia. “We are honored to steward and evolve this iconic brand for a new generation, with the elevated experience and everyday luxury that define Aritzia.”.

Firm description: Project Lobster is a Spanish eyewear brand known for its accessibly priced modern designs. The brand has been acquired by Amsterdam-based eyewear brand Ace & Tate, in a bid for the latter to expand its footprint in Spain.

Funding and round: Acquisition, terms undisclosed.

Investor comments: “Spain is an crucial next step in our European growth,” says Ace & Tate CEO Lex van de Vliet. “This acquisition adds strong local teams and well-performing stores, aligned with our approach to thoughtful design and expert eyecare.”.

According to recent reports, tech giant description: Caruso is an Italian menswear manufacturer, which has been owned by Lanvin since 2021. Lanvin had been building up its investment in the company for many years, acquiring a 35% stake in 2013 and becoming a majority shareholder in 2017. Now, Lanvin has sold Caruso to Mondevita, the luxury division of UAE-based Mondevo Group, a company that integrates private wealth management, technology ventures, and luxury investments for global family offices.

Funding and round: Acquisition, terms undisclosed.

Investor(s): Mondevo Group (portfolio includes: Meight, Ittikar).

It has been revealed that company description: Cambridge-based startup Sparxell develops plant-based colorant technologies. By transforming cellulose from materials such as wood pulp and agricultural waste into vibrant biodegradable pigments, Sparxell allows brands to dye fabrics without using fossil-based or synthetic chemicals. The company joined LVMH’s La Maison des Startups accelerator program in 2023, having since worked with brands including Louis Vuitton, Dior, and Loewe. It previously received a €1.9 million grant from the European Innovation Council, and prepares to use the new Pre-Series A funding to transition from pilot to commercial-scale manufacturing.

Funding and round: $5 million, Pre-Series A.

Investor(s): Swen Capital Partners’s Blue Ocean 2 fund (portfolio includes: NextProtein, Traceless, Avant), Alpha Star Capital, and Cambridge Enterprise.

Investor comments: “By reinventing color through a bio-based, biodegradable approach, Sparxell offers a tangible response to a major environmental challenge, while enabling global industries to transition toward safer and more sustainable practices,” stated Mélanie Le Guen, investment director of Blue Ocean strategy. “We are delighted to accompany them in this next phase of growth.”.

Firm description: Veradermics is a biopharmaceutical company that develops solutions for aesthetic and dermatological conditions, including hair loss. The company announced its initial public offering of more than 15 million shares of its common stock — at an initial public offering price of $17.00 per share — raising $256 million.

Tech giant description: Colorescience is a suncare brand best known for its mineral-based powder sunscreen and SPF makeup. It was founded by beauty entrepreneur Diane Ranger in 2000, and has been acquired by private equity firm Roundtable Healthcare Partners from a group of shareholders led by 1315 Capital. The acquisition will see Colorescience continue to carve out its brand, while capitalizing on current momentum.

Funding and round: Acquisition, terms undisclosed.

Investor(s): Roundtable Healthcare Partners (portfolio includes: Polymedco, Everwell Health).

Investor comments: “Colorescience has built a compelling platform defined by strong consumer advocacy and a differentiated product portfolio anchored by a commitment to science and innovation,” said Tim Connors, managing partner of Roundtable and chair of the Colorescience board.

Sources indicate that manufacturer description: Lobby PR is a London-based communications agency founded by Ashley Smith. The agency is joining the newly formed CultureComm Group, founded by Paul Knipe, who released communications agency Kinc, which is also joining the group. The group aims to “build a connected, culturally fluent group of specialist, founder-led agencies”.

Funding and round: Acquisition, terms undisclosed.

Investor(s): CultureComm Group.

Recent findings suggest that investor comments: “We are playing at the opposite end of the spectrum to the massive [holding company] model. Our structure talks to brands that recognize that cultural proximity and operational depth are best delivered by passionate and knowledgeable agency founders and their teams,” mentioned Knipe.

Manufacturer description: Flock AI is a visual commerce platform that allows fashion brands and retailers to generate product imagery on digital models without requiring a traditional photoshoot. The startup’s $6 million Seed round brings its total funding to $7.5 million.

Funding and round: $6 million, Seed.

Investor(s): Work-Bench (portfolio includes: Spring Health, Cockroach Labs, Goodfire), Red Bike Capital, January Ventures, Outlander VC, AI Furnace.

Investor comments: “Flock is redefining how brands create content and how customers experience it. The team brings deep expertise in the space, solving a problem that sits directly on the path to revenue and brand trust. Across diligence, large retailers were clear: Flock delivers what other AI tools couldn’t. We believe Flock is becoming the content infrastructure for modern commerce,” remarked Jonathan Lehr, co-founder and general partner at Work-Bench.

Company description: Founded by Phoebe Gates and Sophia Gianni, Phia is an AI-driven shopping agent, which helps users research and track down the best price for a product across retailers, including secondhand platforms. The app and mobile browser extension launched in April 2025, before announcing an $8 million seed funding round in September. This series A investment will help Phia develop its understanding of consumer “intent, taste and trust in real time”, as the AI goalposts continue to shift.

Funding and round: $35 million, series A.

Investor(s): Notable Capital (portfolio includes: Quince, Anthropic, RedNote), Khosla Ventures, Kleiner Perkins.

Industry observers note that investor comments: “Historically, shopping was built for an internet of pages and filters, not one mediated by agents. Now, AI sits between people and products, and the challenge is no longer access. It is understanding intent, taste and trust in real time. Phia is building an intelligence layer for that shift,” noted Hans Tung, managing partner at Notable Capital.

It has been revealed that manufacturer description: Chinese sportswear giant Anta Sports has acquired a 29% stake in German sports brand Puma from Groupe Artémis, the Pinault family’s holding company, which is facing pressure as its largest asset, Kering, struggles amid a market slowdown. The stake is worth approximately $1.8 billion, paid in cash. The acquisition makes Anta Sports — which is in the process of executing a globalization strategy — the largest shareholder of Puma. The transaction is expected to close by the end of 2026.

Funding and round: 29% stake, worth approximately $1.8 billion.

Investor(s): Anta Sports (portfolio includes: Anta, Fila, Kolon Sport).

Investor comments: “We believe Puma’s share price over the past few months does not fully reflect the long-term potential of the brand,” said Anta Sports chair Ding Shizhong. “We have confidence in its management team and strategic transformation, and look forward to supporting the brand’s ongoing revival.”.

Company description: Statusphere is an AI software platform that helps brands connect with micro-influencers for product marketing plays. The platform will use the funding to expand its social SEO, reporting and AI optimization capabilities to improve search for brands looking to partner with content creators.

Funding and round: $18 million, series A.

Investor(s): Volition Capital (portfolio includes: Chamberlain Coffee, Chewy, Burst), HearstLab, 1984 Ventures and How Women Invest.

Industry observers note that investor comments: “Statusphere is creating infrastructure that addresses a fundamental shift in how consumers discover and trust brands. The tech giant’s rapid growth over the past year reflects strong market adoption, and we’re excited to partner with the Statusphere team as they build the future of marketing,” stated Larry Cheng, managing partner and co-founder at Volition Capital.

Recent findings suggest that company description: Ex Nihilo is a Paris-based perfumery house founded in 2013, best known for its niche scents and personalized fragrance services. Global investment group Eurazeo made a significant minority investment of around €25 million in January 2024, which it has agreed to sell to L Catterton at more than 2.5x the initial investment.

Funding and round: More than €62.5 million, minority acquisition.

Investor(s): L Catterton (portfolio includes: Equinox, Function of Beauty, Merit).

According to recent reports, company description: Jacobson Group is a family-founded British footwear company with a portfolio of brands including Gola, Lotus, Ravel and Frank Wright, along with the licenses for sports brands Dunlop and Lonsdale. The group has been acquired by Japanese investment conglomerate Marubeni Corporation’s fresh consumer-focused investment platform, Marubeni Consumer Platform US (MCPU), which will integrate Jacobson into its lifestyle platform, RGB.

Funding and round: Acquisition, terms undisclosed.

Investor(s): Marubeni Consumer Platform US.

Industry observers note that investor comments: “The acquisition of Jacobson Group advances the platform architecture we’ve been building, and comes at a particularly exciting time, fueled by Gola’s rapidly expanding market resonance. This marks a defining step in establishing the MCPU lifestyle platform as a scalable, multi-brand ecosystem,” noted MCPU president Shana Randhava.

Firm description: Coty has sold its remaining 25.8% stake in haircare company Wella to investment firm KKR. Under the terms of the transaction, Coty will receive an upfront cash consideration of $750 million, as well as 45% of further sale proceeds or an initial public offering of the business, once KKR’s preferred return has been met.

Funding and round: Acquisition of remaining 25.8% stake.

Investor(s): KKR (portfolio includes: Bytedance, Sonos, GoDaddy).

Investor comments: “This transaction marks a pivotal milestone for Coty — both in our transformation and in our long-running deleveraging commitment,” mentioned Coty CFO Laurent Mercier. “Our strategic partnership with KKR has proven highly value accretive. We have benefited from Wella’s strong growth by progressively monetizing our stake, allowing us to strengthen Coty’s financial foundations year after year.”.

Tech giant description: Kering has revealed a staged acquisition of jewelry manufacturer Raselli Franco Group, starting with an initial 20% stake worth €115 million and ending with a pathway to full ownership by 2032. The luxury conglomerate noted that its jewelry houses — Boucheron, Pomellato, Dodo and Qeelin — are experiencing strong momentum and revenue resilience, so the acquisition strengthens the group’s production capabilities while signaling CEO Luca de Meo’s ambitions for the category. Raselli Franco was founded in 1969 and is known for its expertise across the value chain, from raw materials sourcing and precious stones to R&D and quality control.

Funding and round: 20% stake worth €115 million, with a pathway to full ownership by 2032.

Investor(s): Kering (portfolio includes: Boucheron, Pomellato, Qeelin).

Investor comments: “This acquisition marks a strategic milestone for Kering, embodying our ambition in jewelry,” said de Meo. “Raselli Franco Group brings exceptional savoir faire and innovation, anchored in a rich heritage and a strong commitment to sustainability. By securing critical manufacturing capabilities for our jewelry activity, this partnership will strengthen our value chain and accelerate the growth of our houses.”.

Sources indicate that salma Hayek — who is married to Kering chair François-Henri Pinault — in a Boucheron necklace at the 2025 LACMA Art + Film Gala. Photo: Gilbert Flores/Variety via Getty Images.

Tech giant description: Etro’s founding family is exiting the business after selling their minority stake to Rams Global, Mathias Facchini (head of Swinger International and owner of the Genny brand) and SRI Group. L Catterton will remain the majority shareholder.

Funding and round: Minority stake, terms undisclosed.

Investor(s): Rams Global, Mathias Facchini, SRI Group.

Etro Spring/Summer 2026. Photo: Victor VIRGILE/Gamma-Rapho via Getty Images.

Tech giant description: YSE Beauty is a skincare brand designed for women aged 35 and above, inspired by founder Molly Sim’s battle with hyperpigmentation. In 2025, YSE Beauty experienced 120% revenue growth and expects to deliver more than 80% in 2026. The funding will be used to support the brand’s e-commerce operations, while helping to rapidly scale its wholesale expansion with Sephora.

Funding and round: $15 million, series A.

Investor(s): Silas Capital (portfolio includes: Ilia Beauty, Makeup By Mario, Violette_FR), L Catterton, Willow Growth Partners, Halogen Ventures.

Industry observers note that investor comments: “Molly’s approachable yet authoritative voice has been a key driver in building the loyal and engaged community supporting the incredible momentum for YSE Beauty,” said Silas Capital partner Brian Thorne. “Leveraging her insider network of dermatologists, estheticians and makeup artists, she has curated a line of multi-functional skincare-meets-makeup essentials that cater to an underserved Gen X customer.”.

Molly Sim. Photo: Courtesy of YSE Beauty.

Company description: Supercircle is a reverse logistics platform that helps fashion brands — including Guess, Reformation and J.Crew — implement textile recycling programs and move toward a circular economy. The platform will use the funding to expand its AI-powered operating system, grow its processing and reverse logistics footprint, improve its data systems and support the onboarding of more brands and retailers.

Funding and round: $24 million, Series A.

Investor(s): Foundry (portfolio includes: Loop, Pilot, Whoop), BBG Ventures, Renewal Fund, Elemental Impact.

Recent findings suggest that investor comments: “Supercircle is giving retailers unprecedented visibility and control at the end-of-life stage, an area historically dominated by opaque, low-value liquidation,” said Foundry partner Jaclyn Hester. “Their platform is the new industry standard for waste management infrastructure, delivering regulatory readiness, measurable impact and profitable financial outcomes.”.

Sources indicate that organization description: Pharmaceutical brand Galderma was created in 1981 through a joint venture between L’Oréal and Nestlé specializing in dermatological treatments and over-the-counter or prescription skincare. The company manufactures injectable aesthetics treatments including Dysport, a Botox competitor. In 2014, L’Oréal sold all of its shares to Nestlé resulting in the launch of Nestlé Skin Health. In 2024, L’Oréal returned to acquire a 10% stake in the business.

Funding and round: Doubling stake to 20%, terms undisclosed.

Investor(s): L’Oréal Group (portfolio includes: Kiehl’s, Lancôme, Aesop).

According to recent reports, investor comments: “Aesthetics is a key adjacency to our core beauty business that we are keen to continue to explore. Our initial strategic investment made in 2024 in Galderma has proven very successful, and therefore we are eager to solidify and extend the partnership further,” said L’Oréal CEO Nicolas Hieronimus.

Manufacturer description: Launched in 2010, Tissa Fontaneda is a Spanish leather goods brand known for its signature bubble leather. The company has unveiled its first-ever external capital raise from Spanish legal and accounting consultant Daniel Codes Llamas, who also joins as CEO, bringing his knowledge of financial structuring, scalability and professional management. The company will use the funding to accelerate international expansion, digital development and positioning in key markets including North America, Japan, the Middle East and the DACH region (Germany, Austria and Switzerland).

Funding and round: Minority investment, terms undisclosed.

Investor(s): Daniel Codes Llamas.

Investor comments: “This new stage doesn’t change the soul of Tissa Fontaneda, it enhances it,” remarked Tissa Fontaneda CEO Daniel Codes Llamas. “The combination of Tissa’s artistic sensitivity and a modern management approach will allow us to bring the emotive experience of Tissa Fontaneda luxury products to new audiences while keeping its authenticity intact.”.

Photo: Courtesy of Tissa Fontaneda.

Sources indicate that company description: Supercircle is a reverse logistics platform that helps fashion brands — including Guess, Reformation and J.Crew — implement textile recycling programs and move toward a circular economy. The platform will use the funding to expand its AI-powered operating system, grow its processing and reverse logistics footprint, improve its data systems and support the onboarding of more brands and retailers.

Funding and round: $24 million, Series A.

Investor(s): Foundry (portfolio includes: Loop, Pilot, Whoop), BBG Ventures, Renewal Fund, Elemental Impact.

According to recent reports, investor comments: “Supercircle is giving retailers unprecedented visibility and control at the end-of-life stage, an area historically dominated by opaque, low-value liquidation,” said Foundry partner Jaclyn Hester. “Their platform is the fresh industry standard for waste management infrastructure, delivering regulatory readiness, measurable impact and profitable financial outcomes.”.

The company manufactures injectable aesthetics treatments including Dysport, a Botox competitor. In 2014, L’Oréal sold all of its shares to Nestlé resulting in the launch of Nestlé Skin Health. In 2024, L’Oréal returned to acquire a 10% stake in the business.

Funding and round: Doubling stake to 20%, terms undisclosed.

Investor(s): L’Oréal Group (portfolio includes: Kiehl’s, Lancôme, Aesop).

Recent findings suggest that investor comments: “Aesthetics is a key adjacency to our core beauty business that we are keen to continue to explore. Our initial strategic investment made in 2024 in Galderma has proven very successful, and therefore we are eager to solidify and extend the partnership further,” mentioned L’Oréal CEO Nicolas Hieronimus.

In a recent development, manufacturer description: Rolled out in 2010, Tissa Fontaneda is a Spanish leather goods brand known for its signature bubble leather. The company has announced its first-ever external capital raise from Spanish legal and accounting consultant Daniel Codes Llamas, who also joins as CEO, bringing his knowledge of financial structuring, scalability and professional management. The company will use the funding to accelerate international expansion, digital development and positioning in key markets including North America, Japan, the Middle East and the DACH region (Germany, Austria and Switzerland).

Funding and round: Minority investment, terms undisclosed.

Investor(s): Daniel Codes Llamas.

According to recent reports, investor comments: “This new stage doesn’t change the soul of Tissa Fontaneda, it enhances it,” mentioned Tissa Fontaneda CEO Daniel Codes Llamas. “The combination of Tissa’s artistic sensitivity and a modern management approach will allow us to bring the emotive experience of Tissa Fontaneda luxury products to new audiences while keeping its authenticity intact.”.

Tech giant description: Borland is a Chinese jewelry house known for its 24-karat gold designs rooted in imperial-era craftsmanship. In China, gold brands are surging, thanks to attention from young shoppers looking for exciting designs, cultural symbolism and assets they deem valuable. Kering’s investment from its venture arm also signals the importance of China within its new strategy.

Funding and round: Minority stake, terms undisclosed.

Investor(s): Kering Ventures (portfolio includes: Vestiaire Collective, Vitrolabs).

Company description: BDK Parfums is a French fragrance brand known for its niche scents. Its fragrances are inspired by traditional French perfumery, but transposed for the contemporary era. The buzzy brand’s sales are up 45% this year compared to 2024 and prepares to invest the funds into growing its digital platform.

Funding and round: Minority stake, terms undisclosed.

Investor(s): LVMH Luxury Ventures (portfolio includes: Our Legacy, Lyst, Aimé Leon Dore).

Investor comments: “We are delighted to support BDK Parfums, whose high-quality compositions we hold in high regard, in its new phase of development, particularly internationally,” remarked Julie Bercovy, CEO of LVMH Luxury Ventures Advisors. “We are confident that the brand, led by David, will continue to maintain its unique know-how and expertize, and continue to create distinctive new fragrances that stir powerful emotions.”.

Company description: Founded in 2019 by Alexa Suter, Huha is a women’s intimates brand. Based in Vancouver, the label is known for its Mineral Undies line, which combines Tencel and Smartcel with antimicrobial zinc-oxide liners. Huha will use the investment to further product innovation and expansion into latest markets.

Funding and round: $20 million.

Investor(s): District Ventures Capital (portfolio includes: Chickapea, Symbodi, Balzac’s Coffee Roasters).

Industry observers note that investor comments: “Alexa has developed a brand that resonates with consumers by creating underwear for modern health and comfort,” mentioned Arlene Dickinson, founder and general partner of District Ventures Capital. “We see tremendous potential in her vision and impressive momentum, and we are thrilled to partner on and support the next chapter.”.

Company description: Perelel is a doctor-founded, research-backed women’s supplement business. Debuted in 2020, it was set up by Victoria Thain Gioia, Alex Taylor and obstetrician gynecologist Banafsheh Bayati. The brand’s supplements aim to support women across every stage of their hormonal journey, from fertility and pregnancy, to postpartum and perimenopause. Perelel will use the funding to accelerate innovation, invest in clinical research and expand its product offerings to continue building a comprehensive women’s health platform.

Funding and round: $27 million, growth round.

Investor(s): Prelude Growth Partners (portfolio includes: Sol de Janeiro, Summer Fridays, Tower 28, Westman Atelier), Unilever Ventures, Willow Growth Partners, Selva Ventures.

Industry observers note that investor comments: “Perelel’s doctor founding, coupled with its clinical validation and commitment to women’s health research, stands out in the category. We are extremely proud to partner with the team and support them in creating a powerhouse brand that is reimagining the future of women’s health,” said Neda Daneshzadeh, co-founder and managing partner of Prelude Growth Partners.

Tech giant description: Lan is a Chinese skincare brand founded in 2019. Known for its bestselling facial oils, it was one of the earliest clean beauty lines in the Chinese market. L’Oréal Group has made a minority investment in the brand through its Bold venture capital arm.

Funding and round: Minority stake, terms undisclosed.

Investor(s): L’Oréal Bold Ventures (portfolio includes: Borntostandout, Replika, Ami Colé).

Investor comments: “We firmly believe investing in China is investing in the future, and we will continue to cultivate the Chinese market, work with more Chinese brands to create a beautiful future and meet the expectations of sophisticated Chinese consumers,” Vincent Boinay, L’Oréal North Asia president and China CEO, stated in a statement.

Organization description: Xinú is a Mexican luxury fragrance brand inspired by the craftsmanship, culture and storytelling of Mexico. It was founded in 2017 by Veronica Peña, Héctor Esrawe and Ignacio Cadena, and currently sells in Mexico and the US. Peña hinted that the investment from Estée Lauder Companies (ELC) will be used for expansion, saying in the press release that it marks the moment where “our unique vision for a fragrance company meets global possibility”.

Funding and round: Minority investment, terms undisclosed.

Investor(s): The Estée Lauder Companies (portfolio includes: Tom Ford Beauty, Jo Malone London, Le Labo).

Investor comments: “Mexico has become a vibrant hub of fragrance innovation — a place where craftsmanship and cultural relevance come together in remarkable ways,” stated Stéphane de La Faverie, president and CEO of ELC. “Xinú embodies this spirit, redefining contemporary luxury through authenticity, artistry and storytelling.”.

Tech giant description: American outerwear company Woolrich’s European operations were acquired by Italian licensing company BasicNet Group for €40 million from its previous owner, investment fund L-Gam. Woolrich’s core markets (especially Italy and Europe) overlap with those where BasicNet has built a solid presence, per the release. The deal is expected to be finalized in December.

Funding and round: Acquisition, terms undislosed.

Investor(s): BasicNet Group (portfolio includes: Kappa, Robe di Kappa, Superga).

Industry observers note that investor comments: “We are thrilled to welcome Woolrich into the BasicNet family. Woolrich is an extraordinary brand, with a history and identity that make it unique in the international outerwear landscape. It represents exactly the kind of cultural and authentic heritage we aim to preserve, enhance and relaunch. This is a perfectly coherent operation with our long-term vision, based on dynamic and responsible brand management. The acquisition comes in a complex economic context, but we are convinced that the strength of our model and the experience of our team will allow us to return the brand to growth,” noted Lorenzo Boglione and Alessandro Boglione, CEOs of BasicNet, in a statement.

Industry observers note that firm description: Skims has completed a $225 million funding round, increasing the value of the company to $5 billion. Co-founded in 2019 by Kim Kardashian and Jens Grede with a focus on shapewear, the brand is expected to surpass $1 billion in net sales by the end of 2025. Skims will use the funding to further its physical retail plans and set up shop beyond the States. Right now standing at 18 owned retail stores in the US and two franchised spaces in Mexico, the brand hopes to become a predominantly physical business over the next few years. Skims will also use the investment to boost product innovation and category expansion.

Funding and round: $225 million.

Investor(s): Goldman Sachs Alternatives (portfolio includes: Navex, Trackunit), BDT & MSD Partners (portfolio includes: Charlotte Tilbury, Tory Burch, Under Armour).

According to recent reports, investor comments: “Skims stands as a solutions-driven apparel innovator, pioneering newly introduced categories and redefining everyday wear. We look forward to partnering to pursue significant opportunities and deliver disruptive, sustained growth,” remarked Beat Cabiallavetta, global head of hybrid capital at Goldman Sachs Alternatives.

According to recent reports, tech giant description: Founded in 2019, Trip is a beverage and wellness brand known for its sparkling drinks infused with calming ingredients such as CBD, magnesium and adaptogens. After raising $40 million, the company is now valued at $300 million.

Funding and round: $40 million, Series A.

Investor(s): Coefficient Capital (portfolio includes: Oatly, Zoe, Vita Coco), Joe Jonas, Alessandra Ambrosio, Paul Wesley, Ashley Graham, Sophie Habboo.

It has been revealed that investor comments: “I partnered with Trip because they’re redefining what it means to find calm. The flavor is exquisite and I love the functionality. The ingredients are elite in the perfect kind of way — they really nailed it,” said Graham.

Recent findings suggest that company description: The Outnet is an off-price retailer founded in 2009 as part of Yoox Net-a-Porter (YNAP) Group, which was acquired earlier this year by Mytheresa and folded into the newly formed LuxExperience. At the time of the acquisition, YNAP’s off-price division (which also includes Yoox) was loss-making, so Mytheresa planned to separate its operations. Now, LuxExperience has sold The Outnet to The O Group LLC, who will acquire its assets and scale it into an independent business. LuxExperience will focus on a leaner off-price model for Yoox alone.

Funding and round: $30 million, acquisition.

Company description: Founded by Friends star Courteney Cox, Homecourt is a homecare brand launched in 2022 offering dish soap, surface sprays, hand soap and bodycare. The company will use the investment to propel growth by expanding its retail partnerships, strengthening brand awareness and eventually expanding internationally.

Funding and round: $8 million, Series A.

Investor(s): Cult Capital (portfolio includes: Supergoop, Act + Acre, Lawless).

In a recent development, organization description: Founded in 2019, Whatnot is a social commerce platform that allows users to purchase unique items and collectibles via a live stream. The company’s latest funding round brings its total value to almost $11.5 billion, more than double its valuation at the start of 2025.

Funding and round: $225 million, Series F.

Investor(s): DST Global (portfolio includes: Alibaba, Airbnb, Spotify), CapitalG (portfolio includes: Lyft, Duoligo, Stripe), Sequoia Capital, Alkeon Capital, Greycroft, Andreessen Horowitz, Avra, Bond.

Investor comments: “Whatnot brought the live-shopping wave to the US, the UK and Europe, and has turned it into one of the fastest-growing marketplaces. The brand’s explosive growth, loyal community and relentless execution in service of its buyers and sellers make it one of the most exciting bets in commerce today,” said Laela Sturdy, Whatnot board member and managing partner at CapitalG.

Recent findings suggest that manufacturer description: ShopMy is an affiliate and influencer marketing platform that connects brands including Rhode, Gucci and Kallmeyer with content creators, offering tools for creator commerce and streamlining partnerships. The company has raised $70 million, bringing its valuation to $1.5 billion. Its revenue has grown 200 per cent in the past year, with sustained profitability since 2024.

Funding and round: $70 million, Series B.

Investor(s): Avenir (portfolio includes: Merit Beauty, Sigma), Bain Capital Ventures, Bessemer Venture Partners, Menlo Ventures, Sofia Richie Grainge, Aimee Song, Gregg Renfrew, Revolve’s Raissa Gerona, AGM Ventures’s Alex Mondre, fashion photographer Jacopo Moschin.

Investor comments: “ShopMy has cracked the code on making creator commerce work for elevated brands without diluting their positioning,” said Avenir founder Andrew Sugrue. “When we evaluated the opportunity, the explosive growth was undeniable — they’ve created a complete solution that's taken off in 2025, representing a fundamentally better version of how commerce should work.”.

Manufacturer description: Kering has entered an agreement with L’Oréal Group to offload its beauty business.
