Archive’s software capitalises on this shift and enables brands to own a bigger slice of the resale pie, all while supporting profitability and sustainability goals,” remarked Eileen Waris, principal of Energize Capital, who has since joined Archive’s board.

Company description: AB Parfums, formerly known as Angelini Beauty, holds the beauty licenses to manufacture fragrances for a host of fashion and lifestyle brands including Trussardi, and also distributes a number of L’Oréal brands such as Ralph Lauren and Maison Margiela. The company was founded in 2013 as part of Italian multinational Angelini Industries.

Funding and round: Acquisition, terms undisclosed.

Investor(s): Give Back Beauty (beauty licensee for Chopard, Elie Saab, Zegna and more).

Recent findings suggest that investor comments: “AB Parfums will operate within the GBB Group as a dedicated business unit for European lifestyle and prestige brands within the fragrance and beauty sectors. This acquisition also reinforces GBB’s ‘direct-to-retail’ distribution in key countries like Italy, Germany and Spain,” remarked Corrado Brondi, founder and president of Give Back Beauty.

Recent findings suggest that organization description: Founded in 2000, Golden Goose is a luxury brand known for its sneakers and sportswear. Since 2020, investment firm Permira has held a majority stake and revenues have more than doubled. Blue Pool Capital, the Hong Kong-based family office of Alibaba co-founder and chairman Joe Tsai, has now taken a circa 12 per cent stake. The deal was negotiated shortly after Golden Goose decided to postpone its planned IPO in June 2024, and completed on 28 January 2025. The Italian brand intends to tap into Blue Pool Capital’s expertise in the sports, entertainment and consumer industries, as well as its knowledge of the APAC market, to help it expand.

Funding and round: Circa 12 per cent minority stake, terms undisclosed.

Investor(s): Blue Pool Capital (portfolio includes: Grail, Artifact Labs).

Investor comments: “We are huge believers in Golden Goose and its management team — its positioning at the intersection between luxury and sportswear is truly unique. We look forward to adding value beyond our financing to support [CEO] Silvio [Campara] and the great Golden Goose team as they unlock the brand’s full potential,” mentioned Oliver Weisberg, CEO of Blue Pool Capital.

According to recent reports, tech giant description: ShopMy is an influencer marketing platform that helps influencers monetise their content by gaining commissions through affiliate links. Brands including Reformation, Bergdorf Goodman and H&M are partners.

Funding and round: $77.5 million, Series B.

Investor(s): Bessemer Venture Partners (portfolio includes: Shopify, Pinterest, Twitch), Bain Capital Ventures (portfolio includes: Rent the Runway, Acorns), Gap chief business and strategy officer Eric Chan, along with influencers Camila Coelho, Campbell and Jett Puckett, and Shea McGee.

It has been revealed that investor comments: “ShopMy has cracked the code on scaling authentic influence,” said Jeremy Levine, partner at Bessemer. “By transforming trusted recommendations into measurable performance marketing, they’re pioneering an entirely new approach to commerce. Their remarkable growth and profitability demonstrate the massive potential of this market, and we’re thrilled to partner with them as they expand their vision.”.

Company description: Founded in 2012 by plastic surgeon Dr Yannis Alexandrides, who is based on London’s Harley Street, 111Skin is known for its clinical products and sheet masks that are popular among influencers and celebrities.

Funding and round: Significant minority investment, terms undisclosed.

Investor(s): Skky Partners, which was co-founded by Kim Kardashian (portfolio includes: Truff).

In a recent development, investor comments: “Eva [Alexandridis], Yannis, Vanessa [Goddevrind] and the 111Skin team have created and nurtured a coveted brand with world-class products and a loyal customer base, which fits perfectly with Skky’s strategy. 111Skin has a strong foundation and significant ongoing potential, and we are honoured to partner with the founders and leadership for the next phase of growth,” mentioned Skky Partners managing director David Brisske.

Company description: Minimalist is a premium skincare and haircare brand founded in 2020 by Mohit Yadav and Rahul Yadav, known for its science-based approach.

Funding and round: 90.5 per cent stake.

Investor(s): Hindustan Unilever (portfolio includes: Dermalogica, Dove, Tresemmé).

It has been revealed that investor comments: “This acquisition is another key step to grow our beauty and well-being portfolio in high-growth premium demand spaces. Mohit, Rahul and the team have created a great brand built on science, product efficacy and transparency,” noted Rohit Jawa, CEO and managing director of Hindustan Unilever.

In a recent development, organization description: Vince is a premium US label best known for its seasonless essentials. As part of the acquisition, P180 — which is owned by Brendan Hoffman (who was Vince’s CEO from 2015 to 2020) and tech platform Caastle CEO Christine Hunsicker — has reinstated Hoffman as CEO, effective 3 February.

Funding and round: Acquisition, terms undisclosed.

Investor(s): P180 (portfolio includes: Altuzarra, Elyse Walker).

According to recent reports, investor comments: “Personally, I have a strong connection to the Vince brand, having served as Vince CEO for five years. I am excited to lead the team again as we continue to unlock upcoming growth opportunities, drive innovation, enhance the brand's market position and focus on monetising the organization’s inventory to ensure continued long-term success,” remarked Hoffman in a statement.

Company description: Pangaia was founded in 2018 by influencer-turned-entrepreneur Miroslava Duma along with six other co-founders who make up the Pangaia Collective. The brand is best known for its colourful sweatshirts and for investing in material innovation startups such as Mirum and Kintra Fibres.

Funding and round: Acquisition, terms undisclosed.

Investor(s): Royal Group (portfolio sectors includes: healthcare, real estate and construction, AI, technology, hospitality, media).

Tech giant description: Gloss Ventures is a brand incubator that owns Glossmetics, a skincare brand targeting Gen Alpha and Gen Z, and Sacheu, a brand founded in 2021, which is known for its TikTok-favourite peel-off lip liner.

Funding and round: $15 million, Series A.

Investor(s): Peterson Partners (portfolio includes: Solidcore, Glowbar, Allbirds).

Tech giant description: Founded in 2010 by aesthetician Rachel Roff and led by CEO Victoria Payne, Urban Skin Rx specialises in products for melanin-rich skin (its bestseller is a kojic acid cleansing bar). The brand is stocked at Ulta Beauty, Target, Walmart and Amazon.

Funding and round: Acquisition, terms undisclosed.

Investor(s): American Exchange Group (portfolio includes: Indee Lee, AX Beauty).

Recent findings suggest that firm description: Greenstitch is a decentralised climate data platform that aims to help fashion brands identify gaps in their supply chain management and product lifecycle management systems, while using artificial intelligence and machine learning to fill gaps in the data sets. The platform also aims to help brands assess the environmental impact of design decisions and identify ESG risks early on in the production process.

Funding and round: $1.2 million, seed.

Investor(s): Equirus InnovateX Fund (portfolio includes: Datazip, Pointo), Ivycap Ventures (portfolio includes: Purplle, Clovia), Warmup Ventures (portfolio includes: Nitro Commerce, WeVois), Zeca Ventures (portfolio includes: Zavya, House of X).

Recent findings suggest that company description: Exuud is a fragrance technology company best known for creating Soliqaire, a fragrance delivery system that uses biodegradable polymer to release fragrance rather than relying on heat or aerosols. Exuud claims this technique allows for longer lasting and more intense fragrances. As part of the deal, Estée Lauder Companies will integrate Exuud’s technology into its fragrance portfolio by the end of 2025.

Funding and round: Minority investment, terms undisclosed.

Investor(s): Estée Lauder Companies (portfolio includes: Tom Ford Beauty, Jo Malone London, Le Labo).

Investor comments: “We’re excited to announce our partnership with Exuud on this cutting-edge technology to support our artisanal craftsmanship and revolutionise how we experience fragrances with more control, consistency, personalisation and sustainability. The breakthrough possibilities for customisation in design, fragrance experience and more are exciting,” said Sumit Bhasin, SVP of corporate fragrance research and development, product development and innovation at Estée Lauder Companies.

Tech giant description: Raspberry AI turns garment sketches into photorealistic renderings that show details of how the product would look and fit in real life. The startup uses machine learning to train AI models to learn a brand’s unique DNA, aesthetic and fabric library. Brands including MCM and Under Armour are among its clients.

Funding and round: $24 million, Series A.

Investor(s): Andreessen Horowitz (portfolio includes: Instagram, Roblox, Airbnb), Greycroft Partners (portfolio includes: Epic Games, The RealReal, Goop), Correlation Ventures (portfolio includes: Upstart, Astra, Gabi), MVP Ventures (portfolio includes: Frore Systems, Delphi), angel investor Gokul Rajaram (portfolio includes: Poshmark, Printify), Ken Pilot Ventures (portfolio includes: Lily AI, Sizer, Reupp).

Investor comments: “Raspberry AI supercharges creative teams by leveraging AI at every stage of the design workflow. The comprehensiveness and technical depth of the platform have led to strong customer love and some of the strongest engagement metrics we’ve seen for AI tools. We believe that Raspberry AI will rapidly scale and transform the way creative teams design and develop retail products,” remarked Bryan Kim, partner at Andreessen Horowitz.

It has been revealed that organization description: Ras is an Indian luxury beauty brand, known for its organic ingredients sourced from sustainable farms. The brand calls itself India’s first “farm-to-face” beauty brand, meaning ingredients can be traced back to farms in Raipur, which are then manufactured into skincare products.

Funding and round: $5 million, Series A.

Investor(s): Unilever Ventures (portfolio includes: The Inkey List, Trinny London, Grown Alchemist), Amazon Smbhav Venture Fund (portfolio includes: Axio, Bare Anatomy), Sixth Sense Ventures (portfolio includes: Grab, Bombay Shaving Manufacturer), among other angel investors.

Investor comments: “Over the next five to seven years, the premium beauty market in India will witness significant growth, and Ras, with its distinct value proposition, is well poised to capture this opportunity,” said Pawan Chaturvedi, head of Unilever Ventures Asia.

Industry observers note that firm description: Founded in 2019, Whatnot is a social commerce platform that allows consumers to purchase unique items and collectibles via live-stream shopping. The company’s latest funding round brings its valuation to almost $5 billion.

Funding and round: $265 million, Series E.

Investor(s): Greycroft Partners (portfolio includes: Epic Games, The RealReal, Goop), DST Global (portfolio includes: Facebook, Spotify), Avra Investments (portfolio includes: Zepto), Lightspeed Venture Partners (portfolio includes: Haus Laboratories, Vinted), Durable Capital Partners (portfolio includes: Warby Parker, Duolingo, Deliveroo), plus existing investors.

It has been revealed that investor comments: “Whatnot has tapped into a powerful shift in the way people shop — live, video, social and mobile first. The manufacturer has built a multi-category platform that can address all of retail, approximately $7 trillion in the United States alone,” said Marcie Vu, partner at Greycroft.

Industry observers note that manufacturer description: Bonpoint is a premium childrenswear brand founded in France in 1975. The brand was acquired by private investment firm EPI in 2007, and has grown a strong presence in Asia and Europe.

Funding and round: Acquisition, terms undisclosed.

Investor(s): Youngor Group (portfolio includes: Youngor, Mayor, Undefeated).

Sources indicate that organization description: Founded in 2002, True Religion is known for its denim with distinctive contrast stitching. The brand went public in 2003, but struggled throughout the decade and eventually filed for bankruptcy in 2017 — and again in 2020. In 2021, the brand saw a resurgence thanks to Gen Z Y2K fanatics finding newfound appreciation for vintage True Religion jeans. Under the terms of the acquisition, SB360 (an investor in apparel and retail) will combine resources with Acon Investments to accelerate True Religion’s growth.

Funding and round: Acquisition, terms undisclosed.

Investor(s): Acon Investments (portfolio includes: Beauty by Imagination, New Era, Germaine de Capuccini).

Sources indicate that investor comments: “True Religion has built a unique and powerful brand with a loyal customer base and a deep connection to its core values of authenticity, quality and self-expression. Our partnership with SB360 will provide valuable additional resources essential to unlocking the tech giant’s full potential,” stated Suma Kulkarni, managing partner at Acon Investments.

True Religion jeans on display in 2008.

Company description: Christian Lacroix is a French fashion house known for extravagant and theatrical designs. The couture house was founded in 1987 by its eponymous designer, who made a name for himself working at Patou. In 1995, Lacroix sold the company to LVMH; and in 2005, it was acquired by Falic Group, but entered administration in 2009, later becoming a licensing operation.

Funding and round: Acquisition, terms undisclosed.

Investor(s): Sociedad Textil Lonia (portfolio includes: CH Carolina Herrera, Purificación García).

Investor comments: “We admired the vision, the magic and the craftmanship of Maison Lacroix, so when the opportunity arose we eagerly embraced it. We will do everything we can to ensure that the unique talent of its creator and his invaluable contribution to the fashion world reach their full potential,” Sociedad Textil Lonia noted in a statement.

Christian Lacroix Autumn/Winter 1999 couture show.

Sources indicate that tech giant description: Founded in 1985, Kapital is a Japanese menswear brand known for its high-quality denim and workwear. The brand often uses traditional textile techniques in its designs and has grown a cult following among streetwear aficionados.

Funding and round: Acquisition, terms undisclosed.

Investor(s): L Catterton (portfolio includes: Etro, Ganni, Birkenstock).

Kapital's cult-favourite smile denim jacket.

It has been revealed that manufacturer description: Laura Ashley is a British lifestyle brand founded in the 1950s, best known for its textile designs. The brand sells a variety of clothing, furniture and interior decorations. The brand went public in 1985 following the death of its eponymous founder. In 2020, Laura Ashley was rescued from administration by Gordon Brothers, which acquired the brand to turn it around, with a focus on expanding its licensing and e-commerce capabilities.

Funding and round: Acquisition, terms undisclosed.

Investor(s): Marquee Brands (portfolio includes: Ben Sherman).

According to recent reports, investor comments: “Laura Ashley’s licensed business model and robust group of high-quality partners makes the brand a seamless addition to Marquee Brands,” stated Marquee Brands CEO Heath Golden. “With the existing UK team in place, we are primed and ready to leverage Laura Ashley’s seven-decade legacy to unlock its future potential as a full lifestyle brand innovating fresh products and categories, offering unique collaborations and engaging multi-generational audiences in key markets worldwide.”.

Laura Ashley dresses displayed at the Victoria & Albert Museum in London as part of the British Design 1948-2012 Innovation In The Modern Age exhibition.

Sources indicate that organization description: Neiman Marcus Group owns US department stores Neiman Marcus and Bergdorf Goodman. The merger with Saks Global marks the formation of a fresh American luxury group, and Saks indicates this is only step one in its expansion looks.

Funding and round: Acquisition, $2.7 billion.

Investor(s): Saks Global (portfolio includes: Saks Fifth Avenue, Saks Off Fifth).

In a recent development, investor comments: “This milestone transaction marks a transformative moment for Saks Global and the luxury retail industry. By uniting Neiman Marcus, Bergdorf Goodman and Saks Fifth Avenue, we have created an unparalleled multi-brand luxury portfolio with tremendous growth potential,” noted Saks Global executive chairman Richard Baker.

Company description: Wannaby offers virtual try-on solutions that use augmented reality and computer vision technologies. It was acquired by Farfetch in 2022 for $24.5 million in cash and nearly $5 million in shares. Farfetch will continue to use Wannaby’s solutions following the acquisition.

Funding and round: Acquisition, terms undisclosed.

Investor comments: “By welcoming Wannaby’s capabilities into our portfolio, we are poised to enrich our digital solutions and reinforce our presence in the fashion-tech landscape. This expansion into new fashion categories such as shoes and bags demonstrates our commitment to innovation and our ability to deliver exceptional value to clients across diverse sectors,” stated Perfect Corp CEO Alice Chang.

Recent findings suggest that company description: Gowoonsesang Cosmetics was founded by Korean dermatologist Ahn Gun Young in 2000. The company’s most notable brand is science-based skincare line Dr.G, which Young also founded. The company was previously owned by Swiss retailer Migros.

Funding and round: Acquisition, terms undisclosed.

Investor(s): L’Oréal (portfolio includes: Kiehl’s, Cerave, SkinCeuticals).

Investor comments: “We have been following the brand and its success for many years and we look forward to accelerating its growth in South Korea and the rest of the world,” remarked Alexis Perakis-Valat, president of L’Oréal’s consumer products division.

Organization description: Thirteen Lune is a beauty e-commerce platform that sells products from Black and brown-owned companies, as well as ally brands that uplift communities of colour. The company was founded by entrepreneur Nyakio Grieco and Patrick Herning, founder of plus-size retailer 11 Honoré, in 2020. The acquisition signals a restructuring: Grieco has been named CEO, while Herning has exited the business.

Funding and round: Acquisition, terms undisclosed.

Investor(s): SNR Capital, which channels brands into PCA Companies (portfolio includes: Medik8, Space NK US).

Manufacturer description: Swedish retail software-as-a-service platform Voyado uses artificial intelligence to improve customisation and personalisation through insights and campaign automation. The platform has achieved an annual growth rate of 35 per cent, according to the company, with particular success in the Nordics, the Netherlands, Belgium and Luxembourg.

Funding and round: Minority stake, terms undisclosed.

Investor(s): H&M Group Ventures (portfolio includes: Goop, Klarna, Cult Mia).

Recent findings suggest that investor comments: “We are really impressed by Voyado’s journey so far. After rolling out their solution globally, we’ve seen first hand the difference it makes in creating value at scale. That’s why it makes perfect sense for the H&M Group to deepen our partnership through an investment, which will further support Voyado’s future growth and strengthen their offering for other enterprise customers,” said Erik Lagerblad, head of H&M Group Ventures.

In a recent development, organization description: Vera Wang started as a bridal salon and grew into a lifestyle brand offering ready-to-wear, homeware, jewellery, fragrance and shoes. Wang, who has been the sole owner since founding the company in 1990, has designed wedding dresses for celebrities including Beyoncé, Jennifer Lopez and Ariana Grande. The brand’s annual revenue is over $700 million, according to the company.

Funding and round: Acquisition, terms undisclosed.

Investor(s): WHP Global (portfolio includes: Rag & Bone, G-Star, Joe’s Jeans).

Investor comments: “Vera Wang is a legend. Her name is synonymous with modernity, artistry and impeccable style. We are honoured to partner with Vera Wang and look forward to building on the brand’s remarkable legacy with newly introduced business opportunities around the world,” noted Yehuda Shmidman, chairman and CEO of WHP Global.

Company description: Founded by the eponymous PR guru in Paris in 2006, the agency represents over 100 of the most exciting brands across fashion, beauty, lifestyle and art, including Jacquemus, Coperni and Loewe. Pagès opened a Upcoming York branch in 2019.

Funding and round: Acquisition, terms undisclosed.

Investor(s): The Independents (portfolio includes: Karla Otto, Lefty, Bureau Betak).

Investor comments: “We’re delighted to welcome Lucien, who is the perfect addition to the puzzle we’ve been building for some years now,” mentioned The Independents CEO Isabelle Chouvet. “Today’s clients are so global that it’s no longer possible, I think, to stand alone. So we have to be able to work together to meet these needs.”.

Tech giant description: Tangle Teezer was founded in 2007 in London, and has grown to become one of the most popular hair detangling brush makers in the UK thanks to its two-tiered teeth technology that claims to reduce damage. Since 2021, the brand has been owned by Mayfair Equity Partners. The company has reportedly doubled in size over the past four years, with net sales worth approximately €70 million as of 2024.

Funding and round: Acquisition, €200 million.

It has been revealed that investor comments: “We are excited to acquire a market-leading business in a dynamic, high-growth market where we can drive significant value. Both companies share a deep spirit of joy, innovation, entrepreneurship and a common vision for growth. With a consumer-first approach, together we aim to redefine personal grooming by creating personalised haircare solutions that enhance daily routines,” mentioned Bic CEO Gonzalve Bich.

Manufacturer description: About You is a German e-commerce company founded in 2014 specialising in personalisation and influencer marketing. The company offers business-to-business tech services for online retailers and its annual sales reached €1.9 billion in 2023 — it’s now Hamburg’s first unicorn.

Funding and round: Acquisition, €6.50 per share (approximately €1.13 billion).

It has been revealed that investor comments: “I’m excited about how together we’ll be able to cover a larger share of the fashion and lifestyle market. In B2C, we can offer customers and brands distinct and rich shopping experiences. In B2B, combining our complementary software capabilities — Tradebyte and Scayle — will create an even more advanced e-commerce operating system that enables brands and retailers to manage their multi-channel business across Europe and beyond,” said Robert Gentz, co-CEO and co-founder of Zalando.

According to recent reports, firm description: French boutique hotel group Les Domaines de Fontenille was founded in 2016 and owns 11 properties with strong heritage across France, Spain and Italy, including Tuscany, Marseille and Menorca. The group’s clientele includes young travellers looking for a premium experience.

Funding and round: Minority investment, terms undisclosed.

Investor(s): LVMH (portfolio includes: Louis Vuitton, Belmond, Cheval Blanc) and Anaïs Ventures (portfolio includes: IB2).

In a recent development, investor comments: “This financial investment by LVMH in Les Domaines de Fontenille is an opportunity to explore a complementary realm to the hospitality offerings we provide through our brands. We are pleased to support the founders, Frédéric Biousse and Guillaume Foucher, as well as CEO Linda Hazi, in writing the next chapter of the brand’s development,” stated Jean-Jacques Guiony, CEO of Moët Hennessy, LVMH’s wines and spirits division.

Tech giant description: Beauty brand Pañpuri was founded in Bangkok by Vorravit Siripark in 2003. It is known for its premium skincare, haircare, bath and body, and fragrance products inspired by Thai wellness traditions.

Funding and round: Acquisition, terms undisclosed.

Investor(s): Kosé (portfolio includes: Tarte, Decorté).

Investor comments: “With this acquisition of shares, we will accelerate the global strategy set forth in our medium to long-term vision and aim to establish a presence in the Global South markets and further enhance our value,” remarked Kazutoshi Kobayashi, president and CEO of Kosé.

It has been revealed that tech giant description: London-based resale startup launched in 2022 by Warwick University graduates Woody Lello (CEO), Felix Jackson (COO), Jack Cardwell (CIO) and Connor Mattinson (CTO). The Truss platform uses artificial intelligence to identify the specific product in an image and then shares detailed information about that item, with the goal of improving searchability and conversion rates. Thanks to the latest investment, Truss has secured the match funding to activate a £1.1 million grant from Innovate UK. The startup previously raised £345,000 in pre-seed funding.

Funding and round: $300,000, pre-seed.

Investor(s): Figr Ventures (Truss is its first investment).

Investor comments: “We believe the fashion sector needs to change, we believe circularity is the answer and we believe Truss is the way for businesses to achieve this,” said Fiona Humphries, managing director of Figr Ventures.

According to recent reports, tech giant description: Norwegian premium luggage and travel bag brand Db was founded in 2012, originally called Douchebags, and has risen in popularity among surfers, skiers and other outdoor sports fans. The brand is stocked in Selfridges, Harrods, End, Goodhood and more. The funds will go towards Db’s international expansion, design innovation and store openings in Europe.

Funding and round: Minority stake, terms undisclosed.

Investor(s): LVMH Luxury Ventures (portfolio includes: Our Legacy, Lyst, Aimé Leon Dore).

Investor comments: “Db is a reference in the bags and luggage sector, combining truly distinctive designs with high quality and functionality, and is geared towards a close community of outdoor enthusiasts, athletes, creative people and passionate travellers. Db has a strong position in Scandinavia with an untapped growth potential in the rest of the world,” mentioned Julie Bercovy, CEO of LVMH Luxury Ventures Advisors.

Firm description: Brand Architekts is a beauty group that counts drugstore brands Skinny Tan and Super Facialist among its portfolio. In October, the company reported a 15 per cent drop in sales for the year ended 30 June as it shifted its focus to fewer, larger brands.

Funding and round: £13.9 million, acquisition.

Investor(s): Warpaint (portfolio includes: Technic, W7).

Investor comments: “As part of a larger group we believe applying our established supply and distribution channels and approach to Brand Architekts will improve efficiency, reduce costs and drive profitability,” remarked Warpaint CEO Sam Bazini.

Recent findings suggest that company description: Founded by French makeup artist Violette Serrat in 2021, Newly introduced York-based Violette_FR exclusively offers a 14-piece core collection that includes makeup, skincare and haircare. The brand has risen to popularity thanks to Serrat’s signature ‘French girl’ aesthetic.

Funding and round: Series B, terms undisclosed.

Investor(s): Silas Capital (portfolio includes: Makeup by Mario, Herbivore, Wonderbelly), Experienced Capital, Monogram Capital Partners, Felix Capital.

Investor comments: “Violette_FR stands out in the beauty landscape for its aspirational French brand appeal, driven by Violette’s authenticity and credibility, which resonate deeply with consumers,” said Brian Thorne, partner at Silas Capital.

Firm description: Launched in 2018, Korean womenswear platform Ably has tripled its value to over $2 billion over the past three years, and is now considered a unicorn under Alibaba’s investment.

Funding and round: $71 million.

Investor(s): Alibaba Group (portfolio includes: AliExpress, Tmall, Taobao).

Recent findings suggest that organization description: Indian clean beauty brand Earth Rhythm offers plastic-free packaging and biodegradable products, as well as vegan and cruelty-free formulations. Founded in 2019, the brand has 250 offerings spanning skincare, haircare and cosmetics. In 2022, Nykaa acquired a minority stake in the brand.

Funding and round: Acquisition, terms undisclosed.

Investor(s): Nykaa (portfolio includes: Kay Beauty, Pipa Bella, Dot & Key).

Investor comments: “Earth Rhythm represents an exciting addition to our portfolio and presents an opportunity to expand our play in the clean beauty space, a category with immense long-term potential,” remarked Adwaita Nayar, co-founder of Nykaa and CEO of Nykaa Fashion.

Organization description: H&M Group’s digital fashion outlet launched in 2018. Due to a lack of demand, the group revealed that Afound would be discontinued in August, but it will integrate with Secret Sales under a December relaunch, offering over €5 billion in revenue sourced from 3,800 premium brands.

Funding and round: Acquisition, terms undisclosed.

Investor(s): Secret Sales, an off-price marketplace within private equity firm Perwyn’s portfolio.

Investor comments: “Bringing Afound into the Secret Sales family reinforces our commitment to growing our premium off-price solution across Europe. This acquisition is another step towards transforming the off-price landscape,” said Chris Griffin, CEO of Secret Sales.

Recent findings suggest that firm description: Manchester-based men’s streetwear brand founded by brothers George and Michael Heaton in 2011. The brand has scaled rapidly with a compound annual growth rate of 64 per cent since 2020, delivering double-digit profit margins, and expects to generate around £100 million in revenue by the end of the fiscal year. In 2021, Represent introduced its ‘247’ performance line and in 2024 it introduced its first retail locations in LA and Manchester, with a London store planned for 2025. The brand aims to use the funding to fuel retail expansion and improve operational capabilities.

Funding and round: Minority stake, terms undisclosed.

Investor(s): True (Portfolio includes: Formerly Known As Haeckels, Boy Smells).

Investor comments: “Represent is a real success story for British fashion. The team’s track record of developing culturally relevant products and acquiring loyal customers to the brand, despite the challenging consumer environment, is remarkable,” noted Ejike Onuchukwu, investment director at True, who has joined Represent’s board.

Company description: Paris-based lab-grown leather startup founded in 2021. Faircraft manufactures leather using cellular biology that replicates the structure and cellular composition of animal skin. The funding will be used to expand Faircraft’s team, recruiting more engineers and biologists to scale its operations.

Funding and round: €15.8 million, Series A.

Investor(s): Kindred Ventures (portfolio includes: Poshmark, Postmates), Cap Horn, BPI, Sake Bosch, Entrepreneur First, Alliance for Impact, Heirloom.

According to recent reports, investor comments: “Leather has long been the cornerstone of the fashion industry, valued for its timeless appeal and durability — but its production comes with steep environmental costs. Faircraft’s lab-grown leather is a breakthrough for brands and consumers who refuse to compromise between quality and sustainability, and we’re proud to support them as they scale operations and bring this revolutionary product to market,” noted Kanyi Maqubela, managing partner at Kindred Ventures.

Company description: Founded in 2019, Clean Skin Club is a mass skincare brand known for its single-use disposable facial towels, stocked across Amazon, Target and Beauty Bay, among others. The brand was inspired by an aesthetician’s complaint about the bacteria in spa towels. The funds will be used to expand the brand’s bricks-and-mortar retail, latest product development and grow the team.

Funding and round: $32 million, Series X.

Investor(s): Astō Consumer Partners, Amberstone (portfolio includes: Bloom Nutrition, Crown Affair).

Investor comments: “Clean Skin Club is ushering in a fresh era of skincare through reimagining the category and delivering straightforward, science-backed solutions that truly work. The disruptive brand has amassed a cult following, ranking as a bestseller on Amazon and breaking through the large, high-growth skincare market,” said Clayton Christopher, co-founder of Astō Consumer Partners.

Tech giant description: Prestige haircare brand founded in 2020 and known for its promotion of haircare as a selfcare ritual. Crown Affair previously generated $5 million in Series A funding in 2022, also led by True Beauty Ventures. The Series B funding will be used to expand Crown Affair’s offering at Sephora, build out its team and scale marketing initiatives.

Funding and round: $9 million, Series B.

Investor(s): True Beauty Ventures (Portfolio includes: K18 Hair, Caliray, Maude).

Investor comments: “As a long-time supporter, I have witnessed Crown Affair consistently demonstrate the strength of its brand with a unique blend of elevated, clean haircare innovation, thoughtful hair rituals and authentic storytelling,” said Cristina Nuñez, co-founder and managing partner of True Beauty Ventures.

Sources indicate that company description: Beauty supplements and wellness brand, founded by influencer Tati Westbrook in 2018. Westbrook departed the company in August 2024 after settling a four-year legal battle in which her business partner, Clark Swanson, accused Westbrook and her husband of fraud, negligence and breach of fiduciary duty to Halo Beauty.

Funding and round: Acquisition, terms undisclosed.

Investor comments: “We’re honoured to carry Halo Beauty’s legacy forwards by expanding its mission of clean, effective beauty and wellness. This acquisition marks a upcoming era of innovation and commitment to empowering consumers with products that enhance both their beauty and overall well-being,” said the private investor.

Company description: Skincare brand known for peptide-infused anti-ageing products. The brand claims its signature OS-01 peptide can reverse the skin’s biological age ageing by preventing senescent or “zombie” cells, which are cells that are alive but damaged. OneSkin was founded by four PhD scientists: Carolina Reis de Oliveira, Alessandra Zonari, Mariana Boroni and Juliana Carvalho. The recent investment brings OneSkin’s total funding to $20 million.

Funding and round: $7 million, Series A.

Investor(s): Selva Ventures, Plus Capital, Unilever Ventures, Able Partners, Camila Alves McConaughey (Brazilian-American model and wife of actor Matthew McConaughey), tech entrepreneur Kevin Rose, plus previous investors.

In a recent development, investor comments: “As a Brazilian woman, I am thrilled to invest in a brand founded by four Brazilian female scientists — my heritage is something I’m incredibly proud of, and I am honoured to support those who are executing this work. The OneSkin team has built a line of products that hold a unique space in the massive skincare market. I fell in love with the products the moment I saw the results on myself, and I knew I had to be a part of it! I’m so looking forward to seeing their future innovations and continued success with the help of this funding,” said McConaughey.

Manufacturer description: Wholesale vintage clothing marketplace founded in 2021 by Abhi Arora and Sanket Agarwal. The platform connects retailers and resellers to inventory from verified vintage wholesalers around the world.

Funding and round: £17 million total, £4.7 million in seed and £12.3 million in Series A.

Investor(s): HV Capital (portfolio includes: Depop, Zalando, Hello Fresh), Andreessen Horowitz (portfolio includes: Instagram, Pinterest, Roblox), Y Combinator (portfolio includes: Snap, Airbnb), Shopify president Harley Finkelstein, former Depop CEO Maria Raga.

Investor comments: “We are proud to invest in Fleek, a company that is redefining the secondhand fashion landscape. Fleek’s innovative approach to scaling the secondhand market globally reflects tremendous potential for growth. The marketplace not only addresses current industry needs but also paves the way for a more sustainable future in fashion. We’re excited to be part of this journey,” said Felix Klür, general partner at HV Capital.

Recent findings suggest that company description: Founded in 2005 in Stockholm by Jockum Hallin, Cristopher Nying and Richardos Klarén, Our Legacy is known for high-quality menswear with intricate design signatures. The brand has around 200 stockists and seven of its own stores, and has risen in notoriety thanks to buzzy collaborations with Stüssy and Emporio Armani.

Funding and round: Minority stake, terms undisclosed.

Lead investor(s): LVMH Luxury Ventures (portfolio includes: Aimé Leon Dore, Lyst, Heat).

Investor comments: “Our Legacy is the epitome of what we could call the ‘quiet cool’ tendency, featuring a unique blend of contemporary minimalism and creative subversion,” said Julie Bercovy, CEO of LVMH Luxury Ventures Advisors.

In a recent development, manufacturer description: Californian premium athleisure brand Vuori was founded in 2015 by Joe Kudla. The brand is known for its unique fabrics and is certified as carbon neutral by Change Climate. Following this investment, the brand’s valuation has reached $5.5 billion, building on a $400 million investment by Softbank Vision Fund 2 in 2021, which brought its valuation to $4 million.

Funding and round: $825 million, secondary tender offer.

Lead investor(s): General Atlantic (portfolio includes: Gymshark, Sézane, Tory Burch), Stripes (portfolio includes: On, Reformation, Khaite) and existing investors.

Investor comments: “Vuori encapsulates everything we look for in a Stripes investment — the products are amazing and beloved by the consumer, the team is fanatical about quality and innovation, and the market for athleisure is global with durable tailwinds,” remarked Chris Carey, partner at Stripes.

It has been revealed that organization description: Secondhand peer-to-peer marketplace founded in 2008 by Milda Mitkutė and Justas Janauskas in Lithuania. The platform is Europe’s largest clothing resale marketplace. The recent investment brings Vinted’s valuation to €5 billion.

Funding and round: €340 million, secondary share sale.

Investor(s): TPG Tech Adjacencies, Hedosophia (portfolio includes: Monzo, Go Puff), Baille Gifford, Invus Opportunities (portfolio includes: Coupang, Chrono 24), FJ Labs (portfolio includes: Farfetch, Uber, Klarna), Manhattan Venture Partners (portfolio includes: Discord, Epic Games, X), Moore Strategic Ventures.

Sources indicate that investor comments: “We’ve seen that consumers are increasingly choosing secondhand as a core part of their wardrobe, as sustainability and flexibility become top of mind for many people. Vinted’s customer focus, leading product experience, and sophisticated approach to logistics have made this market accessible to an even broader population,” said TPG partner Andrew Doyle.

Sources indicate that company description: Biotech-powered prestige skincare brand Reome was founded by beauty editor and acupuncturist Joanna Ellner in 2023. The UK-based brand is known for its sensorial products and is stocked in Space NK, Liberty and Moda Operandi among others.

Funding and round: $1.4 million, seed.

Investor(s): Rianta Capital (portfolio includes: El Rayo, Home Cooks).

Sources indicate that company description: UK-based women’s shirt brand introduced in 2017 by a former Vogue stylist and Tatler editor Pip Durell. The B Corp-certified brand, which is known for timeless designs inspired by men’s tailoring and British heritage, launched its first pair of trousers earlier this year and plans to expand further with blazers and knitwear at the start of 2025. With Nothing Underneath was named one of Walpole’s Brands of Tomorrow in 2022.

Funding and round: $2.5 million, seed.

Lead investor(s): Pembroke VCT (portfolio includes: Tala, Me+Em, Bella Freud) and JamJar Investments (portfolio includes: Deliveroo, Oatly, Spoke).

Investor comments: “With Nothing Underneath (WNU) holds a unique position in the womenswear market. Pip and her team have built a fantastic brand around one staple item, the shirt — an essential in most women’s wardrobes. It has become a standout in the fashion industry and early growth metrics have given us conviction in the brand. This investment will enable this emerging British heritage brand to enhance its product range, assist with growth and support WNU’s international reach,” said Andrew Wolfson, CEO of Pembroke Investment Managers.

Firm description: UK-based luxury retail platform that stocks a curation of independent brands. The retailer is known for its selection of vibrant eveningwear. Founded in 2019 by Nina Briance, Cult Mia initially received $3 million in seed funding in November 2023 led by Fuel Ventures, with participation from Morgan Stanley and David Wertheimer of the Chanel family.

Funding and round: $2 million, seed (bringing total seed funding to $5 million).

Investor(s): H&M Group Ventures (portfolio includes: Goop, Klarna) and existing investors.

Industry observers note that investor comments: “We are delighted to invest in Cult Mia on their mission to launch independent and diverse designers from around the world. We have been incredibly impressed by all that Cult Mia has achieved in such a short space of time,” mentioned Nanna Andersen, chief of new growth and ventures at H&M Group.

Organization description: Founded in 1997 by Dr Gregory Brown, Révive is known for its luxury serums and creams powered by bio-renewal technology. The brand was previously acquired by Shiseido in 2016, before it was sold to Tengram Capital Partners in 2017.

Funding and round: Acquisition, terms undisclosed.

Investor(s): S’Young Group (portfolio includes: Evidens de Beauté, Pier Augé).

Derek Hough Reveals Why He Really Gave Everyone the Same Score on ‘DWTS’

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that it seems like Derek Hough’s rage-bait isn’t limited to Coach Jackie J. (IYKYK!) The Dancing with the Stars judge seems to have fans spiraling over his scores from last week’s Grammy Night performances.

Derek scored each couple a 9 for each of their performances throughout the night, and DWTS devotees were understandably curious as to why.

When pro dancer Ezra Sosa chatted with the judge during the after-show livestream on TikTok, Derek joked, “Listen, I’ve had three hours of sleep. I came from Seattle this morning on tour. I’m going to Florida right after this Disney special, and then back on tour…That’s why I think I’m giving nines to everybody today.”.

The joke seemingly went over some people’s heads, as one person criticized the longtime judge for “flying under the radar” as the “nice guy.”.

It has been revealed that “Did derek actually say he was tired so he gave everyone a 9.. #dwts,” one person wrote, while another chimed in, “Yes!!!!! I can’t believe there isn’t more people talking about this right now!!!! That was so unprofessional not only that, but why are you acting like the semifinals aren’t on Tuesday??? Just handing 9s to whoever or whatever the dance was.”.

Another person even joked that Coach Jackie should have been in the ballroom to “keep eyes on Derek.”.

“What do you actually mean derek was ‘too tired to judge’ so he just gave everybody a nine,” they wrote alongside a clip of Jackie in the DWTS audience a few weeks prior.

What’s more: Derek retroactively shared a vlog recounting the day he got “three hours of sleep.”.

“So this is why you were funky during the show 😭,” someone commented, while another criticized, “Next year, maybe delay the tour so that the contestants can be fairly judged by someone who isn’t just throwing in the towel and scoring all 9s because they’re tired.”.

4 Infrared Saunas That Belong in Your Home

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (896 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Esquire

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Go to any high-end hotel or luxury chain gym these days and you’ll see a NordicTrack treadmill with a massive screen, a fancy rowing machine, and maybe a shallow pool for a cold plunge.
  • Sources indicate that before you tell me it’s not feasible or you don’t have the space or don’t want to tear up a wall, hear me out.
  • Recent findings suggest that for all these reasons, infrared saunas started to catch on as a home alternative to spending an extra half hour at your gym or going to the bathhouse.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Go to any high-end hotel or luxury chain gym these days and you’ll see a NordicTrack treadmill with a massive screen, a fancy rowing machine, and maybe a shallow pool for a cold plunge. You also may see a glowing red box in place of the traditional steam room. That’s an infrared sauna, and it’s at the cutting edge of wellness tech. At the end of the day, nothing compares to sweating it out.

Sources indicate that before you tell me it’s not feasible or you don’t have the space or don’t want to tear up a wall, hear me out. Plenty of people have saunas in their homes. And with an infrared sauna, the process doesn’t require complicated plumbing and ventilation. Instead, it’s all electric and easier than ever to set up in your home. Instead of traditional water-based saunas, infrared saunas use infrared light to heat you. The ambient temperature won’t get as hot as steam-based saunas, but the far-infrared light will penetrate your body directly. In short, it won’t feel as hot, and you’ll still sweat.

Recent findings suggest that for all these reasons, infrared saunas started to catch on as a home alternative to spending an extra half hour at your gym or going to the bathhouse. Many of them can fit more than one person, but you can opt for something a bit more snug as well. Some of them even have Bluetooth speakers. We’ve even found an option for those who truly don’t have the space. Call it an apartment-friendly solution. No matter your needs or restrictions, these are the best infrared saunas for your home.

First and foremost, the LIT Method BeautyBox is just a great sauna. No buts or caveats, it was good enough that we called it the best home sauna of 2026 in this year’s gadget awards. It uses the full spectrum of infrared (near, mid, and far), which adds a broader range of health benefits. Far-infrared is what causes the sweating, but the often left out mid and near wavelengths penetrate your skin and blood vessels for more comprehensive relaxation and recovery.

It has been revealed that the BeautyBox comfortably fits two people. It’s crafted with care from Canadian hemlock and nontoxic adhesives, so you don’t worry about heating up microplastics and absorbing that into your skin. Esquire executive editor, Madison Vain, had the BeautyBox installed in her basement and it’s since become a major part of her routine.

“I cannot prove that my LIT BeautyBox kept me any healthier than, say, 30-minute meditation sessions or a regular wine date with friends,” she wrote. “But meditation doesn’t make you sweat, and as good as they say socializing is for the body, I think we can all assume heat therapy does a bit more. All I know for sure is that once I stopped using the sauna, its absence felt profound.”.

Sources indicate that if you ask around on Reddit and the other places where (non-bot) people still hang out, Sun Home makes the best infrared saunas. They can get expensive for the full IR treatment, so most knowledgeable folks seem to recommend the Solstice instead. It only uses far-infrared beams, so it’s hitting your body on fewer wavelengths. You’ll get better coverage from full-spectrum, but the amount of heat and sweat should be about the same either way, since that’s coming from the far-infrared.

The Solstice 1 only seats one, but you can pay more for larger versions, with the largest having the capacity for four people with the Solstice 4. Whichever you pick, they are all made from eucalyptus and low-VOC (volatile organic compound) materials. And they all come with speakers installed that you can connect your phone to via Bluetooth and stream in your favorite Spotify playlists.

If you’re a DIY king, or live with one, you might just want to order something from Amazon; this is the most popular and well-reviewed option. I can’t say I can speak to it beyond that. It does basic far-infrared heating (not full spectrum) between 115 and 135 degrees. The look isn’t half bad either, as it’s made using natural hemlock wood. It’s also got a pair of built-in speakers that you can connect to with a 3.5mm aux cord, or more likely, Bluetooth.

It has been revealed that the most common complaint among customers is that the assembly isn’t as straightforward as they would like. That’s a fair critique, but your time is a small price to pay when you look at how much money this option saves compared to others. Besides that, while the listing advertises it as roomy enough for two, there seems to be customer consensus that it runs on the small side. Depending on your height this could be a no-go, or it might just mean you’ll want to make sure you’re close with someone before taking them in the sauna.

If you just can’t do the full-on sauna, okay, we hear you. Higherdose makes this blanket for people who want a solo, easy-to-store sauna alternative. It’s a single-person alternative that uses the same far infrared to detoxify and relax. When you’re done, it can be folded up like any other yoga mat. And it’s only $700, which you’ll realize is a steal once you move on from weekly use to never wanting to miss a day.

Latest Update: Everything You Missed From Inside the Governors Awards

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that awards season is officially underway.
  • After posing for photos on the step-and-repeat, celebrities made their way to the reception just outside the Ray Dolby Ballroom, where the crowd quickly grew shoulder-to-shoulder.
  • According to recent reports, servers weaved through the sea of guests, offering trays of savory bites, including mini burgers, pierogies, tuna cones, and dates stuffed with goat cheese and pistachios.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that awards season is officially underway. On Sunday night, Hollywood’s biggest names gathered at the Ray Dolby Ballroom at Ovation Hollywood for the 17th annual Governors Awards, hosted by the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences. The star-studded evening celebrated extraordinary achievements and contributions to the film industry, honoring Floyd Norman, Glenn Close, and Ridley Scott, as well as Christine Vachon and Pamela Koffler, who received the Irving G. Thalberg Memorial Award.

After posing for photos on the step-and-repeat, celebrities made their way to the reception just outside the Ray Dolby Ballroom, where the crowd quickly grew shoulder-to-shoulder. Nathan Fielder was among the first to arrive, chatting with fellow guests about his outfit for the evening: a midnight-blue Armani tuxedo. Soon after, a beaming Parker Posey made her entrance in a black lace-and-mesh ensemble, accompanied by Martin McDonagh and Sarah Finn, with whom she recently worked on the new comedy-thriller Wild Horse Nine.

According to recent reports, servers weaved through the sea of guests, offering trays of savory bites, including mini burgers, pierogies, tuna cones, and dates stuffed with goat cheese and pistachios. Close paused to examine the latter, asking one server, “What is that tiny little thing?” Though the legendary actress ultimately passed on the appetizer, the interaction appeared to make the staff member’s day, as the server couldn’t help but smile.

It has been revealed that around 5:45 p.m., an announcement over the loudspeaker signaled for guests to make their way into the ballroom, where dinner would soon be served. Charles Melton lingered at the reception a little longer, chatting with a group that included actress Piper Curda. Inde Navarrette, meanwhile, settled in early, as a waiter poured her a glass of white wine.

Emmy Rossum made her way inside just as the five-minute warning was declared, squeezing past Elizabeth Debicki and Carla Gugino, who were deep in conversation. Among the last to enter the ballroom were husband-and-wife duo Zendaya and Tom Holland, who walked hand in hand.

Upon taking their seats, attendees were greeted with an assortment of appetizers, including smoked salmon oscar matzah, fennel-crusted seared tuna on confit potato, spicy carrot hummus on pumpernickel, and a wagyu carpaccio roll with winter vegetables.

Lynette Howell Taylor, president of the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences, was the first to address the room. “Take a look at the five artists we’re honoring here tonight,” she began, sparking a round of applause. “When we think about their extraordinary careers, it’s easy to see the great films, the iconic performances, and the groundbreaking achievements. What we don’t always see are the years of determination behind them, the risks that didn’t pay off, the doors that didn’t open, and the moments when it would have been easier to take a different path. And yet, they kept going, and that is something that should be awarded.”.

Sources indicate that following her remarks, dinner was served: pan-roasted chicken with truffle velouté, roasted heirloom carrots, and potato purée. Guests sipped on a selection of wines throughout the evening, including La Clarté de Haut-Brion, Le Dragon de Quintus, and Piper-Heidsieck Champagne.

Norman was the first honoree of the evening, with Mahershala Ali presenting him with an honorary award. “I am so deeply honored to present the first award tonight to a pioneering animator, story artist, and writer who has been creating exceptional work for more than 70 years, the great Floyd Norman,” the two-time Oscar-winning actor remarked.

In a recent development, during his acceptance speech, Norman reflected on his childhood and the pivotal role his parents played in nurturing his passion for film. “I was a lucky kid because my mom and dad often took me to the movie theater, and those times gave me the education I needed,” he recalled. “In that darkened theatrical classroom, I was just learning the language of film. Somehow, even at that young age, I absorbed the excellent storytelling techniques of lighting, composition, the effective use of sound and music from the Hollywood masters, and seeing on screen what they created in the Hollywood Dream Factory gave me my own dream to become a filmmaker.”.

John Malkovich then took the stage to present Close with her honorary award. The actress appeared visibly emotional as she approached the podium, though the mood swiftly turned lighthearted when she stumbled over her words while reading from the teleprompter, drawing laughter from the room. “What is that? Wait, put it down the other way. Oh, okay, I got it now!” she exclaimed.

Sources indicate that like Norman, Close looked back on her upbringing, revealing that she was “under the thumb of a restrictive cult” from ages seven to 22. “Don’t look at yourself in the mirror. No flirting. Dress this way. Talk this way,” she recalled of the rules she was expected to follow.

Recent findings suggest that after leaving the cult, Close enrolled at the College of William & Mary as a 22-year-old freshman, and she soon found her calling in the theater department. “It was like water on the desert, the revelation and the deep sense of purpose and fulfillment that started to bud when I stepped onto the stage of Phi Beta Kappa Hall has led me directly to this very moment in this room.”.

Recent findings suggest that next to take the stage was Matt Damon, playfully poking fun at Scott who accepted his award remotely. “Gladiator, Black Hawk Down, Alien: Covenant—these are just three extraordinary Ridley Scott films that he did not cast me in, and I was totally available,” the actor joked, drawing laughter from the room. “All is forgiven though, as I did get to make The Martian with him.”.

Industry observers note that while accepting his first Oscar, Scott paid a heartfelt tribute to his late brother, Tony. “Now past 80, I’ve thought about those days and moments and it does resonate, it seems like yesterday, both of us sharing our first film together,” he recalled. “I’m flattered and proud to accept this award, and I also accept it for Tony.”.

Last but certainly not least, producers Christine Vachon and Pamela Koffler were honored with the Irving G. Thalberg Memorial Award, presented by Julianne Moore—dressed in Bottega Veneta—and Todd Haynes. Before presenting the award, however, the duo had a surprise in store for the audience: a performance by Neil Patrick Harris, who sang “The Origin of Love” from Hedwig and the Angry Inch, a film produced by Vachon and Koffler.

In a recent development, “Tonight’s honorees, your speeches were so incredible,” Vachon began, kicking off their acceptance speech. “We were sitting there going, ‘Oh no! We’re just producers, guys.’” She then turned her attention to her decades-long collaboration with Koffler. “Pam and I have been making movies together for over 30 years. Our longevity and endurance are owed to a few factors: very hard work, plenty of really good luck, and working with the absolute best people, and of course our partnership.”.

Industry observers note that koffler then took a moment to look back on their early days working together. “We decided to call ourselves Killer Films. An ethos emerged in those early years, and it has guided the company from day one to champion voices we believe in, stories we love, with a pragmatism that enables them to actually exist.” And just like that, the ceremony came to an end. If the evening was any indication, though, Hollywood is in for a memorable awards season.

Christine Vachon and Pamela Koffler.

#19782. Robert Pattinson Will Make a Bold, Dangerous, and Entirely Original 007

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 10m • 📚 Deep Dive (1978 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Esquire ↗ Open Full Page

Robert Pattinson Will Make a Bold, Dangerous, and Entirely Original 007

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1978 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Esquire

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • James Bond’s greatest weakness is not megalomaniacal madmen bent on world domination.
  • It has been revealed that that’s why Robert Pattinson’s casting as filmmaker Denis Villeneuve’s fresh 007 is a bold and promising choice.
  • Some things shouldn’t change, like his seductiveness, the Walther PPK, and the way he likes his martinis to be shaken.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

James Bond’s greatest weakness is not megalomaniacal madmen bent on world domination. Those he can handle. The superspy is far more likely to be taken down by well-meaning committees.

It has been revealed that that’s why Robert Pattinson’s casting as filmmaker Denis Villeneuve’s fresh 007 is a bold and promising choice. The two of them together have amassed enough industry clout to craft the character their own way, to make him distinctive and daring in a way, hopefully, that we haven’t seen before.

Some things shouldn’t change, like his seductiveness, the Walther PPK, and the way he likes his martinis to be shaken. But those things only make up the silhouette of James Bond. Each actor must put his own imprint on the core of Ian Fleming’s debonair secret agent, just as the author did in his original novels. Sean Connery added ruggedness to the savoir faire. George Lazenby gave him a soulful vulnerability in his solo outing as the character. Roger Moore sharpened 007’s sense of humor. Each actor leaves his fingerprints behind as he hands it off to the next.

This leads to the essential question for anyone signing up to play James Bond: Are you strong enough to stand out?

It’s not so easily answered. I’ll let Timothy Dalton, my personal favorite Bond, explain: “I have some good friends from the Bond days, some really good people, but they’re trapped. Everyone’s trapped by it in a way,” he told me. “Whoever does it has got to have a very clear sense of what they want to achieve, because everybody in the world has got a different opinion about it.”.

To figure out what comes next, we should look back at what came before.

Dalton (who happens to be Christopher Nolan’s favorite Bond too) made that comment to me back in February 2025, when Amazon MGM Studios first acquired the rights to the 007 character.

It has been revealed that when he first took on the role in 1987’s The Living Daylights, his choice was to add a renegade wolf quality. But he also recognized that James Bond must remain, ultimately, the good guy, and that movie was entirely defined by an act of mercy. Fleming’s short story “The Living Daylights” makes up the film’s opening scene: Bond has been sent to take out an enemy sniper, but when he sees that his target is a beautiful cellist (played by Maryam d’Abo), he aims his own rifle to distract her rather than kill her.

Sources indicate that he then becomes responsible for her life, and his 007 has no problem cutting down any foes who block their paths. Dalton’s Bond was more polished than Connery and less comedic than Moore, but he was led by a kind of stormy passion. He had heart, but it pumped cold blood.

Still, Dalton had to break through that formidable wall of consensus. Bond is not a solo enterprise, of course. The director has a say, as do the producers and the screenwriters, but the danger comes from two places: the studio and the audience itself. As Dalton said, “Everybody in the world has got a different opinion about it,” and those voices have to be defied, just as his 007 refused the order to place a bullet in the enemy cellist’s heart.

Sources indicate that nothing makes hands wring and sweat pour in a studio conference room like something unexpected, and know-it-all supposed “fans” often resist change while paradoxically demanding something fresh and new. He had two outings as Bond, the second being 1989’s License to Kill, in which 007 goes even more rogue, defying Her Majesty’s secret service to embark on a mission of revenge. Then the character became tied up in rights lawsuits for several years, and Dalton chose not to return.

In a recent development, when Daniel Craig took over 007 from Pierce Brosnan in 2005, purists complained about his blue eyes and blond hair. When they finally saw him bring the character to life in 2006’s Casino Royale, those critics soon fell silent. Craig gave Bond a soldier’s mindset. He was a battlefield veteran whose latest uniform happens to be a dashing suit. He was successful for so long because as he added his own spin, he capitalized on the best of what came before: He was as rough as Connery and as lethal as Dalton. The humor and playfulness that defined Moore and Brosnan were still present, but they served as a mask for the kind of wounded vulnerability that Lazenby had introduced.

Pattinson is now free to pick and choose whatever qualities he likes from this Brotherhood of Bond, but if he is going to take anyone’s advice, it should be Dalton’s: “Whoever does it has got to have a very clear sense of what they want to achieve.”.

Recent findings suggest that fortunately, no one tells Villeneuve what to do. The filmmaker has spent two decades establishing himself not just as a distinctive artist but as a reliable box-office draw. Those two qualities give him a powerful weapon—clout—that can stave off the onslaught of opinions that will inevitably surround this casting choice.

Just this Saturday, I moderated a Q&A with Villeneuve at the Golden Globe Foundation before an audience of students, and one young filmmaker named Oscar Flores asked the Dune filmmaker, “When is the right time for you to listen to feedback, and when is the right time to listen to yourself?”.

According to recent reports, villeneuve gave an answer that perfectly matches Dalton’s advice and increases my optimism about his approach to Bond: “Honestly, people say that I’m humble, but that’s bullshit,” he mentioned, only partly joking. “If I’m asking for $200 million for a movie, what kind of humility is that?”.

Industry observers note that the suggestion he made to the students was to not take on projects that are outside their control. Start small, stay true, and build up your skill set behind the camera while establishing a reputation that gives you defining power over the movies you make. He warned them not to follow the “siren” song of a big-budget offer if it means ceding control. Instead, Villeneuve stated, he found it effective to build up his status with smaller films, moving from 2010’s more intimate Incendies to 2013’s harrowing Prisoners and 2015’s even more sprawling Sicario before leveling up in scale to 2016’s Arrival and 2017’s Blade Runner 2049.

“The thing that I did when I was a young filmmaker is that I tried not to jump steps,” he told us at the Golden Globes Foundation forum. “I went step-by-step on projects. I was able to keep control of them. I was making sure that I was in control of the tools, and control of the language, and getting strong with the crew, being able to and making sure that my voice would be heard. … What I will say to you is: Be careful of the sirens.”.

It has been revealed that only after amassing this authority, Villeneuve noted, did he feel the time was right to take on his dream project of Dune. “If you made a successful first feature film that cost $200,000 and they offer you a major blockbuster, be careful,” he said this weekend. “Be careful who you are working with, and don’t listen to your ego. Do you really believe that you have the skills to bring it to the screen? Maybe you do. Some people can, by the way. I was not ready to make Dune after my second [film]. ... It took me a lot of movies before I knew that I was able to handle the pressure and making sure that I would be able to control totally, 100 percent, the film. At the end of the day when I look at the movie and the screen, it’s my movie.”.

No doubt Pattinson’s casting was his decision, and Villeneuve’s status ensured it was accepted by the powers that be at Amazon MGM Studios. It probably wasn’t a difficult yes, given that Pattinson is currently in his prime. Not only is he The Batman, but he stood out as the conniving usurper Antinous in Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey and has earned accolades for his haunting performance as a predator-hunting journalist in Primetime.

Is he a heartthrob? Ask the legion of Twilight fans, and cover your ears for their deafening reply.

In a recent development, pattinson forged his bond with Villeneuve with another upcoming role in Dune: Part Three, playing the Face Dancer Scytale. He’s a shape-shifting psychological assassin who seeks to undermine Timothée Chalamet’s all-seeing, all-powerful emperor by getting inside his head, and the actor and filmmaker worked closely to figure out the look, mannerisms, and motivations of a creature void of form.

Industry observers note that as Pattinson said in a recent cover story I wrote for Empire magazine about Dune: Part Three: “I went into it being like, ‘I want to look like an alien,’ and initially Denis was saying, ‘Well, I think he’s got to fit in with everybody. I think he just looks like you. He’s normal,’ ” Pattinson said. The actor was candid about his own reaction: “I was a little bit disappointed.”.

According to recent reports, then Villeneuve thought about it some more. As the director told those students on Saturday, he has a strong point of view, but it’s not inflexible. Villeneuve is not interested in the whims of a crowd, but he is very open to suggestions from creative partners. If their own insights open his eyes to a possibility he hadn’t considered, he will seize upon the ideas.

Sources indicate that shortly before shooting, Villeneuve reversed course on Scytale, and Pattinson said the filmmaker sent him an email with a latest look for the Face Dancer. Pale skin, white hair, no eyebrows, which has the effect of making his expressions somewhat inscrutable. In other words, a blank page, upon which the characteristics of others can be written as he shifts his own natural shape. Pattinson said he felt relief: “I’m like, ‘Okay, this is very much not like a normal guy at all.’ ”.

Sources indicate that this anecdote is meaningful for 007 because it demonstrates that the filmmaker and the star can share ideas, experiment and explore, and listen to each other. That’s the collaboration this character needs.

Sources indicate that at 40, Pattinson is not the youngest possible Bond, but he brings life experience that will be vital for playing a character who needs a certain prowess and wisdom to survive. He and Villeneuve both have a kind of double-0 swagger that will allow them to ignore the cacophonous advice of the masses and devise something original.

It has been revealed that pattinson has been doing this for a long time. Consider his doomed Cedric Diggory in 2005’s Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire, another character—like Bond, Bruce Wayne, and Edward Cullen—who exists as an intense, preexisting image in the minds of millions of fans. But with his brooding presence, he added uncertainty to Cedric’s innate decency and fair-mindedness. The kid who dramatically hops down from a tree in his jump-scare introduction to Ron and Harry could very well have been there to bully them. That’s a sneak-attack entrance, proposed by Pattinson himself, and little details like that gave this upright, wholesome character a dose of intrigue.

Pattinson was only 17 when he filmed that. In the more than two decades that followed, he has paid his dues, learned his lessons, and no doubt gotten his share of scars. With Villeneuve backing him, he’s bulletproof. The two of them can take chances, be bold, and defy orders—just like 007 would, just as playing the character demands.

Pattinson is not a paper doll that will fold when the committees come for James Bond.

The Data Highlights It: The Faux-Fur-Trimmed Coat Is the Coat of the Season

📅 15 Jan 2024 | ⏱️ 4 min read (866 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vogue

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A very specific coat has taken the internet and fashion people alike by storm.
  • Sources indicate that with searches for the designer up 967% on The RealReal, vintage dealers racing to list their versions, and creatives DIYing it at home, it’s safe to call this the coat of the season.
  • It has been revealed that “The coat taps into a growing appetite for pieces that feel expressive and one of a kind, qualities that have always made vintage compelling,” says Noelle Sciacca, head of fashion at The RealReal.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A very specific coat has taken the internet and fashion people alike by storm. Conner Ives’s robe coat looks like a piece pulled from a 1920s opera-house coat check, and everyone from Sienna Miller to Zoë Kravitz has worn iterations of it. First introduced in his fall 2025 collection, it pairs antique silk with reclaimed fox at the lapels and cuffs, and sells for a cool $9,000. And it’s in extremely high demand.

Sources indicate that with searches for the designer up 967% on The RealReal, vintage dealers racing to list their versions, and creatives DIYing it at home, it’s safe to call this the coat of the season. While the Ives version might top many of our wish lists (and budgets), its essence is rooted in the feeling of a bygone era—maybe one we’re craving more than ever these days, if the style is any indication.

It has been revealed that “The coat taps into a growing appetite for pieces that feel expressive and one of a kind, qualities that have always made vintage compelling,” says Noelle Sciacca, head of fashion at The RealReal. “We’re seeing a real shift toward everyday opulence, rich textures, and a sense of history. The Conner Ives coat captures that mood. It feels glamorous and eccentric but still effortless enough to throw over jeans.”.

It has been revealed that the proof for demand is in the data. According to Sciacca, searches for fur-trimmed jackets and coats are up 33% year over year, while jacquard searches have increased 60% and tapestry prints have surged 170%. “What’s great is shoppers don’t necessarily need the exact coat to capture the look,” Sciacca indicates. “They’re exploring vintage and archival pieces across designers and decades, looking for ornate prints, beautiful fabrics, and unexpected details.”.

Recent findings suggest that retailers are also swiftly catching on with similar-style coats from Ciao Lucia, Rixo, Dôen, and Maison Essentiele selling out within days of appearing live on their sites. “I had a gut feeling that it [the Taimi Satin Bouquet coat] would be a top seller,” Lucy Akin, founder of Ciao Lucia, shares. “It was validating to not only see it sell out so quickly but also have my entire Instagram feed flooded with these vintage-inspired jackets. They are having a moment, no doubt!”.

Stylist Bailey Moon echoes this. “I think there’s a real appetite for clothes that have personality again,” he says. “The Conner Ives coat taps into a sense of nostalgia, but it also feels playful and a little irreverent, which I think is part of its appeal.” That’s also what separates it from the Penny Lane coat. While that style reads bohemian and casual, this one trades suede for silk and leans closer to eveningwear, so the rest of the outfit has less to do.

In a recent development, “Fur and shearling inherently have a sense of drama, so I prefer to let the coat be the centerpiece and keep everything else relatively understated,” Moon shares. “A great pair of trousers, beautiful knitwear, or even a simple dress can make the look feel incredibly modern. I love the contrast of something quite extravagant paired with something very utilitarian.”.

Laura Harrier in a short Conner Ives coat.

In a recent development, but the appeal extends beyond ornament. Memory and timelessness play a part too. Nour Hammour’s Sima coat was designed after founder Hammour’s grandmother’s coat and the way her grandmother carried herself in it. “It is the balance between exceptional materials, craftsmanship, and a silhouette that will remain relevant long after the season has passed,” shares marketing director Zeina El Zein Hammour. “The quality of the shearling, the depth of the trim, and the way the coat falls on the body are what distinguish a piece that you’ll keep for decades.”.

For vintage hounds, it’s also a real marker of the shift away from all-neutral everything that’s dominated for so long. “After years of quiet luxury and minimalism, I think people are ready for a little romance and extravagance,” says Susan Kim of Estella NYC, who sells similar vintage iterations on her site and at vintage fairs.

Kendall Jenner wearing a Conner Ives duster.

According to recent reports, secondhand enthusiast and influencer Katie Casper tried her hand at re-creating the coat using pieces she already owned: a Shanghai Tang silk jacket from her mother-in-law and a removable fur stole from an old Zara coat. “In its simplest terms, the coat is a colorful brocade base with a fur trim,” she indicates. “Both are easy to source secondhand.” The trickiest part was proportion, since the stole overpowered the jacket; she said she’d choose a narrower one next time.

It has been revealed that whether the style lasts beyond this season is another question. “I fear we may all be a little exhausted by 2027,” Casper muses. But Moon sees it differently. “A beautiful statement coat can live in someone’s wardrobe for years,” he indicates. “The question is whether you’re buying it because you genuinely love it or because you’ve seen it on everyone else. The best clothes should still feel exciting to wear long after they’ve stopped being the thing everyone is talking about.”.
