📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Yesterday, in the wake of Friday’s grounding of all flights in the continental United States and the weekend of cancellations and chaos that ensued, Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy made the rounds of the Sunday-morning political talk shows to make this face.

According to recent reports, it’s been a tough few days for Duffy, and Duffy has been huffy. From Friday’s press conference with Markwayne Mullin, to his own microphonically challenged solo outing on Saturday, through all five morning-show appearances, Duffy has checked all the boxes the modern Republican official must: look aggrieved, place blame elsewhere, praise the president, be white. It’s all television, after all, and there’s a role to be played.

Industry observers note that sean Duffy has been at this for decades. You know he was on the sixth season of The Real World, and you know he met his wife and fellow Real Worlder Rachel Campos when they participated in an early season of what would become The Real World/Road Rules Challenge. But when you really go back and look, you’ll see that they’ve both been practicing for this moment since the ’90s. Game recognizes game; as a fellow alumnus of 20th-century MTV, let me walk you through it.

Sources indicate that the Real World was born when MTV decided to try its hand at creating a weekly soap opera, in the style of the era-defining Beverly Hills 90210 and Melrose Place. But cable budgets being what they are, a full scripted show was untenable, so producers had the bold idea to do away with actors and writers entirely. The first couple seasons of The Real World kept the focus on art by casting young artists: Julie the emerging dancer amid the model and writer and singer-songwriters in season 1, Jon the wannabe Garth Brooks in season 2. But that went out the window quick, as producers and aspiring castmates figured out the same thing at the same time: The job was to stir the pot. So by season 3, deeply unpleasant bike messenger Puck was dropped into the San Francisco house to clash with saintly AIDS educator Pedro, with whom conservative Rachel initially refused to share a bathroom for fear of sink-based HIV transmission. In 1994.

By season 6, casts seemed chosen specifically to play a predetermined part and drive each other up the wall. Real World: Boston features Stanford med student Kameelah and ladies man Syrus, Catholic Texan Elka and Manhattan-born mess on wheels Montana. And then there was Sean Duffy, Wisconsin boy, lumberjack-games participant, and future secretary of transportation. Sean occupied the Cute Boy spot in the cast that had been held by Aaron in Los Angeles and St. Louis race car driver Mike in London. But this being 1997, he was also a different cultural archetype: the knee-jerk Rush Limbaugh–era conservative. Accent on jerk. Here’s a moment when Sean makes fun of Elka’s underwear and then immediately denies it.

Recent findings suggest that just straight-up, reflexively, smoothly denying he did something we just saw him do, because he did it on camera and into a microphone. Lying with a straight face. This would become a job skill.

According to recent reports, it’s a little like something we saw Sean’s future wife Rachel do on her season. In an early episode, she engages in the hot, safe rebellious act of 1994 by getting her navel pierced. In a later episode, she gets a telephone call from her angry mother, who has seen the belly-button bauble in a photograph (a physical photograph, sent through the U.S. Mail—again, we lived differently in the ’90s). Rachel assures her mother it’s not a piercing but instead a sticker she put there. Forget the fact that, again, all of this is on camera and the mom is going to learn the truth soon enough. Watching back then, I remember thinking two things: One, this person lies very easily, and two, I think she might be one of those people who’s conservative just so they don’t upset their parents.

In a recent development, anyway. Sean and Rachel did The Challenge and got married and had three hundred and fifty children. Sean became a congressman for Wisconsin; Rachel tried out for The View but never quite nailed it and now she’s on Fox & Friends sometimes. And because it all comes back to reality television and personal branding, the Duffy family spent a few weeks of Sean’s tenure as secretary of transportation to film a show. The Great American Road Trip was supposed to have aired on Fox Nation, but instead it got dumped onto YouTube, where most episodes are hovering around 10k views.

According to recent reports, also, Duffy’s son-in-law Michael Alfonso, who’s 26, is set to become the youngest person in Congress, having won a seat in Wisconsin’s 7th District in this month’s elections. Alfonso’s campaign was buoyed by generous campaign donations from numerous transportation companies, executives, and lobbyists, including a $2,500 contribution from Air Space Intelligence’s PAC in March. In June, the FAA awarded the AI start-up a contract worth up to $875.95 million. The firm’s SMART system went nationwide days before the November 13 ground stop, though the FAA and the company said the outage was unrelated to SMART.

Industry observers note that I’m sure it’s nothing. But I’m even more sure Duffy will say it is.

In a recent development, the way that John F. Kennedy understood television in the way Richard Nixon did not, Sean Duffy understands reality television in a way few others do. He’s lived it. He understands it as a marketing exercise. Knowing your brand, hitting the beats of the scene you’re supposed to play, showing up with a yearbook picture-day haircut and lying with a smile will get you far in this world. Whether he survives this turbulence or not, he’s learned that lesson.

In a recent development, sean and Rachel have been at this for decades, but as viewers so have we. We can see them as they are: dishonest children, playing a role, begging for approval, just trying not to get yelled at.

What Is a Golden Retriever Boyfriend? Everything to Know About the Internet's Favorite Partner

📅 31 Jul 2025 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1208 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cosmopolitan

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • We may earn commission from links on this page, but we only recommend products we love.
  • There are two kinds of people in the dating world: those who think waiting three hours to text back makes them mysterious, and those who would happily text you three times in a row just because they saw a dog that reminded them of you.
  • Sources indicate that if you've spent any time on Dating TikTok, you've likely encountered the golden retriever boyfriend (or GRBF), a term for the kind of guy who's affectionate, enthusiastic, and almost aggressively happy to be in a relationship with you.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We may earn commission from links on this page, but we only recommend products we love. Promise.

There are two kinds of people in the dating world: those who think waiting three hours to text back makes them mysterious, and those who would happily text you three times in a row just because they saw a dog that reminded them of you. The latter? Probably a golden retriever boyfriend.

Sources indicate that if you've spent any time on Dating TikTok, you've likely encountered the golden retriever boyfriend (or GRBF), a term for the kind of guy who's affectionate, enthusiastic, and almost aggressively happy to be in a relationship with you. Think Travis Kelce with Taylor Swift. Subtlety isn't exactly the selling point.

Sources indicate that “A golden retriever boyfriend is the human equivalent of a tail wagging, wide-eyed pup who lives to love you,” explains Tiff Baira, relationship expert, matchmaker, “Streethearts” host, and author of Modern Dating for Dummies. “He’s sweet, loyal, emotionally available, and basically imprinted on you after the third date.”.

Which, after one too many situationships with men who consider responding to a text an act of vulnerability, sounds pretty damn appealing. But is having a boyfriend who worships the ground you walk on always as great as TikTok makes it look? Not necessarily. Here's what experts want you to know about golden retriever boyfriends, including how to spot one and why all that devotion isn't automatically a recipe for relationship bliss.

“A golden retriever boyfriend is loving, positive, energetic, loyal, and uncomplicated,” notes matchmaker and dating coach Blaine Anderson, founder of Dating By Blaine.

In a recent development, “He remembers your coffee order, sends good morning texts unprompted, and genuinely enjoys helping you build IKEA furniture,” adds Baira. “He’s not playing games; he’s the overly nice and caring type who puts you before himself.”.

Recent findings suggest that sounds like the dream, right? Mostly. While the golden retriever boyfriend is known for being easygoing and devoted, that same enthusiasm can sometimes mean he's a little too eager to please.

“There may also be an undertone of ‘nice guy,’—specifically as opposed to ‘bad boy’—perhaps implying the golden retriever boyfriend is the guy you settle with after having your heart broken by a bad boy,” Anderson adds. Still, the term is generally a compliment. “You date the golden retriever guy because you don’t want to waste time on moody losers,” says Anderson.

As for how the trend got started? “The term ‘golden retriever boyfriend’ definitely gained traction on TikTok, where women proudly indicated off their partners as the ultimate romantic prize,” Baira explains. “These were the guys who happily did whatever their girlfriend said.”.

Recent findings suggest that and in an era of dating app burnout and doomscrolling, “golden retriever boyfriends became a symbol of hope in a dating landscape flooded with horror stories,” claims Baira. “Amid all that chaos, the GRBF became a mythical figure—an aspirational fantasy. Someone who might actually treat you like the princess you are.”.

Recent findings suggest that “If you’re wondering whether you’re with a golden retriever boyfriend, the signs are usually wagging right in front of you,” notes Baira. “He lights up when he sees you, offers to carry your bag without being asked, and says, ‘let me know when you get home’ like it’s a sacred ritual.” In short, “There are no games, no ego—just someone who wants to be near you, build with you, and see you shine.”.

Recent findings suggest that on the flip side: “Does he make you worry he’s cheating? Have you come to expect he won’t buy you dinner? Does he only text at 10pm?” asks Anderson. In that case, “you do not have a golden retriever boyfriend!”.

Sources indicate that of course, not every guy who seems like a golden retriever boyfriend actually is one. Enter “the wolf in golden retriever clothing—the guy who seems endlessly kind and selfless but secretly has an agenda,” says Baira. “If his niceness comes with strings attached, like using your connections, expecting money, or subtly manipulating you, he’s not golden; he’s gold plated.”.

Industry observers note that in other words, “Sometimes the nice guy isn’t actually nice at all,” Baira adds. “If he makes you feel like you owe him for his kindness or if his affection feels performative or transactional, that’s a clear sign it’s not real golden retriever energy.”.

Some other red flags signaling you may be with a fake golden retriever? “He’s only sweet in public, performs affection when people are watching, and suddenly goes cold the second you’re alone,” says Baira. “He expects praise for basic things like texting back or showing up on time. He might flood you with compliments but makes subtle jabs when you're shining too bright.”.

As much as TikTok might make you think golden retriever boyfriends are the end-all, they're not necessarily the right match for everyone.

“While every relationship is nuanced and there’s no universal good or bad, it’s vital to remember that golden retriever energy still needs to match your energy,” notes Baira. “Just because someone is nice to you doesn’t mean they’re right for you.”.

Case in point: The Sex and the City love triangle between Carrie, Major, and Aidan. “On paper, Aidan was everything: warm, loving, emotionally present, always chasing Carrie,” says Baira. “But that’s just it. She didn’t want to be chased; she wanted to be challenged. And no matter how hard she tried to make him the one, he wasn’t.”.

Sources indicate that dating coach Grace Lee, founder of A Good First Date, adds that for some people, golden retriever energy can feel stifling. “Doting affection can breed contempt. At first, it feels amazing to be adored so completely. But over time, you might feel overwhelmed—or even guilty,” she notes. “He’s so focused on making you happy that his own needs seem to disappear.” This can create an unhealthy dynamic where one partner constantly needs space while the other feels underappreciated.

That doesn't mean golden retriever boyfriends are inherently bad partners. It just means being nice isn't the same thing as being compatible, and staying in a relationship because it feels safe isn't necessarily the same as being happy in it.

Lee also warns that the Very Online nature of the golden retriever boyfriend trend can create unrealistic expectations, encouraging people to play a specific role in their relationships rather than address their actual needs.

“The hashtag acts as a checklist—for both the boyfriend and the girlfriend,” notes Lee. “If you’re a GRBF, that means you’re a ‘good boyfriend.’ And if you’re a good boyfriend, then you don’t have to worry about the relationship falling apart. You’ve met the criteria. You’re safe from rejection. On the flip side, having a GRBF is proof that you’re desirable. You must be the kind of person who deserves that level of devotion. Instead of confronting your insecurities, you point to the list.”.

Recent findings suggest that ultimately, a golden retriever boyfriend can absolutely be a great partner. But a relationship doesn't automatically work just because it checks all the right boxes on TikTok. What matters is whether you're actually happy together, not whether your boyfriend fits the internet's favorite dating archetype.

Tech Report: Our 10 Favorite Men’s Fisherman Sweaters to Wear All Winter

📅 25 Feb 2025 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1025 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Esquire

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, we love fisherman sweaters for the same reason we love a great martini: They’re classic, and they’re comforting.
  • Industry observers note that now, it’s crucial to remember that when it comes to the backstory of most garments, there tends to be a lot of lore mixed in with the genuine history.
  • Industry observers note that in 2026, you probably don’t need a fisherman sweater to keep you warm while you’re on the water off Ireland’s west coast.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, we love fisherman sweaters for the same reason we love a great martini: They’re classic, and they’re comforting. A proper fisherman knit brings the whole winter wardrobe into alignment. The chunky texture instantly upgrades jeans and boots, warmth doesn’t sacrifice style, and that easy, rugged-prep vibe that works at the office as well as it does on the couch. In other words, it’s the rare cold-weather staple that’s as practical as it is handsome.

Industry observers note that now, it’s crucial to remember that when it comes to the backstory of most garments, there tends to be a lot of lore mixed in with the genuine history. That said, here’s how the story generally goes. Traditional fisherman sweaters hail from Ireland, where in the late 1800s to the mid-1900s, they were popular for men who had to work long hours on fishing boats. Usually, fisherman sweaters were hand-knit by their wives or by local artisans, and they were always designed to be sturdy and warm, keeping the wind and chill out. Cable-knit patterns became popular for fisherman sweaters. You might know these sweaters as Aran sweaters, referencing the Aran Islands, where the textured design has become a specialty.

Industry observers note that in 2026, you probably don’t need a fisherman sweater to keep you warm while you’re on the water off Ireland’s west coast. (Or maybe you do! We don’t know your story.) However, you do need a fisherman sweater for the sheer coziness and looks they provide, though. Our favorite options of all time are below, tested and reviewed by Esquire editors (with some photographed on Esquire’s editor in chief, Michael Sebastian). Anyway, these fisherman sweaters are seriously making us want to take some fishing lessons. Anyone know where we can do that?

You don’t need to break the bank for a high-quality fisherman sweater that’ll last you years to come. Quince is proof. Crafted from organic cotton, this thick, warm sweater is a perfect layering piece for winter—put a tee or a button-down underneath, a topcoat or a puffer on top, and you’re golden. The rib detailing offers some extra texture and style, and relaxed raglan sleeves offer more freedom of movement.

Ok, so the pictured sweater is no longer in stock. The cable knit rollneck was seasonal, but there is always a fisherman-y option in the collection. Honestly, whichever J. Crew rollneck hits this bar at any point in time, that’s likely my favorite fisherman sweater of the moment.

In a recent development, L.L. Bean crafts a classic fisherman sweater to a tee. It has everything you’d want in the style: a thick, heavyweight fabric that carries some structure with it; a cable-knit design; and thick cotton yarn that keeps the chill out and the warmth in. This style is a go-to for something timeless without too much fuss or frill. It has a slim fit, so if you want something baggier, more classically cut, make sure to size up.

Okay, hear me out—this isn’t your traditional fisherman sweater, but you can make a damn good excuse for Polo Ralph Lauren’s ultra-soft, ultra-luxe cable-knit sweater when you feel how unbelievably plush this is. This is the fisherman sweater you go to when you want something distinctly elevated and chic but you still want to have a cable-knit design and a fit you can dress down with joggers and slides.

You may already know that we at Esquire have an affinity for shawl collar cardigans. With their laid-back Western vibes and classic Americana silhouette, shawl collar cardigans look handsome on just about any guy. One of our favorites is this fisherman style from Filson. It’s made from thick, warm cotton and features a classic button front and ribbing on the hem and cuffs.

In a recent development, if you, like commerce editor Luke Guillory, aren’t into the super chunky fisherman sweaters and are looking for something a little more lightweight that you can easily layer, this Buck Mason pick should be right up your alley. Luke has even endorsed the style, lauding the sweater for its warm yet lightweight feel, perfect not-too-boxy but not-too-slim cut, and durable cotton that can be machine washed and still not miss a beat.

In a recent development, this gorgeous wool fisherman sweater is from Finisterre, a surf clothing brand from Cornwall, England, so it’s specifically made for cold, windy days on the water. It’s made from 100 percent heavyweight, pure new wool with a natural crimp, which means it creates natural pockets of air to help insulate you (even if you’re not on the water). One writer states it’s one of his go-to winter sweaters.

According to recent reports, brooks Brothers’ woolly sweater is so damn good I might just have to take up the art of fishing to pay proper tribute to it. With a soft and cozy yet breathable wool fabric and cable-knit pattern, this relaxed style puts a contemporary spin on the traditional fisherman sweater. It’s warm, soft, and stylish, and it looks just as good with dress pants and loafers as it does with jeans and sneakers.

In a recent development, begg x Co’s Isla cashmere sweater is another fantastic, high-quality cashmere option. It’s just oppressively beautiful. Begg x Co operates its own mills in Scotland, which shows up in the world-class materials and construction, but the vibe isn’t overly capital-F-Fashion the way some French or Italian luxury brands can feel. It’s timeless, understated luxury. Made from 8‑ply cashmere, it lands in a perfect mid-weight sweet spot for fall and winter: substantial and warm without being bulky. It’s definitely quite pricey, but you’re paying for the highest level of quality and finish.

Sources indicate that this sweater from Ghiaia Cashmere is divine, surprising considering the brand is based out of southern California. The mock neck is the star here—cozy without the bulk of a turtleneck—and the rich brown color is lovely (though it also comes in a clean cream if you want something lighter). A chest pocket adds a surprisingly practical touch, making it feel more functional than you’d ever expect a sweater to be.

Breaking: I’ve Rejected a Lot of Ballet Flats, But I Can’t Stop Thinking About These Glossy Repetto Pumps

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (849 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cosmopolitan

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that everyone is unreasonable about something, and mine happens to be ballet flats.
  • Reader, I never claimed to be easygoing.
  • The toe is round and delicate without tipping into stumpy.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that everyone is unreasonable about something, and mine happens to be ballet flats. Catch me in a one-on-one for long enough, and I will spew out my long list of grievances, most of which come down to shape. A lot of ballet flats are, to use the technical term, uggo: They cover too much of the foot or too little of it, the toe is square or stumpy or so long it enters the room before I do, and the block heel is cut at an angle when a block heel should be straight and symmetrical, as nature intended. Sometimes the body of the shoe is scrunched up like a shower cap, and sometimes someone goes and puts metal aglets on the bow. The horror!

Reader, I never claimed to be easygoing. But hear me out: Repetto's red patent Camille pumps are the rare pair that cleared the entire list. Repetto is about as iconic as ballet flats get, so the name kept coming up during the several nights I spent researching at 2 a.m. for a pair with a little more dressy oomph. What never came up was a proper deep-dive review of the Camille, so here's mine.

The toe is round and delicate without tipping into stumpy. The block heel is straight on every side. The hull of the shoe, for lack of a better word, is structured but still flexible, so it holds its shape instead of gathering around my foot like a drawstring bag. And there is no hardware anywhere, which feels laid-back and chic in a Parisian way to me and also means they go with whatever jewelry I already have on.

In a recent development, one disclosure: They do show some toe cleave, which I personally like. I'm aware a large portion of the population does not, and to those people I say, respectfully, you do you.

The consensus on Repettos, and the brand's own advice for this pair, is to size up. I went with a 37. For context, I wear a 6 in sneakers, and I've since learned I'm more of a 5.5 in ballet flats and loafers, which is the kind of self-knowledge that arrives exactly one pair too late. They're big on me, and I wish I had trusted my flats size.

I tried the usual fixes. I put in heel grips, then doubled up on heel grips, and they were still too substantial. I pulled the little drawstring to tighten them, which didn't do much besides make the edges wavy. My advice is to go by how you fit in flats specifically, not sneakers, and to buy from somewhere with a return policy you've read all the way through. (Groundbreaking advice, I know.).

Recent findings suggest that the soles are thin—intentionally so. Repetto stitches the sole to the shoe inside out and then flips the whole thing right side out, a technique it has used since 1947. It's meant to make the shoe comfortable, the way a dance slipper is comfortable, soft and flexible enough to bend with your foot. What you don't get is much cushioning or support. It's also not what I'm used to, and not what most ballet pumps feel like. I can feel the ground under me, and I can feel the arch give a little when I walk. If you prefer a sturdier shoe, the Camille also comes with a rubber sole, like the grey-blue pair here. It comes in plenty of colors beyond red too.

Repetto Blue Camille Rubber Sole Heels.

Repetto Red Rose Mary Janes Heels.

Repetto Repetto Taupe Camille Rubber-Sole Heels.

It has been revealed that I won't pretend $475 is a casual amount to spend on a pair of shoes. It's a lot, and whether it's worth it comes down to how much you'll wear them. For me, that's all the time. I mostly wear neutrals, like jeans and a baby tee or an all-black outfit with low-rise trousers, and these are classic enough to go with all of it yet fun enough to carry the whole outfit on their own. The red isn't a seasonal one, either, so they work in November the same way they will in May. That's my idea of a forever wardrobe piece, and by that math, they're worth it.

If that math doesn't work for you, there are other red ballet pumps that clear my list, and several of them cost a lot less.

Shop other ballet pumps I’d consider.

Tech Report: I Have Serious Questions About the 2026 Grammy Nominations

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1665 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Esquire

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Grammys, more than any other awards-voting body of the big EGOT four, is easily the most chaotic.
  • The Recording Academy declared on Monday, November 16, that Kanye West is a Grammy nominee once again.
  • So, before the Grammys decide to ignore all of our desires and complaints and just shower Taylor Swift with more little golden phonographs on February 7, 2027, let’s try to make sense of the 2026 Grammy nominees below.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Grammys, more than any other awards-voting body of the big EGOT four, is easily the most chaotic. Sure, we can shake our fists in the air all day about how Stanley Kubrick somehow never won an Oscar, or ask ourselves why the Tony Awards ever allowed themselves to become a place where SpongeBob SquarePants: The Broadway Musical leads with 12 nominees. But recalling Grammy events like Macklemore beating Kendrick Lamar, Esperanza Spalding claiming Best Fresh Artist over Justin Bieber and Drake, and Beck taking home Album of the Year instead of Beyoncé, it’s a wonder just what happens between when the votes are submitted and when the winners are revealed.

This year? The Recording Academy declared on Monday, November 16, that Kanye West is a Grammy nominee once again. And there’s a single category where Bruce Springsteen, Phoebe Bridgers, and Charli XCX are lumped together, so I guess they’re considered basically the same kind of artist to voters. Plus, new ideas like “Best Asian Pop Music Performance” are moving forward despite immediately losing support from the most prominent artist in that category, and Best New Artist nominees can apparently put out their fifth studio album and still be considered. What’s going on?

So, before the Grammys decide to ignore all of our desires and complaints and just shower Taylor Swift with more little golden phonographs on February 7, 2027, let’s try to make sense of the 2026 Grammy nominees below.

In a recent development, the first thought that entered my mind when I saw this year’s nominees for Album of the Year was, Are we confirming who will be available to perform before announcing the nominees now? Because even if so, I think Bruno Mars would perform either way.

It’s very cool to see how women dominated the music field this year, especially because they truly did. Olivia Rodrigo, Phoebe Bridgers, and Rosalía all earning Album of the Year nominations is a no-brainer. Olivia Dean, who won Best Newly introduced Artist last year, and Ella Langley, who wrote “Choosin’ Texas,” make up the rest of the list. (Did we really love that entire nineteen-track Langley album?) Plus, of course, the obligatory Taylor Swift nominations.

But were Bruno Mars and Leon Thomas—who are tied with seven nominations each after the leading women, including an Album of the Year nod for Mars—the two men with the best offerings this year?

According to recent reports, bruno Mars had a very good song on The Romantic with “Why You Wanna Fight?” The Luther Vandross-esque R&B ballad was everything you’d look for in a Song of the Year nominee. But instead, it looks like Bruno is going all in on “Risk It All” and “I Just Might,” the latter of which is more of a “Happy” by Pharrell Williams-type song that somehow isn’t the lead single of the next Trolls movie.

Industry observers note that sorry Madonna! Apologies Robyn, Tinashe, Slayyter, and every other pop artist who soundtracked our year on the dance floor with some of the best albums of 2026. Breaking into the top four major categories still looks like a no-go.

Instead, Madonna, Robyn, and Tinashe were relegated to categories such as Best Dance Pop Recording and Best Dance/Electronic Album, even despite critical acclaim. If you want a Record of the Year nod, try writing a song for Toy Story 5.

Don Toliver is up for Best Upcoming Artist. The Houston rapper, who was signed to Travis Scott’s label in 2018, released his fifth studio album, Octane, this year. He had a song on the F9 soundtrack in 2021—which isn’t even the latest Fast & Furious movie—and his 2023 album, Love Sick, featured James Blake, Future, and Justin Bieber. But here we are, in 2026, watching him compete for Best New Artist.

According to recent reports, equally puzzling: Remi Wolf is nominated for Best Fresh Artist. The singer’s exceptional debut record, Juno, came out in 2021. And her best record to date, Mud, was released recently on October 9, just outside of the Grammy submission window that closed in late August. But following the logic of how Olivia Dean won Best New Artist last year even though Dean’s album is competing this year, it’s clear that the whole Best New Artist category needs some rethinking.

Recent findings suggest that 2026 wasn’t a banner year for rap. I can admit that. Sure, we had very good records from A$AP Rocky, Denzel Curry, Vince Staples, JPEGMAFIA, Isaiah Rashad, Genesis Owusu, and Baby Keem. But none of the musicians I listed above went recognized this year, except for Keem’s single “Best Rap Performance” nomination.

Instead, the Recording Academy nominated Wale’s Everything Is a Lot—the Washington, D.C., rapper’s best and most mature album of the last decade, but far less influential than Rocky’s or Keem’s releases. And if not for Drake’s long-running boycott, the absence of Iceman’s “Janice STFU” just looks silly. But if you want to talk ridiculous, let’s see how Rap Album of the Year nominee Kanye West plays out for the Recording Academy over the next couple of months.

Harry Styles won Album of the Year for Harry’s House in 2023. He beat out Un Verano Sin Ti by Bad Bunny, Renaissance by Beyoncé, Mr. Morale & the Big Steppers by Kendrick Lamar, and 30 by Adele. It was a major upset. And just last month, the former One Direction member wrapped a historic thirty-night residency at Madison Square Garden in Upcoming York City in support of his latest album, Kiss All the Time. Disco, Occasionally.

Now, I’m not saying Kiss All the Time is a masterwork, but it’s strange that Styles didn’t receive a single nomination for his Harry’s House follow-up. “Aperture” was very catchy! Taylor Swift can’t sneeze without the Recording Academy inventing a new category for her to compete in. But an artist who just won Album of the Year can find himself completely shut out, even if his latest record is a success?

The global K-pop megastars reunited this year following mandatory military service in South Korea for one of the genre’s most-anticipated albums of all time, ARIRANG. The record paid homage to the popular Korean folk song of the same name while also pushing the K-pop genre forward with hip-hop-heavy material. ARIRANG’s fourteen tracks also filled the top fourteen spots of Spotify’s global Top 50 chart on its first day of release on March 20. I’ll stop there, but there are a hundred more ways to say that it was one of the biggest albums of the year.

But when the Recording Academy confirmed a latest category this year, “Best Asian Pop Music Performance,” the group made the decision not to submit for the Grammys this year. The move was widely regarded as a protest of the new category, which many interpreted as a ghettoization to keep the rise of popular Asian acts away from the general field categories. “I hope that music can be heard and loved for what it is, rather than being divided by region or language,” the group posted on social media.

On Monday, November 16, the Academy went through with the category anyway, announcing nominees including Lisa from Blackpink, the Japanese pop-metal group Babymetal, the K-pop group IVE, and the Filipino girl group Bini, among others. But with BTS joining Drake in his boycott of the Grammys, I wonder how the Recording Academy will fare without two of the world’s most popular acts entertaining its awards show.

Recent findings suggest that the Great Divide, a seventeen-track rock album that turned Kahan into one of the most popular touring musicians of 2026, was considered a favorite to receive a nomination in every major category this year. Songs like “American Cars” dealt with past failures and road trip blues, while lead single “The Great Divide” tackled how fame added extra struggles to many of his already-strained relationships. And Kahan had the resume to become a major category contender this year. He had a Number One record! He did the full press tour, he performed on Saturday Night Live, and he sold out stadiums all across the country.

It has been revealed that but it must have been an omen when Kahan sang that “California’s so much more than some awards show” on the deluxe edition’s “Orbiter,” because he received just one nomination on Monday for Best Contemporary Folk Album. It’s a shame.

According to recent reports, best Album Cover is back. The category returned last year and accurately awarded Tyler, the Creator’s zany Chromakopia artwork, which featured the artist wearing a black, ceramic mask. He told Complex at the time that it symbolized how the new music was “so honest, that I think I had to wear a mask of my own face to get some of that sh*t out.”.

But what about this year’s nominees? Well, Mavis Staples’s Sad and Beautiful World artwork depicts the artist sitting at a table. Interpol’s This Mirror Weighs a Ton artwork is a chandelier made of security cameras, and Lily Allen’s West End Girl is a painting of the artist wearing a polka-dot jacket. Are these nominees... the best album covers of the year?

Charli XCX’s photograph of Martin Scorsese, John Cale, and Marc Jacobs was easily the much-talked-about album cover of the year, even though Music, Fashion, Film wasn’t nominated. Olivia Rodrigo’s upside-down swinging for you seem pretty sad for a girl so in love is definitely one of the more memorable covers that come to mind. Same goes for Robyn’s blurry and nude Sexistential photo, the politics behind Kneecap’s Fenian, Thundercat biting his dark leather jacket on the cover of Distracted, or even a pregnant Latto posing with a baby tiger for the Substantial Mama cover ahead of her cheetah-themed baby shower.

We might not have a specific shade of green to color this year and make Best Album Cover an easy choice, but if you’re going to bring the category back? At least wow us.

“Chaats are a mighty snack that tell India’s culinary story more adeptly than any other food,” writes Nashville-based Indian chef Maneet Chauhan in her cookbook Chaat. She reminisces about a fruity street snack sold by a chaat vendor near the Hyderabadi train station. Sweet pineapple, tangy lime juice, sour-salty chaat masala, chile powder, cilantro, and pomegranate seeds created what she describes as “a decadent mosaic of colors and plucky flavors.” Chauhan suggests swapping in ripe mango or watermelon when in season, or drizzling the finished dish with lightly salted yogurt for added richness and depth. Serve as a snack, or as a side dish for barbecued meats or seafood.

In a recent development, every year, the Baby2Baby Gala brings together the biggest names in philanthropy, entertainment, and fashion for an evening of fundraising and celebration. And last night, the 15th edition was no exception—with the likes of Demi Moore, Andrew Garfield, Jessica Alba, Barbara Palvin and Dylan Sprouse, Kerry Washington, and Katy Perry showing up in West Hollywood to support the organization’s mission to help kids in need.

It has been revealed that from the gala’s inception, Baby2Baby co-CEOS Norah Weinstein and Kelly Sawyer Patricof wanted to create an event that felt “less like a traditional fundraiser.” Year after year, the night has offered its star-studded guests more than just an excuse to get dressed up and a chance to make a difference with their wallets—pairing fundraising efforts with exclusive dining experiences from top chefs and intimate performances from award-winning musicians. (Last night, Carbone flew in from Upcoming York City and Cardi B took the stage.).

Industry observers note that “We wanted to create an event that would appeal to a younger generation of donors through our approach to food, fashion, and celebrity, while making sure that nobody left the gala without understanding our mission,” Weinstein and Patricof told Harper’s Bazaar. “Fifteen years later, the gala has evolved in ways we never could have imagined, but some themes have stayed exactly the same. Every flower and fork is underwritten by our generous sponsors so that every dollar raised can go directly to Baby2Baby and the children we serve.”.

Industry observers note that each year, the funds raised from the gala help get millions of basic essentials—from diapers to formula to clothing—to children who need them. But the organization, with an all-female board of directors, spends all year working towards the Baby2Baby mission. “The gala brings this extraordinary community together for one night, but it’s their commitment throughout the year that makes our work possible,” the CEOs shared.

Industry observers note that versatility is the name of the game here. You can dress up any fleece vest with a button-up and breathable chinos, or keep it casual with, say, a long-sleeved tee and some jeans. And really, it’s the only thing that can fit between a bulky sweater and a winter jacket.

In a recent development, wear it open, wear it zipped. Wear it over a long-sleeved tee or a sweater or a button-down; this is the affordable vest that’s ready for anything.

Industry observers note that if you don’t know where to start, I’m going all in on Columbia. With a collared neck and thick, cozy fleece, this top layer is made for chilly days and windy nights.

In a recent development, when you look at vests like this, you think North Face. The Glacier Fleece is an especially light option, perfect for the days when you need more than three layers.

Listen, even I admit that the fleece vest isn’t always the most fashionable choice. And frankly some of them look better zipped up than others. The Pelican and Treeline Green variants of this Patagonia vest are at the top of that list.

  • If you want to smell shower-fresh at all times (who doesn’t?), keep reading to discover team Cosmo’s favorite fresh perfumes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Even though I love writing about fragrance, I don’t necessarily want to smell like perfume. Most of the time I wish the scent of my body wash lasted for hours or that my clothes eternally smelled like I just pulled them out of the dryer. But, as we all know, a majority of those wonderful clean scents disappear in an instant. That’s why I made it my mission to find the dreamiest fresh perfumes.

In a recent development, fresh perfumes typically feature notes like ambroxan and aldehydes (two synthetic compounds that smell, you guessed it, clean and fresh), as well as citrus and musk. They can be aquatic, green, warm, or even floral, but of course, there’s an overarching subtlety about them that fits in this specific family. There's no better smell in the world (to me) than soap, fresh laundry, or simply skin, but "clean" means something different to everyone. That’s why we found an array of fresh perfumes to choose from. Just take a look at some of our faves...

If you want to smell shower-fresh at all times (who doesn’t?), keep reading to discover team Cosmo’s favorite fresh perfumes.

One Cosmo editor states: “Nothing compares to the scent of a mineralic sea breeze, and Jo Malone bottled the essence perfectly. If I close my eyes when I spritz Sea Salt & Bergamot, I’m transported back to the rocky Cornish coast. This perfume is simple in the best way possible. Even though it has just three notes—bergamot, sea salt, and driftwood—it’s completely unforgettable. I’ve gone through a full bottle since it rolled out this summer.”—MARY HONKUS, CONTRIBUTING BEAUTY EDITOR.

One Cosmo editor says: “Alto Astral is simply fresh. (Fitting that it won the Best Fresh Perfume category in our Holy Grail Beauty Awards, right?) It’s clean and light thanks to aldehydes and coconut water, yet it becomes deep and complex with hints of sandalwood and salted amber. If you like to keep things simple, wear it alone. Don’t be afraid to layer with it though! It works with every scent family.”—JASMINE HYMAN, ASSISTANT BEAUTY EDITOR.

One Cosmo editor notes: "Sometimes I want to smell exactly like a bubble. And Replica has, ahem, replicated that fragrance. It's the epitome of squeaky clean. Somehow, this reminds me of being in the tub as a kid and using fluffy soap bubbles to turn myself into Santa Claus. That may not sound super appealing as a fragrance, but trust me, with the additions of creamy coconut and lavender, it's amazing."—JAYNE LEMIRE, EXECUTIVE ASSISTANT.

It has been revealed that one Cosmo editor says: “Just like a tall glass of water on a hot summer’s day, this perfume feels inexplicably refreshing. Light florals—including hyacinth, lotus blossom, and jasmine—are enshrouded with a unique water accord to make the notes smell dewy and wispy. Then this settles in an ambery musk for a soft yet warm finish.”—MH.

One Cosmo editor says: “A nod to fresh laundry, Rinse Cycle is a fresh, clean fragrance with a bright, citrus opening. After it came out last year, I traveled everywhere with a mini size—I’m talking from Coachella to Paris to Miami to NYC. No matter where I went, this scent worked with every destination. It's also entirely season-less, making it a wonderful choice for hot summer days as well as cool winter nights.”—BETH GILLETTE, BEAUTY EDITOR.

Sources indicate that one Cosmo editor says: “I fell in love with this perfume at first spritz. Created in collaboration with Morgan Riddle, it's reminiscent of fresh tennis whites, cut grass, and breezy air. I adore how it makes my clothes smell, most of all. It’s like I used the best laundry detergent in the world. It smells incredible on skin, too!”—BG.

One Cosmo editor claims: “You know that feeling when you’re lounging in nature and a sliver of light perfectly heats up your skin? I don’t know how, but 5Sens turned that moment into a perfume. This isn’t your average skin scent: It combines fuzzy apricot with a delicate bouquet of peonies and freesia that’s gently warmed with woods and skin musk. It’s the ideal understated perfume that helps me shine a little bit brighter.”—MH.

It has been revealed that one Cosmo editor notes: "There's always been something so supremely comforting about the smell of fresh, warm laundry straight out of the dryer. The only downside is that the wonderful detergent aroma fades promptly. Thankfully, Clean Reserve's Warm Cotton has miraculously managed to bottle it. If you've ever walked around NYC, you'll know there are a million different scents at any given time (many of them, truthfully, not amazing). However, one of my favorite city smells is walking past an apartment building and smelling clean laundry through one of the many vents along the sidewalk. I'll always pause and take in a deep breath; it reminds me of home. Warm Cotton is that moment."—JL.

Industry observers note that mary Honkus is a beauty contributor for Cosmopolitan with over eight years of experience researching, writing, and editing beauty stories. She is an authority in all beauty categories, but has a sweet spot for fragrance with a collection of over 600 scents. While researching for this story, she tested dozens of fresh to bring you an array of calming options.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, in January 1971, the members of the Democratic majority, in what was to be the 92nd Congress, met to determine who would lead them. At the time, there was a rising faction of Democrats demanding congressional reforms, including new leadership. Speaker John McCormack, the ancient Speaker, had finally retired, elevating majority leader Carl Albert into the Speaker’s chair with little or no opposition. However, a serious fight erupted within the caucus over who would replace Albert as the next majority leader. The establishment choice was Representative Hale Boggs of Louisiana, while the reformists lined up behind Representative Morris Udall of Arizona. Boggs managed to squeak out a win, which elevated a Boston congressman named Thomas P. O’Neill to be majority whip, beginning his rise through the leadership.

(The reformist impulse, however, continued to flow through the party, culminating in the reforms that resulted in the nomination of George McGovern for president in 1972.).

It has been revealed that at the moment, it seems that the parallels are all in the Senate. (Representative Hakeem Jeffries’s rise to Speaker seems safe.) Once again, we have solid Democratic majorities in the coming Congress facing off against a villainous Republican president. Once again, there is a reform-minded faction in the incoming Senate majority challenging Senator Chuck Schumer that has begun to coalesce behind Senator Chris Van Hollen of Maryland. The 67-year-old Van Hollen is an unlikely insurgent against Schumer, whose age is the primary strike against him. From the AP:.

It has been revealed that however, Van Hollen has an undeniable streak of independence. He took on the administration boldly in the case of Kilmar Abrego García, the deportee from Maryland whom the administration used in a cruel game of hide-and-seek.

Sources indicate that van Hollen stood against some serious fire while advocating for Abrego García from the governments of both the United States and El Salvador. This included Salvadoran officials planting margarita glasses on the table at which Van Hollen and García sat during a photo opportunity. And, fundamentally, it’s just time for Schumer to step aside. The newly elected senators need fresh leadership, and if Van Hollen is the leader they want, then he should lead them.

  • Back in my full-time sportswriting days—and, in fact, throughout my journalism career—I managed to disguise my fundamental innumeracy.
  • Industry observers note that in this era of analytics and the tyranny of numbers, there is one statistic that remains not only my favorite but that is likely never to fall, and it comes from, of all sports, hockey.
  • The first time I ever saw Gretzky play was during the 1988 Stanley Cup playoffs, when my Boston Bruins faced his Edmonton Oilers.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

No one told me there would be math.

Back in my full-time sportswriting days—and, in fact, throughout my journalism career—I managed to disguise my fundamental innumeracy. Then suddenly, quite recently, numbers became paramount in sports. Baseball led the way, as it does in so many areas where boredom is involved. Now, thanks to gambling’s explosion in popularity, statistics have become one of the primary ways to be a fan.

Industry observers note that in this era of analytics and the tyranny of numbers, there is one statistic that remains not only my favorite but that is likely never to fall, and it comes from, of all sports, hockey. It is this, which boggles the mind: Wayne Gretzky ended his career in 1999 with a total of 2,857 points, which includes goals and assists. Factor out the goals, and he’s still at 1,963, which is 42 more points than the player with the next-highest total, Jaromir Jagr, who is retired.

The first time I ever saw Gretzky play was during the 1988 Stanley Cup playoffs, when my Boston Bruins faced his Edmonton Oilers. These were the dynastic Oilers, loaded with talent: Mark Messier. Jari Kurri. Glenn Anderson. Grant Fuhr between the pipes. All of them Hall of Famers. Amid all this clamorous talent, Gretzky was a phantom. He had this strange and wonderful ability to vanish in the middle of the action and then, suddenly, appear in exactly the right spot at exactly the right time to make exactly the right play.

Gretzky will likely be the leading point scorer in NHL history for the next several decades. In fact, you have to go all the way down to seventh place on the list to find an active player, Sidney Crosby, who is 202 short of Gretzky’s 1,963 assist-only number. Another active player, Alex Ovechkin, is in tenth place, but he’s got one skate out the door already. The next active players on the list are Evgeni Malkin and Patrick Kane, at 23rd and 24th.

Recent findings suggest that like Gretzky himself, this statistic disappears among all the more key numbers until it suddenly pops out to amaze and astound. I like Sidney Crosby a great deal as a player, but I hope he never gets there.

Charles P Pierce is the author of four books, most recently Idiot America, and has been a working journalist since 1976.

#19756. Will Your Relationship Survive “November Theory”?

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (843 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cosmopolitan ↗ Open Full Page

Will Your Relationship Survive “November Theory”?

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (843 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cosmopolitan

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that the holidays are famously known as cuffing season.
  • According to recent reports, “November theory” is the idea that this time of the year brings about a lot of reflection.
  • Warnings like this usually come tied to astrology, but this theory circulates every November.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that the holidays are famously known as cuffing season. But for those already in relationships, this season could mean something entirely different.

According to recent reports, “November theory” is the idea that this time of the year brings about a lot of reflection. For some people, this looks like exes coming back into their lives or someone entirely new coming into the picture. But for couples, this theory may signify endings.

Warnings like this usually come tied to astrology, but this theory circulates every November. So what is it about the 11th month of the year that seems to signal a doomsday for relationships?

Recent findings suggest that “As the end of the year approaches, people begin considering the new year and what they want for themselves,” therapist Jessica Steinman, LMFT, tells Cosmopolitan. “People start discussing New Year’s resolutions and intentions, and they consider who they want to have as a part of that.”.

And sometimes after reflection—and seeing how unhelpful your boyfriend is at Thanksgiving—people decide that it’s time to call it quits.

Industry observers note that so will this November be a death sentence for your relationship? Or will you come out on the other end of “November theory” in a stronger connection?

It has been revealed that okay, there’s no legitimate research behind November causing mass breakups. But there is a reason the trend exists.

“The latest year brings the psychological concept of ‘fresh start effect’ as well as reflection over the past year,” Steinman explains.

Recent findings suggest that while some people are mentally revising their workout routines or making resolutions to read more, they’re also taking stock of what in their life is working and what isn’t. Sometimes, the latter is their relationship. If they notice that they spent a majority of the year feeling uninterested and unhappy in or exhausted by their relationship, they may begin to think about whether the connection is even worth it.

“They want things to feel better, be easier, and move forward in the latest year,” Steinman states.

Before you get swept up in November theory, Steinman suggests taking a beat to think about the relationship as a whole.

“They need to consider if the struggles and issues in the relationship have been an ongoing concern or if this is something that could be intensified due to the stress and bigger feelings around the holidays,” she says.

In a recent development, sometimes dealing with the stresses of buying gifts, being around your problematic uncle, and having to spend time in your childhood home can trigger a lot of negative emotions. The holidays aren’t always joy and cheer for everyone. And these stressors may be lending themselves to feelings of annoyance.

“They need to focus on the unhealthy patterns of what is going on in the relationship, not specific feelings that might be happening in those end-of-year moments.”.

And while it’s fun to take part in internet trends, you should have a conversation with your partner before you make a video of yourself crying on TikTok post-breakup saying, “November theory is 100 percent real.”.

Sources indicate that if something is genuinely bothering you about your relationship, communicate that to your partner. You might learn that your feelings of discontent have a pretty easy solution. “Change can’t happen between partners if it isn’t communicated and looked at together,” Steinman says.

Industry observers note that november theory doesn’t necessarily mean you need to call it quits with your partner. It can actually be a really great opportunity to do some admin on your relationship.

“Having healthy, open, and vulnerable conversations with a partner before the newly introduced year is a great way to start the new year together,” Steinman indicates.

She explains that rather than making an impulsive and permanent decision to end the relationship, couples can think of the end of the year as an assessment period and think about how they can make meaningful changes in the new year instead of giving ultimatums and ending it.

Recent findings suggest that but this is a conversation that’s going to require some thought. Steinman warns against using broad statements like “I’m unhappy” or “I don’t wan’t to do this anymore.” They’re just not productive.

“A statement like ‘I feel like we’ve been disconnected’ or ‘I feel like we’re not on the same page and I’d like to get on the same page’ could work a lot better,” she says. “Having a reflection conversation together is a good way to start.”.

Any trend that encourages you to reflect on your life and relationship is a trend I can get behind. But the second you start making decisions about your relationship because the internet told you to, you’re going about it all wrong—and may even lose a good thing while you’re at it.

Slow down, and take the time to think about what you want—and don’t feel like you’re confined to making your decision within the month. There’s plenty of time to think about your relationship in December, too.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that the Governors Awards are back. The annual gala hosted by the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences (who also hosts the Oscars) to honor lifetime achievement and extraordinary contributions to film has returned for its 17th edition—and the red carpet is brimming with star power.

Sources indicate that while this gala itself is not aired live, like the main Oscars ceremony (which takes place in March every year), the awards given are considered genuine Oscars. Until 2009, the awards now given at the Governors Awards were presented live during the main Oscars telecast, but the Academy separated them into their own gala—both to shorten the main television broadcast and to give honorees more time to celebrate their wins and present their speeches.

Last year, Tom Cruise, Debbie Allen, and Wynn Thomas received Honorary Oscars, while Dolly Parton was given the Jean Hersholt Humanitarian Award. On the red carpet, we saw everyone, from Jennifer Lawrence to Anya Taylor-Joy, Cynthia Erivo, and Dakota Johnson.

It has been revealed that meanwhile, tonight’s honorees include Glenn Close, Ridley Scott, and Floyd Norman—who are all receiving Honorary Oscars—alongside producers Christine Vachon and Pamela Koffler, who will receive the Irving G. Thalberg Memorial Award.

But there are plenty of other guests in attendance this evening at the Ray Dolby Ballroom at Ovation Hollywood in Los Angeles—from Penélope Cruz in Chanel to Zendaya in Gilles Deacon, Charlize Theron in Tom Ford, Tessa Thompson in Schiaparelli, and Emma Stone in Louis Vuitton.

Ahead, see all the celebrity looks from the 2026 Governors Awards red carpet.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The carpet at our annual GQ Men of the Year party may be red, but we’re seeing—dare we say it—Brat green.

Last night, as the stars of our latest MOTY problem gathered at the iconic Chateau Marmont, we noticed a verdant trend emerge on the carpet. Who better to kick things off than two of the most boisterous creatives from our 2026 Breakout Stars crew? First up was actor-comedian Stavros Halkias, who sported a screaming lime green suit by Alan David, a matching Cego silk shirt, and olive-hued Bottega Veneta loafers. Not far behind was Club Kid director-star Jordan Firstman, who also greened out in a full runway look from Anthony Vaccarello’s final menswear collection for Saint Laurent: a boxy, greenish khaki suit with bejeweled buttons, layered over a liquid-silk chartreuse shirt. Both ensembles sure were bright, but ask any color theorist and they’ll probably tell you that wearing green on a red carpet is a surefire way to stand out—they’re opposite of each other on the color wheel for a reason!

Jordan Firstman in Saint Laurent.

The chartreuse looks just kept on coming: the one and only Ice Spice donned a flowing green DSquared2 dress, with matching green eyeshadow (and a curiously hirsute handbag) to boot.

Elsewhere on the carpet, The Bear’s Ayo Edebiri—already a bonafide menswear star—opted for a different but equally striking shade of green. Her sleek striped power suit by London-based designer Connor Ives popped thanks to a kelly green shirt and a contrasting crimson tie. (Edebiri wasn’t the only woman who rocked tailoring on the MOTY carpet this year: model Cara Delevingne, who stars in Firstman’s Club Kid, wore a slouchy-chic black suit by Saint Laurent, while Luciana Damon, wife of cover star Matt, layered a tuxedo-style bolero jacket over her gown.).

Sources indicate that if the MOTY red carpet can provide any insights into the year of fashion ahead, we’ll surely be seeing even more green in the months to come. We’re manifesting abundance, in more ways than one.

Latest Update: This Three-Day Wedding Brought Persian Traditions, Dramatic Design, and an Ibiza-Style Rave to Oaxaca

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 22 min read (4467 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vogue

⏱️ ~22 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, brian Downs and Sarvenaz Shahbazi had a classic college library meet-cute.
  • The couple got engaged two-and-a-half years later, over July 4th weekend on a trip to Puglia.
  • Industry observers note that sarvi’s family, who were in on the initiative, told everyone to meet for sunset drinks at the beach club of the masseria where they were staying.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, brian Downs and Sarvenaz Shahbazi had a classic college library meet-cute. One day, while they were both at Columbia Business School, Brian was tutoring their mutual friend—and future wedding officiant—Alex in a study room. Sarvenaz, who goes by Sarvi, walked by and jumped right in, taking the lead in guiding everyone through accounting problems. “I remember immediately thinking how pretty she was, but also how smart and confident she was,” indicates Brian. The two became friends, and by the time they were back from winter break, Brian asked Sarvi out for drinks at The Commerce Inn on January 7, 2022. Says Sarvi, “I had mentioned to him in passing that I had been wanting to go a month or two earlier since it had just opened, so I was very impressed with his thoughtfulness and planning!” The two were inseparable from that point on.

The couple got engaged two-and-a-half years later, over July 4th weekend on a trip to Puglia. Sarvi’s parents had planned a week-long vacation in the region, and Sarvi and her brother decided to join last minute with their partners. Brian, who was already on an engagement ring search, expedited the process to have it ready for the trip. “At the time, I genuinely did not think an engagement was on the table for at least a few more months,” notes Sarvi. “We had only recently started talking about it, and Brian had very strategically staged our first-ever ring shopping trip the week before we left, which I then learned was just a decoy.”.

Industry observers note that sarvi’s family, who were in on the initiative, told everyone to meet for sunset drinks at the beach club of the masseria where they were staying. When the couple arrived, one of Sarvi’s favorite songs was playing, and a single table was set with flowers and Champagne with views of the water. “I looked at the setup and immediately said to Brian, ‘Oh my God, I think someone is going to get engaged here. We’re going to see it,’” Sarvi states. When they walked towards the deck, Brian pulled out the ring and got down on one knee. “She was in utter shock,” recalls Brian. “I had thought a lot about what I was going to say, but the only thing I actually remember saying is ‘eshgham,’ which means ‘my love’ in Farsi.”.

When choosing a destination to tie the knot, Brian and Sarvi found themselves constantly drifting back to Mexico, ultimately deciding to exchange vows in Oaxaca City on November 15, 2025. The couple went on their first trip together to the country and had each visited countless times before and after they started dating.

According to recent reports, the bride took charge to bring their dream wedding to life. “I work in hospitality as the director of strategy and development at Catch Hospitality Group, so what I truly find most fulfilling in life is creating experiences for others centered around exceptional food and drink and a carefully curated ambiance,” she indicates. Alongside planners Gutierrez F Studio, Sarvi helped orchestrate three days of events that blended this ethos with traditions from her Persian culture. The weekend would kick off with a rehearsal dinner full of delicious food and speeches at Criollo, followed by a Persian wedding ceremony and party at the historic Proyecto Murguía, and finally, the massive day at Loma Noble. “We had so much fun creating a completely different world, each with a distinct personality, for every part of the wedding day—leading our guests on a journey from a ceremony in a bucolic agave field, to an energetic and dramatic dinnerscape, all the way to an after-party rave in a cactus garden,” says the bride.

Sources indicate that while Sarvi had clear ideas of how to bring together all the events, it took some work to come up with her wedding wardrobe. “I wasn’t a bride with a pre-constructed Pinterest board, so when I first started thinking about what I would wear, I was completely overwhelmed by the sheer number of options,” she indicates. “I never wanted to wear anything that felt stiff, stuffy, or overly traditional.” This drive to find something unique led her to a pale butter-yellow dress with a sheer cape from Harithand for her rehearsal dinner, which she paired with diamond and ruby flower earrings from her aunt. “I felt immediately comfortable in it—it was soft, ethereal and subtly sexy—and felt perfect for our dinner under the stars at Criollo,” she says.

Her ceremony dress search ultimately led her to two iconic bridal designers: Danielle Frankel and Vera Wang. When Sarvi first saw Wang’s Ariel dress, it reminded her of Van Gogh’s Starry Night. “It ultimately felt perfect for our Persian ceremony,” she states. “There is so much artistry, symbolism, and craftsmanship that goes into an ‘aghd’ and the ‘sofreh’—the traditional ceremonial table—with countless individual symbolic items and details coming together to create something incredibly beautiful. There was a similar sense of artistry and romance in the Vera Wang gown that felt especially fitting for that night.” She paired the look with pink sapphire and diamond flower drop earrings from her maternal grandmother, who recently passed.

For the western wedding day, Sarvi wore a strapless gown by Frankel. While she wasn’t planning to try it on before she entered the showroom, the style called to her. “I loved the contrasting shades of white, the different textures, and the subtle lace throughout the skirt, which gave the dress so much dimension and movement,” she says. Once again, the bride wore a jewelry piece from her grandmother: a pearl choker with a gold flower and a tiny ruby. “They were playful, distinctive, and deeply personal, with those unexpected touches of color that I always love,” she says.

After dinner, the bride changed into a custom look she made with Brooklyn-based designer Delfina Balda. The two-piece look featured a mix of textures and fabrics with varying degrees of sheerness. “It felt like the perfect party look—artful and completely unique, but something I could actually dance in,” she claims. For the after-party, which was modeled after DC10 in Ibiza with a completely red lighting scheme, Sarvi decided to change out of bridal white and donned a red dress by The Attico. “It has this intricate soutache detailing and a fringe skirt that gives the dress incredible texture and movement, especially on the dance floor,” she says.

Industry observers note that the groom wore a mix of vintage and bespoke looks throughout the wedding weekend. For Friday night, Brian donned a relaxed suit found at Ebreo Vintage in Williamsburg that fit him perfectly. “Even the owner basically said, ‘Honestly, you should just buy that.’ I got pretty lucky,” he claims. His next two looks were made alongside Tyler Sequeira at P. Johnson. The groom wanted to wear a double-breasted chocolate brown suit for the Persian ceremony to complement the natural tones throughout the celebration. “On my second visit, when I was picking fabrics and locking everything in, Sarvi’s uncle Mohammad, or Momo, insisted on joining me,” says Brian. “It’s a tradition in their family to buy a new suit for the groom joining the family, so he ended up helping me design the suit for the aghd. I loved that the suit became something more meaningful than just something I had picked out for myself.” For the black-tie wedding day, Brian wore a bespoke tuxedo made in midnight blue.

According to recent reports, the wedding weekend began at Criollo, for an open-air dinner filled with mezcalitas, tacos, and chickens roaming freely through the space. “It immediately gave everyone a sense of the place we had fallen in love with,” says Sarvi. The night full of speeches ended with a night of dancing at a local vinyl bar. “It was one of the first moments where I looked around and really processed that all of these people we loved had traveled to Oaxaca to be there for us,” says Brian.

On the Persian wedding day, the couple paraded with their guests through the streets to their venue, where the space was filled with florals, Persian food, music, and a sofreh table ready for the ceremony. The bride’s uncle officiated the aghd and her mother and other family members participated throughout. “By the time the ceremony ended, the night very quickly became a full-on Persian dance party,” indicates Sarvi. “We had hoped Friday would have just as much energy and dancing as Saturday, but even we underestimated it.” Adds Brian, “Seeing my parents and friends dancing to Persian music alongside Sarvi’s family is one of the funniest and most joyous memories I’ll have from the weekend.”.

The ceremony the next day was held at sunset among the agave fields of Loma Noble, an agronomic project outside the city of Oaxaca. “We wanted the ceremony to feel as though it belonged within the landscape rather than creating something that completely competed with it,” indicates the bride. Sarvi walked down the aisle to a string rendition of “Creep” by Radiohead. “Certainly not the most traditional wedding choice, but one of my favorite songs of all time and, to me, one of the most beautiful songs ever written,” she says. The couple’s business school friend Alex officiated, weaving in sentimental passages from Brian’s late grandfather Jack, and the groom’s mother shared a reading. The couple wrote their own vows, including an entire section Brian prepared in Farsi. “I learned afterward that my younger cousin had secretly been tutoring him so he could learn and practice that portion,” says Sarvi. “It was one of the most deeply sentimental gestures I could have imagined.”.

The couple share they were both emotional, yet calm and present for the ceremony. The two recessed to “California Dreamin’,” which they sang with joy down the aisle. “It was this perfect release of all the emotion we had been feeling, and immediately shifted the energy from the ceremony into pure excitement for the night ahead,” indicates the bride. The two spent a moment alone together in the bridal suite before joining guests at cocktail hour along a tree-lined pathway.

In a recent development, when guests moved into the reception tent, they found the space decorated with a nod to an eclipse, complete with a glowing orb above a circular central stage and serpentine tables along the room. Dinner was punctuated with speeches, assigned “table captains” to keep the energy alive, and dances with their parents. The newlyweds shared their own first dance at the end of dinner to “Sunny” by Bobby Hebb. “As soon as it ended, Brian and I grabbed the microphones and essentially declared, ‘Now, it’s time to party.’ At that exact moment, trays of carajillos came out for everyone, giving the room one more jolt of energy before the curtains separating the dinner space from the dance floor opened,” states the bride. Their 300 guests moved to the disco-ball-filled space complete with a martini bar and music by DJ César.

Recent findings suggest that “At one point, Brian and I ended up dancing on top of the bar and apparently were dancing hard enough that the staff became concerned it might come crashing down—so the bartenders were literally holding it up beneath us while we were dancing,” indicates Sarvi. “That probably sums up the energy of the night better than anything else.” The party didn’t stop as guests next moved through a glowing red tunnel. “Once you emerged into the cactus garden, everything was washed in red light, with an enormous triangular LED structure framing the dance floor,” says the bride. “It felt almost otherworldly and created exactly the kind of late-night atmosphere we wanted.” The couple danced until 6 a.m.

In a recent development, looking back, the couple describe it as the most magical weekend of their lives. “I constantly find myself wondering what I did to end up married to someone so cool and so loved by her friends and family,” states Brian. “She draws people into her orbit, and getting to stand next to her while all of those people demonstrated up to celebrate us is something I’ll never forget.”.

We’re mere weeks away from Dancing With the Stars season 35 wrapping up, and you know what that means: it’s almost time to start fan casting Dancing With the Stars season 36, and that definitely includes guest judges.

The show always invites a roster of guests to join the judges’ panel, from former Dancing With the Stars pros to random celebrity fans—and Jan Ravnik has a suggestion.

Speaking to Entertainment Weekly, Jan mused, “Oh, who would be my dream? You know what would be cool, if there would be the Kelce brothers here, one of them.”.

He added, “They would be incredible. They would know nothing about dance, but somehow judge great.”.

Reminder: Jan was a backup dancer for Taylor Swift during the Eras Tour, which means he presumably knows the Kelce brothers. So, if he states they’d be good judges, we have faith. And honestly, it could happen. Dancing With the Stars has managed to book some pretty major celebrities, including Cynthia Erivo, who revealed up for Disney Night a few weeks ago. On top of that, the show introduced a Super Bowl night this season, and if they do so again, having Jason or Travis guest judge would be an obvious choice!

Meanwhile, according to The Sun back in 2024, Jason Kelce is a fan of the show and even considered joining. “He looks forward to being on TV when the NFL season starts. But he also wants to do multiple things and loves TV indicates,” their source stated. “He been asked to appear on plenty of shows in the last few months, and he is really interested in being on some of them. Jason is sure to have fun on Dancing with The Stars and hopes it will work out in the coming season.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that “Ordinary People” might be the title of a Grammy-winning song by John Legend.
  • The benefit gala recently welcomed Legend alongside Mickalene Thomas, Lena Waithe, Mike Jackson, Cyndi Lauper, and Donna Murphy to Current—a private event space within Pier 59 at Chelsea Piers.
  • Sources indicate that television personality Bevy Smith, who was on hosting duty for the evening, fielded well wishes from the crowd, having just celebrated her 60th birthday.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that “Ordinary People” might be the title of a Grammy-winning song by John Legend. Yet Legend’s persona and career trajectory have proven to be anything but ordinary—as exemplified by his attendance and performance at The National Black Theatre’s inaugural Fall Fête.

The benefit gala recently welcomed Legend alongside Mickalene Thomas, Lena Waithe, Mike Jackson, Cyndi Lauper, and Donna Murphy to Current—a private event space within Pier 59 at Chelsea Piers. Inside the venue, a crowd gathered for a cocktail reception as the Kotchegna Dance Tech giant helped kick off the evening with their powerful rhythmic processional while Reverend Rhonda Akanaké McLean-Nur poured libations to set the tone.

Sources indicate that television personality Bevy Smith, who was on hosting duty for the evening, fielded well wishes from the crowd, having just celebrated her 60th birthday. “The room is so full—full of hope, love, laughter, and impact. And tonight is a firm reminder that Black enterprise and artistry stem from community,” celebrity hairstylist Vernon Francois told Vogue as they took their seat. Sharing a similar sentiment was Pose star and NBT alum, Ryan Jamal Swain: “Honestly, this is a full-circle moment for me. Walking through the door tonight and seeing a large photo of myself on the wall takes me back to the beginning of my career—I’d just graduated from Howard and moved to Newly introduced York, and Sade [Lythcott] welcomed me with open arms.”.

In the dining room, linen-draped banquet tables topped with roses, mini orchids, and calla lily arrangements provided a colorful setting for warm plates of grilled artichoke, artisan steakhouse beef, steamed halibut, and Caesar salad. “Tonight is a call to action,” Smith mentioned as she headed toward the podium. “This gala is further proof that Black people must continue to show up and show out. At the election booths, at special events, and all across the globe, because the world needs your talent and your energy.”.

In a recent development, as the night progressed, event co-chairs Andi Bernstein and Sonja Warfield joined Smith onstage and spoke of the importance of NBT’s legacy. Esteemed industry creatives including Michael F. Lythcott (NBT board chair), Thelma Golden, Charles Randolph Wright, Debra Martin Chase, and Nina Shaw presented special awards to gala honorees Margaret Anadu, Sanford Biggers, Nona Hendryx, and Get Lifted Film Co.’s Mike Jackson, as well as Legend.

Accepting the Excellence in Creative Producing Award with his business partner Jackson, Legend stated: “It’s a blessing to be a Black storyteller, and I’m so grateful that the National Black Theater exists for times such as these.” Shortly after his acceptance speech, Legend serenaded the crowd with a medley of hits, including the soul-stirring “Ordinary People,” along with a new song from his upcoming NBT-backed musical Imitation of Life—a reimagining of the 1959 film.

Additional stage presentations saw Liza Jessie Peterson perform a spoken word poem, while jazz singer Somi Kakoma provided a moving vocal selection. Describing the program, actress Murphy stated it was “an honor to witness and experience, because the arts can transform every single human being, and NBT does it so well.”.

Recent findings suggest that the fundraising total of almost $1 million was powered by Subyn Novelle’s boisterous paddle-raising expertise. Afterwards, a disco-fueled dessert reception closed out the evening with porcelain trays of raspberry macarons, brownies, and coconut cream bites doing the rounds. DJ Stormin’ Norman spun upbeat R&B tunes from Stevie Wonder and Chaka Khan to Earth, Wind & Fire as guests flooded the dance floor to celebrate.

Holding court next to the espresso café station was NBT’s chief executive officer Sade Lythcott, who reflected on the night’s success: “When Black culture takes center stage, it’s a reminder that anything is possible for all people. And tonight’s fundraising—which partly benefits The Theatre of the Future—is a long-awaited dedication to the extraordinary vision and original building intends of my mother,” she told Vogue.

NBT’s executive artistic director Jonathan McCrory echoed the sentiment. “Tonight, we celebrate 58 years of Black artistic excellence and deep-rooted Harlem legacy founded by Dr. Barbara Ann Teer in 1968. And as we near completion of our fresh world-class cultural arts complex, we’re reminded of how far we’ve come—but we’re also inspired by how much further we can abundantly support our community.”.
